News.title: Fallon Sherrock defeats Luke Littler to land £501,000 prize in one-leg event
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Fallon Sherrock won the second biggest prize in darts history as she claimed £501,000 by beating Luke Littler in a one-off leg.

The 32-year-old was crowned the champion of Netflix show ‘Beat Luke Littler’ when she took out 501 in 15 darts.

She was the 15th competitor out of 20 to take on the double world champion after he had won 14 straight legs.

While Littler made light work of some of the amateurs, which included an Australian jockey, a bin man and a Nando’s manager, he came up short against a top quality opponent.

Sherrock threw a 180 and checked out with him stranded on 124.

Victory, and over half a million pounds, throws Sherrock back into the limelight again, seven years after she made history by becoming the first woman to win at the World Championship on her way to the third round.

Her place in the show attracted some criticism given her stature in the game, but she was delighted to prove her worth.

“I’m over the moon, I can’t believe I have just won a leg of darts and won half a million,” she told the Press Association.

open image in gallery Littler took on an Australian jockey, a bin man and a Nando’s manager (Peter Byrne/PA) ( PA Wire )

“This is definitely one of those top moments because it’s like an opportunity to kind of show off the women’s stars, and I feel like I’ve kind of taken the opportunity again.

“I’ve shown in the past women what can do as well and you know it’s definitely going to be put up there because it’s definitely the biggest prize money that I’ve won.

“I’ve just beaten the best in the world, and I can’t say that very often.

“When I hit the 180, I was like, ‘right, just relax and just go for the shot out because this is probably the only shot that you’re going to get’.

“And I took it.”

Littler was not at his best in a truncated format which saw him one leg every 10 minutes.

Irish student Pearse Mackie, who was the eighth contestant to face Littler, was the first to have a dart for victory, but he missed bullseye to claim what would have been a memorable win.

Mark Pooke, who played Phil Taylor in a professional match almost 20 years ago, also had darts to win in the ninth leg, but could not take out 138.

Despite, having his pride dented by losing, the 19-year-old is keen to go again.

open image in gallery Luke Littler beat 14 contestants in the one-leg event in Manchester (Peter Byrne/PA) ( PA Wire )

“Yeah, (she was) brilliant. That’s what one person had to do. Win the bull and go out in 15,” Littler said on stage.

“That’s exactly what Fallon did. I hit a 140 to leave 142.

“When she missed the first going tops, I was like, ‘give me a chance’. She didn’t and world class.

“I’ve enjoyed every bit of it. The advert, the photo shoots, everything. It’s been good and maybe Netflix we can do it again next year.”

News.title: Canada and EU announce new alliance in response to hostility from Trump
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The European Union and Canada announced a new alliance of “ever-closer association” designed to bring together like-minded countries to address common challenges.

Canadian prime minister Mark Carney said on Friday he and his European counterparts would define the scale and scope of a "new form" of European Union membership over the coming months, and that Canada would become its first "associate member."

They will define by a 2027 summit what the association would entail exactly, Carney said.

In a post on X, Carney said that what he called an “Alliance for the Future” would not only be open to Canada and the EU, but to “other countries that share our views to address common challenges and strengthen our collective power.”

open image in gallery European Council president Antonio Costa, Canada's prime minister Mark Carney and European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen attend a Signature Ceremony at the Canada-EU Summit in Montreal ( Reuters )

Donald ‌Trump last ‌month threatened trade sanctions in ⁠response to von der Leyen's proposal to create ⁠a new status for the EU-Canada relationship.

The US president has adopted a more transactional approach to foreign ​policy and has repeatedly attacked multilateral institutions.

Carney called Canada “the most European of non-European countries” early in Trump’s trade war. This week, it was reported that discussions regarding trade between the US and Canada had seen only modest advancement.

On Thursday, European Commission president Ursula ⁠von der Leyen said the EU ​and ⁠Canada continue to ‌explore the North American nation becoming the union's first "associate member," a term so divisive among member ‌countries that it does ‌not appear in the final statement.

Carney said the alliance between EU and Canada, announced at a summit in Montreal on Friday, would focus on resilience in areas including AI, energy and critical minerals.

"We are working towards the deepest possible partnership, short of accession," he said, adding that this would result in "Canada ‌becoming the European Union’s first Associate Member."

open image in gallery Mark Carney was in the UK last month, where he and Andy Burnham - both Evertonians - watched their side together ( Getty )

The associate member term, which Germany and several other EU countries oppose, has no legal meaning.

In a joint statement released to mark the end ⁠of the summit, Canadian and EU leaders cited an “unwavering commitment to effective multilateralism, democracy and to the rules-based international order."

The statement said Canada and the 27-nation EU would work to resolve the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East and deepen security ties elsewhere, including in the Arctic.

It added talks had been ‌concluded on a ​digital trade agreement that would ‌complement the existing trade agreement between ​Canada and the EU.

Carney also said he had accepted the European Council president's invitation to attend meetings in Europe next June, where he said talks on the deeper relationship would be concluded.

"We are building the industries and infrastructure that underwrite our collective security," Carney said.

"This is only the beginning."

News.title: G20 photocall cancelled after Miliband refuses to be pictured with Russian foreign minister
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The group photocall at Friday’s G20 meeting was cancelled after foreign secretary Ed Miliband and his European counterparts refused to be photographed with Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio was forced to pull the plug on the photograph at the start of the meeting of the world’s largest economies in Atlanta, Georgia, after several European officials said they intended to boycott or walk out of the photograph that often kicks off the gatherings.

Rubio decided to scrap the picture because he thought the controversy would be a distraction, according to two US officials, who spoke to the Associated Press.

Some G20 countries had already expressed concern that the US invited Russia during its heightened attacks on Ukraine, especially after Donald Trump pushed ties with Kyiv to new lows by waiving fresh sanctions on Moscow and temporarily limiting logistical and intelligence assistance.

In his intervention at Friday’s meeting, Mr Miliband said: “Let me say this directly to the Russian foreign minister – we all know who the aggressor in this war is.

“Let’s talk about what happened at Dnipro railway yesterday. Only yesterday your drones attacked and killed 15 people.

“And there are countless examples like this of you killing innocent civilians throughout this war.

“We all know you are the aggressor. We all know you started this war four and a half years ago with the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

open image in gallery The G20 foreign ministers' meeting took place in Atlanta, Georgia ( Reuters )

“And Putin thought then he would win this war easily. But you are not winning this war.

“Thanks to the courage of the Ukrainian people and the solidarity of countries round this table, you are not winning.

“If you had the courage to tell the truth and to do what is right you would tell Putin that he is not winning this war and will not win.”

A UK Government source told the Press Association: “We were not going to take part in any official picture with the Russian foreign minister.”

They added: “The Foreign Secretary is here in Atlanta focused on the global challenges that are driving up costs for people at home.

“The UK has a longstanding policy not to have direct, bilateral engagement with Russian ministers since the invasion of Ukraine and we are not about to change that.”

Polish deputy prime minister Radosław Sikorski told reporters in Atlanta that “I am not the only one who does not want to be photographed with Lavrov.”

German foreign minister Johann Wadephul said “there is no normality with Russia” as he explained there would be no photograph taken.

But he added “we must exchange the controversies at the table here,” the German news agency dpa reported.

He also said that “we also must not send falsely optimistic signals.”

open image in gallery Atlanta police officers stand guard along a street as a sign directs attendees to the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta ( AFP/Getty )

Lavrov has traveled only infrequently to NATO member states since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and resulting severe sanctions were imposed on Moscow.

Rubio still opened the talks with an appeal for unity on the issues that threaten international security and trade.

“We are in a critical moment,” he told his colleagues. “We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises.”

He pointed to disruptions to global energy and food supplies, trade and freedom of navigation and said many are posing “severe threats to essential foundations of the global economic order.”

Yet there was no sign that the G20 diplomats could come to consensus on many of the most contentious issues they face.

Among them are the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, U.S. tariffs and Chinese machinations in the South China Sea. All have contributed to spikes in the global cost of fuel as well as uncertainty about trade.

Diplomats who attended the opening session described it as cordial but said Russia’s position on Ukraine is unyielding — as is its opposition to Poland's membership in the G20 - the Associated Press reported.

News.title: Labour delivers planning officers pledge as 1.5m homes target deadline nears
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Labour Party has met its manifesto promise to bring in 300 new planning officers amid a looming deadline to build 1.5million new homes.

The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government announced that around 420 new planning officers have been hired through government supported schemes.

Despite the push, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner admitted geopolitical turbulence means Labour will be unlikely to deliver on their 1.5million news homes promise by the proposed deadline of 2029.

The ministry said on Friday the new recruits, which exceed the 300 new officers pledge, will help families and businesses obtain quicker decisions.

The extra officers could help to provide quicker answers for homeowners looking to extend or convert their loft, and small businesses improving their premises, the Government said.

open image in gallery Angela Rayner said there was a ‘slim chance’ the government would meet its target (PA) ( PA Wire )

Officials hope a new AI system, PlanAssist, could also cut admin for staff by bringing together applications, policies and site constraints in one place for planners to review.

Ms Rayner said: “Families wanting more space and businesses looking to grow shouldn’t be left waiting unnecessarily for straightforward planning decisions.

“We’re giving councils the people, tools and reforms they need to get applications moving faster, while freeing up planners and councillors to focus on the developments that will deliver the homes and infrastructure communities need.

“We’ve already beaten our manifesto commitment to recruit 300 planners, and we’re going further with 1,400 new recruits across the planning system by the end of this Parliament.”

open image in gallery AI minister Kanishka Narayan (James Manning/PA) ( PA Wire )

Ms Rayner told the BBC last month that there was a “slim chance” the Government would meet its target of building 1.5 million homes in England by the next election, “but I’m definitely not giving it up”.

Rayner stressed that the government was “making a difference” regardless, thanks to investing billions in social and affordable homes.

She said it was important to keep the goal - which Rayner asserts had always been a “stretch target” - in place, but that she was “being honest with the public” that it would be difficult to achieve.

AI minister Kanishka Narayan said: “This is what putting AI to work for the public looks like in practice.

“By slashing the time spent on routine planning tasks by more than half, we’re helping families get quicker answers while freeing up skilled planners to focus on the major developments that will get Britain building.”

News.title: Fallon Sherrock beats Luke Littler to win £501,000 in Netflix show
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Fallon Sherrock defeated Luke Littler to win £501,000 and triumph in the first-ever ‘Beat Luke Littler’ show.

The ‘Queen Of The Palace’, who made headlines by becoming the first woman to win a match at the PDC World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace back in 2019, produced a 14-dart leg to beat the world champion in the Netflix event.

Littler had beaten 14 ‘amateur’ players in a row in the single-leg format, on a night when any of the contestants could have won the prize of half a million pounds if they reached a score of 501 and produced a double finish before Littler.

The inclusion of Sherrock as one of the 24 challengers had created some controversy when the line-up was announced by Netflix earlier this month; other players included a bin man, a restaurant manager at Nando’s, a driving instructor, and an electrical engineer.

While Sherrock is used to performing on the big stage, with the 32-year-old qualified hairdresser becoming a fan favourite at Alexandra Palace and reaching the third round in 2020, the £501,000 prize is the biggest of her career.

The £501,000 prize is the second-highest single payout in darts, behind the £1m prize for the World Championship winner. Sherrock’s previous biggest payday was the £25,000 she won for reaching the third round at Alexandra Palace in 2020.

After winning the ‘bull-up’ to earn the first throw in the leg, Sherrock took control and raised the roof in Manchester by hitting five treble 20s in a row and leaving 43 to finish. She had two attempts at double top and found the target at the second opportunity.

“It’s insane, I can’t put it into words,” said Sherrock, who was also playing in front of her son, Rory, for the first time. “Especially having Rory here, it’s the first time he’s been to anything and he’s seen me win!

“I’m really lost for words but it’s a great moment. I’ll remember this forever. I’m like, if you give me an opportunity I’m going to take it every time. I don’t know what it is but I’m really proud of myself right now.”

Sherrock was able to take part as she does not hold a PDC Tour card, and took her chance after Littler had dismissed a series of low-ranked players and before teeanger Mitchell Lawrie, the top seed and WDF No 1, had made it to the oche.

open image in gallery Luke Littler had survived a match dart earlier in the show ( (Photo by Nathan Stirk/StillMoving.Net for Netflix) )

open image in gallery Fallon Sherrock with the 'I Beat Luke Littler' trophy ( (Photo by Nathan Stirk/StillMoving.Net for Netflix) )

Littler, the two-time world champion and world No 1, was far below his best in Manchester, hitting well below his usual average and managing just two 180s across the night. He had also faced a match dart during his leg against Ireland’s Pearse Mackle, who missed bullseye for £501,000.

Littler, 19, praised Sherrock’s performance and said: “Brilliant. That’s what one person had to do, win the bull and go out with 15 and that’s exactly what Fallon did. When she missed the first double top I thought, ‘give me a chance’. But she didn’t. World class.

“I’ve enjoyed every minute of it. It’s been good. Maybe we can do it again next year.”

open image in gallery Littler was far from his best as he took on a series of amateurs and lower-ranked players ( (Photo by Tom Dymond/StillMoving.Net for Netflix) )

open image in gallery Sherrock celebrated with her son, Rory, who was watching her on stage for the first time ( (Photo by Nathan Stirk/StillMoving.Net for Netflix) )

The ‘Beat Luke Littler’ show was hosted by Gary Lineker and Richard Osman, who had predicted that one of the challengers would beat Littler.

“I would be shocked beyond words if we don’t give away £501,000,” Osman had said. “It’s really exciting. You’re going to see somebody throwing one dart for half a million pounds. That’s the only thing that makes me sort of hesitate in my judgement.

“I know those players good enough that one of them, out of 20, will beat him. He’ll have an off leg, they’ll have a good leg. But they are going to have to, in front of a big live audience, throw a single dart at a single double for £501,000. And is that humanly possible would be my question. It’s incredibly exciting.”

News.title: Are Liverpool back? Andoni Iraola’s evolving project now faces the ultimate test
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

When Andoni Iraola and Mikel Arteta talked on 20 May, each could praise his boyhood friend for a historic achievement. While Arteta had just won Arsenal’s first Premier League title for 22 years, the kingmaker was Iraola, whose Bournemouth team had held Manchester City, leaving the Gunners four points clear with a game to go. “We spoke the next day just to congratulate each other because it was massive for us as we got Europe,” Iraola said.

If Iraola was an unwitting ally to Arteta then, now he assumes the role of obstacle to his fellow Basque’s ambitions. It is not merely because he has three victories in their last four meetings. “It doesn’t mean a lot,” said Iraola; now he has different players and a different team. Then he faced Arsenal as underdogs, now perhaps as equals.

But there is a school of thought that, if Arsenal do not retain their title, Liverpool are the likeliest champions. That mantle would rest with Manchester City, but the threat of a sizeable points deduction hangs over them. Liverpool have already lost to City at Anfield; beat Arsenal, as they did last year, and the gap between is reduced to three points. Lose and a nine-point deficit could look too big to overhaul.

open image in gallery Alexander Isak is enjoying his best run at Liverpool with six goals in six in the Premier League ( Getty )

It isn’t Iraola’s way to talk about the title. “It is too early to start looking at the standings,” he said, arguing they take on a greater meaning when everyone has played everyone else once.

It may be more instructive how few others contemplated the prospect of Liverpool winning the league, given that they were defending champions last year. That says something about how unsuccessful their defence of their crown was. They trailed in 25 points behind Arsenal. They then appointed a manager, in Iraola, with a track record of improving teams and players, but not of winning trophies. They stumbled out of the blocks this season.

“In the first bunch of games, I think the two draws at the beginning condition everything else,” said Iraola. After being held by Newcastle and Nottingham Forest, and trailing to each, there were few predictions of imminent glory. Even now, when Liverpool have gathered momentum on a run of five straight wins, Iraola has noted only two have come in the Premier League. He is aware his side are more prolific in Europe. “In the [English] league, we have been less dangerous offensively,” he said.

But there are encouraging elements. Without quite reaching the levels he did at Newcastle, Alexander Isak has nevertheless scored six goals in his last six top-flight games. Iraola’s band of four wingers have shown a productivity, with eight goals and nine assists between them in all competitions. Despite all preferring the left, each has delivered when on the right; in a match-up with Arsenal, without Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman, possibly without Christos Tzolis or Noni Madueke, Iraola could seem to have the better options on the flanks.

open image in gallery Iraola and Arteta are friends from the Basque country but could be the coaches contesting a title race this season ( Getty )

While his brand of football can seem more adventurous than Arteta’s, perhaps Iraola has borrowed from his old friend’s playbook. While Arsenal’s set-piece specialists had to wait until last Saturday’s win over Everton for their first goal from dead-ball situations this season, Liverpool, who kept conceding from corners in the first half of last season, have been frugal this year. “I think we have, touch wood, dealt very well with defending set-pieces so far this season,” said Iraola, who credits his assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper for their training-ground work. “But it [Arsenal] is probably the biggest challenge.”

Even the composition of Iraola’s back four appears influenced by Arteta. The Arsenal manager has a fondness for deploying centre-backs as full-backs; as, indeed, did Pep Guardiola at the end of his reign at Manchester City. A transformative moment in Liverpool’s season came when Iraola dropped the erratic Jeremie Frimpong for Ronald Araujo, a central defender by trade.

open image in gallery Araujo is developing cult-hero status as a makeshift right-back in Liverpool’s defence ( Getty )

“It definitely helps having a centre-back at right-back when we talk about defending set-pieces,” said Iraola. “It helps a bit with the height and the physicality of the team.” Since Araujo’s introduction, at Ipswich in September, Liverpool have only conceded one league goal with 11 men on the pitch, albeit augmented by three after Ryan Gravenberch’s red card against City and a trio in each of their last two European matches.

“We are defending really well lately but still we have some situations where we need to improve,” said Iraola. That is a recurring theme in his rhetoric. He can seem a project manager, his side forever a work in progress seeking further improvement. Liverpool, with plenty of youth in their team, with a side shorn of the title winners Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate, have an annual aim of Champions League qualification. They might not have pencilled in a title challenge for this season. It took Arteta six-and-a-half years to make Arsenal champions. Few thought Iraola would do it in a year at Anfield. He certainly does not seem to be considering the possibility.

“It is still too early to take big conclusions,” Iraola insisted. Win or lose on Sunday, however, and others will draw them.

News.title: Michael Carrick explains ‘hard truth’ being shared at Man United
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Michael Carrick has insisted that Manchester United’s players and hierarchy are speaking the hard truth to each other in blunt discussions about their troubled season.

Carrick has survived as manager after crisis talks in which chief executive Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox decided to give him the chance to reverse their slide.

And he held clear-the-air talks with Bruno Fernandes after dropping his captain following his criticisms of United’s tactics in last week’s 4-1 defeat to Como.

Carrick has also had meetings with his underachieving squad, who are only 16th in the Premier League and 20th in the Champions League after going eight games without a win, as he revealed they have been honest, even when that is not pleasant.

“It’s pretty clear,” he said. “It’s not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that’s between me and the players, whether that’s between me, Jason or Omar or the owners. It’s the truth, it’s the hard truth at times and it’s what we need to move forward. Whatever we need to move forward, we’ll do.”

Carrick, whose side face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, said he welcomed players disagreeing with each other and with him.

He added: “We always do what we think is going to get the best out of the team. Whether that’s certain players that you speak to at certain points, that’s normal.

“That’s why if you ask for leaders in the dressing room and you want opinions on certain things, then there’s going to be times when you ask that, that’s fine. Absolutely no problem, doesn’t mean that we always agree with that, but absolutely no problem with that. And then we head off in the same direction.”

News.title: Red Roses cruise to dominant victory over United States in final WXV game
News.content:
English rugby chiefs have been on a charm offensive in the United States this week, but the players on the pitch opted for more of a brute-force approach.

The Red Roses were in the unfamiliar position of coming off the back of successive defeats and Meg Jones had called on her team to respond. They certainly did that, looking far more like world champions than they have over the past fortnight with a convincing nine-try win – four of them scored by Claudia Moloney-MacDonald – albeit there is still room for them to “grow”, as Jones put it after the game.

That is what the Rugby Football Union (RFU) have been trying to do off the field. Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, and his colleagues used this fixture in New Jersey as an opportunity to tap into the US market by “creating connections” with business leaders and potential investors.

It is little wonder English rugby is trying to get a piece of the American pie. There are an ever-growing number of US owners in British football and with the US hosting the men’s and women’s Rugby World Cups in 2031 and 2033 interest in the oval-ball game is sure to grow too, although the sparse crowd in New Jersey would suggest there is work to do on that front.

News.title: Embarrassing England on brink of historic World Cup exit
News.content:
It is, because they showed their quality and offered themselves a sniff with their Gallic heroics. They had to maintain that pace on Friday to put the pressure on Samoa, but after the ideal beginning they contracted a nasty case of white-line fever from which they could not recover. “It looks like we’re going out of the tournament,” McDermott said. “That second half got scrappy and we should have handled that a lot better.”

McDermott is not blameless. The directives were clearly to offload when they could, and perhaps when they should not have, and the call to start Jez Litten over Brad O’Neill at hooker was, on reflection, a mistake. Litten has so much more impact off the bench and the Hull KR livewire could have been the spark England required when it proceeded to fall flat. It was also strange to see Lewis coming on in the No 9 role.

Yet it must be noted that this was just McDermott’s third match in charge and that Tonga was his first. With no warm-up game and with his English-based players at a disadvantage because of travel and the jet lag, that all-important opener was appallingly timed. Yet having been a member of the exclusive top three for so long, England must now concede they are merely in the top five. This tournament proved as much.

News.title: Everton give Burnham something to shout about by booking quarter-final spot
News.content:
David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

What a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

News.title: Trump administration loses grip on bird flu, experts warn
News.content:
The Trump administration has been criticised for losing control of a bird flu outbreak that has spread among mink and cattle farms across the United States.

The H5N1 virus has infected around 1,000 people since it was first detected in the late 1990s, killing roughly half of them. While it currently does not spread among humans, scientists have long worried that it could trigger a pandemic, and that each human infection raises the risk of the virus mutating.

A new variant emerged in 2020 and has since spread to millions of birds and hundreds of animal species across the globe, leading to devastating losses in both wildlife and farmed livestock and poultry.

While some countries have introduced tough measures to curb its spread, including mandatory culls of infected animals, “flockdowns” (where birds are kept indoors) and vaccination of farm workers who handle at-risk livestock, experts say the US is allowing the virus to run rampant.

For more than two months, an outbreak has raged unchecked on a Utah farm that raises thousands of mink for fur, news outlet ProPublica reported last week.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

Mink have very similar respiratory systems to humans, increasing the risk that a virus can spread between the animals and people, and undergo a process known as “reassortment”, when two or more viruses mix together to make a new, more dangerous strain.

News.title: Britain faces unprecedented squeeze on incomes, IFS says
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. John Healey has ruled out making “crude cuts” to welfare after he failed to tackle the rising benefits bill in Wednesday’s Budget.

The Chancellor acknowledged last night that the current benefits system is “unsustainable” but said he will only look to make cuts “in a Labour way”.

Speaking to the BBC in the wake of Wednesday’s Budget, Mr Healey promised that “there will be a reduction in the benefits bill” before the next election.

However, he said this will not include “crude cuts” to payments.

He said: “We will do that in a Labour way, and we will do that because it is simply not good for Britain, or progressive, to have a bigger and bigger benefits bills.

“This system is unsustainable. I’ve been clear about that. The Prime Minister’s been clear about that. It’s what you do about it.”

He added: “We have to bring the benefits bill down. You don’t do that by crude cuts, especially when people are feeling the cost of living pressures.”

His comments on welfare come after Tory leader Kemi Badenoch accused Labour of presiding over a Government that had left Britain “overspent, overborrowed, overtaxed and drowning in an out-of-control welfare system”.

She said: “Next year, under Labour, the tax burden will be the highest in our country’s history and our benefits bill is going up by tens of billions of pounds because this Government has put welfare first.”

The latest figures from the Office for Budget Responsibility released on Wednesday revealed that benefits spending is expected to jump by almost 30pc to £431bn by 2032.

Almost half the total is pensions and disability benefits for pensioners, despite the planned abolition of the triple lock. Here is what you need to know.

News.title: Risk of Ebola spread in UK is low, experts stress
News.content:
Infectious disease experts have stressed the likelihood of Ebola spreading to the UK is low after the head of Africa’s health agency warned that the haemorrhagic fever could reach Britain.

The Democratic Republic of Congo is struggling to contain an outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of the deadly virus that began in the volatile eastern region of the country. There have been 10,000 cases, including nearly 5,000 deaths, since the outbreak was first reported in May and it has now become the second largest Ebola epidemic in history.

In recent weeks the virus has spread to Kenya, where there have been nine cases including two deaths, and Nigeria. The case in Nigeria is concerning because the patient, the wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, the country’s capital, had no history of travel to the affected region of DRC. She has now been evacuated to Switzerland.

In comments reported by the Guardian Jean Kaseya, head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, described the outbreak as “unprecedented” as it was the first time that the disease had spread to three geographic regions of the continent. He warned that there was scope for further spread.

“We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot,” he said. “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”

On Wednesday the United States announced that travellers arriving by air would have to sign a statement affirming that they had not been in the DRC within the previous 21 days. Anyone found to provide false or misleading information would face imprisonment or a fine.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) stressed that the risk to the UK is low. Dr Sam Collins, head of guidance, clinical and public health response at the agency, said the Ebola outbreak in DRC is serious but “the UK is well prepared to respond safely and effectively to the risk of imported cases arising here”.

UKHSA is monitoring travel routes from the affected countries and is providing information on symptoms.

The UKHSA said it is rare for Ebola to occur in returning travellers and the NHS has “well established procedures in place” for such a situation.

News.title: Wesley Fofana’s Chelsea nightmare continues as Liverpool win shoot-out
News.content:
It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola said ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”

Sports.title: Man Utd's January plan sums up summer's transfer failings as club make rare move
Sports.content:
Man Utd's January plan sums up summer's transfer failings as club make rare move

Manchester United are willing to make a rarely seen move by entering the January transfer market as they look to rectify their season, which began with some poor summer decisions

View 2 Images Manchester United's hierarchy are prepared to spend in January with their squad being exposed (Image: PA)

Manchester United are ready to act in January by making at least one signing as they look to try and rescue their season.

‌



The Red Devils ploughed all their finances into improving their midfield in the summer, which ended with three new arrivals - Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba. The latter has only just come into the first-team picture after struggling with injury.

The aforementioned duo have question marks over them at this early stage of the season, contributing to the club's worst start to a campaign in 40 years, which has left Michael Carrick as a man under pressure.

It seems the board have accepted their failings, as The Times report that they will look to make an addition in the New Year, with the holes in their squad being seriously exposed.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

But United are not a team who do such business in January, history suggests so. Even in the past under the likes of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Erik ten Hag they've started poorly, but still stuck with the squad they had.

Bruno Fernandes is an example of a January signing proving a huge hit, but notoriously the first month of the year is a tough time to do successful business for the right fee. That is backed up by the fact United have signed only THREE new players in the January transfer window since their capture of Fernandes back in 2020.

Amad was signed from Atalanta the year after, but allowed to remain with the Italian club for a period. More recently Ayden Heaven was captured from Arsenal, but he was another young player who was seen as more of a long-term project.

The only player signed with a view to going straight into the first-team is Patrick Dorgu. He joined from Lecce when Ruben Amorim was in charge.

Dorgu had the profile to play as a wing-back, which was a major part of the system Amorim tried, but failed, to implement. Since his dismissal Dorgu has had positive moments, but is by no means a regular with United reverting back to a conventional back four under Michael Carrick.

View 2 Images Some of Manchester United's summer arrivals are already being called out (Image: Getty Images)

Under Ten Hag, they signed the likes of Jack Butland, Wout Weghorst and Marcel Sabitzer on loan, but their impact was limited, and even those decisions copped criticism.

United's need to bolster all areas of their squad is well known, which will no doubt drive up the price. January signings can be overpriced with selling clubs often knowing that the buyer is in, something of, a desperate situation.

The Red Devils need a left-back, which they failed to land in the summer, to cover for Luke Shaw. They've also not welcome a major centre-half since Leny Yoro in 2024.

In attack, they're without the injured Benjamin Sesko as there's no genuine No 9 to cover for him, leaving the likes of Marcus Rashford and Matheus Cunha to act as makeshift solutions.

Even in midfield their new trio have not lit the world alight, and frustration among fans and ex-players has only mounted by watching how impressive the likes of Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali have been. Two men who United backed away from due to their price tags.

"We are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time, we're going to demand him like to anybody else because he needs to earn the right to play. Otherwise, the rest of the boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair. Let's go."

Arteta also hit out at the FA after they knocked back Arsenal's appeal meaning Dowman will remain suspended for domestic matches against Liverpool, Hull and Newcastle. "Very disappointed, to be fair," he explained.

‌



"Especially with the reckless tackles that he received, and then his reaction is minimal in relation to the action. Disappointed that it's not been overturned after looking at the action back.

View 2 Images Max Dowman was sent off against Fleetwood (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

‌



"It could have been really bad, yeah. And we are lucky today that he hasn't had a broken foot. That's clear. It is what it is. We have put every argument on the table to make a case for it.

"Not only the action, obviously, that it's evident, and when you look it back in slow motion, the previous action and Max's action, it's clear that obviously we have a very different opinion.

Article continues below

"And on top of that, I think you have to read the context of the player, the age, and what happened previously."

Sports.title: Premier League icon breaks silence on being handcuffed at McDonald's for 'stealing a taxi'
Sports.content:
Gareth Barry has the most yellow cards in Premier League history. But he was shown a red by Spanish police when placed in handcuffs after joyriding in a taxi.

The midfielder starred for the likes of Aston Villa, Manchester City and Everton throughout a career that saw him rack up a whopping 54,439 English top-flight minutes. But in 2018, whilst playing for West Brom, Barry's number was up when he and three team-mates, Jonny Evans, Jake Livermore and Boaz Myhill, were caught after an infamous late-night joyride on a team bonding trip to Barcelona.

The 45-year-old has now broken his silence on the Taxi-gate incident and revealed that he was handcuffed after returning to a McDonald's to resolve the situation. Recalling the incident on All Out Football's In The Mixer, Barry said: "Four of us go to an Irish bar and it's past midnight. We broke our curfew.

"So we thought we'd have a couple more drinks and then head home, which we did. The lads are hungry. On the way home, we asked the taxi driver, 'Do you mind just stopping at McDonald's?' As you do. Typical professional footballer food.

‌



You can listen to brand new episodes of In The Mixer on Spotify and Apple Podcasts!

Harry Kane makes knighthood admission as he sets out demand for name change READ MORE :

Jack Grealish's Everton future uncertain as disciplinary issue casts shadow over positive impact READ MORE :

"For some reason, he got out of the car to order it, which was a mistake by the taxi driver. One of us decides to jump in and drive the taxi away as a bit of a joke and said, 'We'll drive it around outside, around in a circle and bring it back.'

"So all four of us are now in the car with no taxi driver, we drive it around, the plan's going well. But we go the wrong way. And the next thing you know, we're in traffic on a highway.

"I'm an experienced player. The experienced pro. I jump out the car and say, 'Right, I'm going to go and tell the taxi driver we're bringing the car back.' But by the time I get there, the police are there.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Barry and three team-mates were involved (Image: Getty)

"So I called the lads and said, 'Don't come back. The police are here.' They continued on and I think they go and take the taxi to the hotel like good boys.

"But then I'm in handcuffs looking for them. In the police car! So I'm ruling myself out of driving this taxi. So you can blame one of the other three.

‌



"Anyway, we got back to the hotel and I call the lads and say, 'Boys, what have you done with the taxi?' - 'We just parked it around the corner.' Fine. I think nothing of it. Just go to bed. The phones are ringing in the morning…

"Team meeting. Alan Pardew goes, 'What's going on lads? Somebody in this team has stole a taxi.' I say to the boys, 'Look, four of us have broken the curfew. We don't throw anyone under the bus.' We stayed in it together.

"We went down the police station and I don't know what they said. I know my side of this story. I protected everyone! But we broke curfew and it was unprofessional. Just one of those team bonding moments that got out of hand."

‌



The four Baggies players did not face any criminal punishment after the taxi driver dropped the charges but they were slapped with disciplinary action by the club. All of them were fined and Barry admitted he was docked two weeks' wages. They also issued a joint public apology, but Barry says that his team should never have embarked on the trip in the first place.

View 3 Images The Baggies played Southampton a few days after the incident and lost 2-1 (Image: Getty)

He continued: "We shouldn't have gone on [that trip], by the way. They booked it thinking we were going to be knocked out of the FA Cup because we were playing Liverpool away at Anfield.

"We ended up beating Liverpool and then we still go and the lads are like, 'We won't do this trip, shouldn't go on this trip because we're playing on the weekend and we're flying back in on Thursday.'

‌



"It's like poor preparation really, isn't it? But the team bonding. You know what happens on team bonding? It's important. So Alan Pardew was like, 'No, we'll continue doing it. We'll have one night out. A bit of team bonding, get some good training, warm weather training and come home.'

"Tuesday, we have the team night out. Fine. No curfew. Wednesday, the next night, Alan Pardew says, 'Right, go get some food lads and make sure you're back at midnight.' Them curfews are dangerous, aren't they?"

The Baggies went on to lose 2-1 to Southampton in their fifth-round clash, with Barry and Evans receiving a mixed reception from the crowd, while back-up keeper Myhill remained on the bench and Livermore was absent through injury.

Sports.title: Man Utd Ineos takeover timeline emerges as Glazers handed major update
Sports.content:
Man Utd Ineos takeover timeline emerges as Glazers handed major update

The Glazers, who took control of the club in a controversial takeover in 2005, remain majority owners after selling a minority stake to Sir Jim Ratcliffe in 2024

View Image Sir Jim Ratcliffe could take full control of Man United in the future

The Glazers could potentially face a Manchester United takeover bid from Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos during the latter half of 2029. The club's most recent financial arrangements provide a significant indication of when a shift in majority ownership might occur. Ratcliffe acquired a 25 per cent stake in United through a deal valued at approximately £1.2billion in 2024, with his Ineos group assuming responsibility for managing football operations.

‌



‌



The British billionaire additionally committed a further £245million in investment, taking his overall financial commitment to roughly £1.5bn. Nevertheless, the Glazer family remains the majority shareholders and retains substantial control over any prospective sale of the club.

‌



According to the conditions of their 2024 arrangement with Ratcliffe, the Americans possess the authority to compel him to dispose of his stake, which has subsequently risen to approximately 28 per cent, should they agree to sell United to a third party under specific circumstances. The Glazers previously placed United's value at around $6bn (£4.5bn) while considering a possible sale, though the club's continuing financial challenges have prompted doubts about whether that valuation remains achievable.

‌



Glazer family angry at Sir Jim Ratcliffe for breaking Man Utd 'promises' READ MORE :

Harry Maguire has already given Man Utd green light for blockbuster January transfer READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

According to The Telegraph, United's recent £411m refinancing deal offered a telling indication of when Ineos might look to increase its shareholding and potentially wrest majority control from the Glazers. The agreement points to 2029 as a potentially pivotal year for the club's ownership structure, positioning United better to settle existing debts while raising funds for their proposed 100,000-seater stadium.

Under the terms of the arrangement, United could settle certain loans without incurring early repayment penalties from 10th June 2029, provided the repayment forms part of the financing arrangements for a new stadium. This could enable the club to clear a portion of the debt stemming from the Glazers' deeply controversial leveraged takeover in 2005, which has continued to heap financial pressure on United ever since.

‌



A further crucial date is 31st December 2029, when a separate credit facility United uses to manage its cash flow is due to expire. With both milestones falling within the same year, financial experts believe the latter half of 2029 could present the perfect opportunity to overhaul the club's debt structure entirely.

Such a development could also pave the way for Ratcliffe to acquire further shares from the Glazers, potentially enabling Ineos to obtain majority control while helping to fund the new stadium. Nevertheless, no arrangement currently confirms that the Glazers plan to relinquish their controlling interest, meaning 2029 represents a potential takeover opportunity rather than a definite date for an ownership transition.

‌



Since finalising his minority investment in February 2024, Ratcliffe has implemented substantial changes behind the scenes at Old Trafford, including cost-reduction initiatives designed to strengthen the club's long-term financial standing.

Yet recent reports indicate the Glazer family has become progressively dissatisfied with how United has been managed under his stewardship, despite granting Ineos responsibility for football operations.

‌



A source with social connections to the American family told the Mail that the situation at Old Trafford represented a 'travesty', asserting it was not what the Glazers had anticipated or been assured of when Ratcliffe became involved. The source also maintained that the Glazers had never run the club in such a fashion, prompting further doubts about their faith in the British billionaire's strategy.

‌



Meanwhile, ESPN reported that another source claimed the Glazers believe Ratcliffe 'couldn't have masterminded a worse situation,' as his cost-cutting measures and changes across several departments reportedly contradict the strategy he initially outlined.

United's woes have also spilled onto the pitch, with the Red Devils enduring a dreadful eight-match winless streak across all competitions. Having secured just a single Premier League victory this season, the club are suffering their worst start to a campaign in nearly 40 years.

‌



Their alarming slump has left them a mere two points above the bottom of the table ahead of Saturday's showdown with Chelsea, heaping further pressure on Ineos and those at the helm of football operations.

The club's dismal performances and mounting financial worries have additionally cast doubt over United's valuation, potentially throwing a spanner in the works should Ratcliffe attempt to secure majority ownership from the Glazers further down the line.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta doubles down on Max Dowman anger and reveals new disappointment
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta doubles down on Max Dowman anger and reveals new disappointment

Max Dowman found himself sent off during Arsenal's loss to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday evening, with Mikel Arteta opening up on Michael Salisbury's decision

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has spoken about Max Dowman's red card (Image: Beanyman Sports)

Mikel Arteta has explained that he remains "very disappointed" that Max Dowman was sent off against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday evening. Arsenal suffered a shock penalty shootout loss to the Fishermen in the Carabao Cup, with the game having finished 1-1 in normal time.

‌



‌



Summer signing Bruno Guimaraes squandered a crucial spot kick, with Jay Lynch diving low and hard to his left to make the save. Conor Haughey then converted coolly to tip the shootout 5-3 in Fleetwood's favour, as the League Two side advanced to the quarter-finals.

‌



There, they will take on Everton on December 15. However, the shock defeat wasn't the only headline; Dowman's red card late on sent football fans into a frenzy. With just four minutes remaining, the 16-year-old was dispossessed by Harrison Neal on the byline, and the Fleetwood defender trapped Dowman's leg in the process.

‌



The teenager reacted instantly by kicking out at Neal, sparking a fracas among players. Salisbury then responded by brandishing a red card Dowman's way, with Arteta seemingly furious at the decision.

And now, the Spaniard has doubled down on his criticism of the official. Speaking in his pre-Liverpool press conference on Friday, he said: "Very disappointed to be fair especially with the reckless tackle that he received.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"His reaction is minimal in compared to the action. It is what it is, we have put every argument on the table to make a case for it. Max's action is clear, obviously we have a very different opinion, you have to read into the context, the age, the player. It could have been really bad and we're really lucky today that he doesn't have a broken foot."

Speaking about his fiery reaction toward Dowman, meanwhile, Arteta added: "My reaction comes in a moment of heat and extreme frustration because I know the consequences of that, especially for Max. We discussed it just before we went out and it will continue happen unfortunately because of how he attracts opponents.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"He's 16 and we have to be very protective of him but also very straight with what we expect from him towards the team, individual and the clubs."

Arsenal had appealed the three-match ban that Dowman faces as a result of his red card, only to see their challenge rejected. His dismissal resulted from 'violent conduct,' which, according to the rules of the game, occurs when a participant "uses or attempts to use excessive force or brutality against an opponent when not challenging for the ball."

‌



View 2 Images Max Dowman was sent off (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

It means that the midfielder will miss Sunday's trip to Anfield, as well as their upcoming matches against Hull City and Newcastle United. However, he is not the only expected absentee.

Article continues below

Bukayo Saka will miss the clash as a result of a muscular injury sustained during Arsenal's Champions League draw with Bayern Munich earlier this month. Arteta said of the winger: "He needed another scan to see the amount of fluid there was resolving, afterwards we will know more about it."

Sports.title: Club owner suing EFL side for £2m over 'cheating' as bitter feud takes ugly twist
Sports.content:
Club owner suing EFL side for £2m over 'cheating' as bitter feud takes ugly twist

Tensions are bubbling over in the English Football League, with a National League team owner taking legal action after accusations of being 'cheated'

View 2 Images Forest Green Rovers owner Dale Vince is suing Peterborough United (Image: PA)

Dale Vince is suing Peterborough United and their head coach, Robbie Savage, for £2million in damages. It comes after the head coach left Forest Green Rovers for Posh earlier this month, with the club's owner Vince claiming that an illegal approach was made.

‌



‌



Speaking with Sky on Friday, Vince was asked if his feud with Peterborough chairman Darragh MacAnthony had been resolved. There, the 65-year-old explained that he is taking legal action against Peterborough, seeking £2m in compensation - the figure which was the buyout in Savage's contract.

‌



He told the broadcaster: "It’s not all sorted. It’s now gone legal and we are suing Peterborough and Robbie Savage for £2 million which was the buy out clause we were cheated out of.

‌



"That process started last week. What has come to light in the last two weeks is an abundance of evidence of an approach made by the chairman of Peterborough himself, while he’s been denying any such approach was made.

England U15s rush to protect referee from being attacked by opponents in extraordinary scenes READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"That’s quite aggrieving really. I know people will say, ‘It’s just football’, but we shouldn’t just shrug our shoulders and allow badness to happen."

‌



Sharing a message on his personal X account, meanwhile, Vince shared a further update with Forest Green fans. He said: "Early start this morning, for me anyway.

"Up before 8am, here at Forest Green. Doing a little bit of TV, just done Sky. Doing ITV and BBC next, and I'll show you what it's all about.

‌



"It's about the changing rooms and it's all about plants. A little bit about Peterborough as well, the news that we've begun a legal process for the tapping up of our manager, ex-manager now, Robbie Savage.

View 2 Images Robbie Savage joined Peterborough earlier this month (Image: Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"And that's the day so far. Plants, and what would you call it? Hassle. Hassle that we didn't want, but what are you going to do?"

‌



The camera then cut away to Vince in the Forest Green dressing room, which featured plants in abundance above player lockers. The owner added: "Here it is, check it out. Changing room, chocka full of plants."

At the time of writing, Forest Green sit 15th in the National League after 13 games played, with five wins, as many losses and three draws to show for their efforts. They face Harrogate Town at Eco Park on Saturday, October 31 at 12.30pm.

‌



Peterborough, meanwhile occupy 21st in League One with a record of two wins, four draws and six losses. Savage has held tenure with the club since October 2, having replaced Luke Williams following a dire start to the season.

Up next for Posh is a 3pm clash with Luton Town on Saturday. That game will take place at the Weston Homes Stadium on London Road, the home of Peterborough United.

Sports.title: Leclerc seals Mexico City practice double as Hamilton suffers technical issue
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue.

Leclerc produced a time of 1:17.827s to finish just over a tenth clear of McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell, with the British pair among 10 drivers who had earlier sat out the opening session to make way for rookie drivers.

Kimi Antonelli, who only needs to finish ninth in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, was a tenth down on his team-mate Russell in fourth.

Hamilton had been on course to go fastest as the session approached its midway point before suffering what appeared to be an engine issue in the final sector of his push lap.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton complained about a power issue before retiring from FP2 at the Mexico City GP

He completed the lap but was then swiftly told by his engineer to pull over on track, ending his session early and denying him valuable information that his rivals were able to gather with their race simulations.

Max Verstappen, another to have sat out first practice, was three tenths off the pace in fifth, with his team-mate Isack Hadjar slotting in behind him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Red Bull's Max Verstappen make contact during FP2 at the Mexico City GP

Verstappen was involved in a bizarre collision with his former team-mate Liam Lawson in the early stages of the session as the four-time world champion attempted to overtake the Racing Bulls driver.

Lawson defended and retained track position, only for the battle to continue on for several more corners before the pair made contact, leaving debris on the track that caused a red flag to be thrown so it could be cleared.

The pair will not only have to explain themselves to their teams, who are both part of the Red Bull family, but also the stewards as they were called to see them following the session.

Sports.title: Canelo and Mbilli make weight for world title fight in Riyadh
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli both made the weight for their WBC super-middleweight world title fight on Saturday in Riyadh.

Canelo was 167.6lb with Mbilli a fraction heavier at 167.8lb.

Alvarez is looking to win back one of the world titles he used to hold in his first fight since his stunning loss to Terence Crawford last year.

When Crawford retired it left the four major world championships vacant and Mbilli became the WBC titlist.

"I'm the challenger now, but in my mind I've always been the champion, ever since I was a little kid," Canelo said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights as Crawford stunned Alvarez to become undisputed super-middleweight champion. Canelo vs. Crawford is available to watch globally only on Netflix

He elected to go straight in with Mbilli, a high-calibre, tough, aggressive fighter, right off the back of that defeat.

"I don't believe in shortcuts. I want to become a world champion again, and that's why I want to face the best. Mbilli is the world champion," Canelo said.

Mbilli, unbeaten with only one draw in his 30-fight professional career, declared: "I have a lot of respect for Canelo and his career, and I congratulate him on everything he has achieved. But inside the ring, it will be a different story, and I'm coming to win.

"I'm ready to shock the world."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at occasions when boxers seemed to slow down time in a fight and make their opponent miss with everything

The event in Riyadh is going ahead amid escalating conflict in the region.

Houthi attacks have targeted Saudi airports, including Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, while security concerns have led to the postponement or cancellation of other sporting events in the kingdom.

"You know, fighting in Saudi for me is special and whatever it takes I'm going to be a world champion again," Canelo has said.

"Because I'm a fighter and I want to achieve a lot of things in boxing yet and that motivates myself. I love boxing."

Could Mbilli tarnish Canelo's legacy?

Matthew Hatton boxed Canelo back in 2011, in the first world title fight of the Mexican superstar's career. He thinks this fight could affect Canelo's legacy.
