“I’m also working really well with Valtteri. I think he’s been very unfortunate in a few races. I think in Austin he showed very strong pace. So it’s not an easy decision for the team.”

However Perez said the team’s priority over the coming months needs to be its preparations for 2027.

“Marcin will be looking at all the data and all the information and he will be ultimately making that decision to see what he thinks is best for the future of the team.

“Obviously we are in a period where we need to evolve extremely quick. The next three or four months [for] the team are really, really crucial in our preparation, so I think it’s down to him.”

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Gives Floyd Mayweather February 6 Ultimatum
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia wants Floyd Mayweather to stop talking and commit to February 6, but the bigger sales job is convincing fans that beating the retired star would carry championship value. Mayweather’s name can sell the event. His unbeaten record gives Garcia something even easier to advertise.

Garcia says Mayweather called him about the fight, and he is now demanding action. His latest post presents February 6 as a date he intends to keep, whether Floyd takes the offer or another opponent gets it.

“You called me and wanted this fight and I agree this is a big fight. But I am fighting FEB6th regardless so unless you actually make this happen then this fight is gone,” Garcia said on X. “You can go fight whoever but this is for a championship. I will TAKE you 0 with pleasure. Final warning no more games let’s make it happen.”

That unbeaten record is the prize Garcia keeps pointing toward. Taking Mayweather’s first professional defeat would generate enormous attention, but it would not mean Garcia had beaten the fighter who once ruled the sport. Floyd would enter February 6 at 49, approaching his 50th birthday.

Garcia is entitled to chase the biggest commercial fight available. Fans are equally entitled to distinguish between beating a famous former champion and beating an elite opponent in his prime. Putting a championship belt into the promotion does not erase that distinction.

Teofimo Lopez has also been mentioned for Garcia’s February return, giving this public ultimatum another purpose: pressure on Mayweather to commit while Garcia advertises that he has alternatives. February 6, 2027, was already being discussed before this latest post.

Ryan’s message establishes what he wants, rather than what both sides have signed. There is no completed agreement announced in the post, and his account of Mayweather’s call remains his account.

The demand is clear enough. Garcia wants Floyd’s name and unbeaten record on the contract. Until that happens, threatening to take the zero is promotion for a fight still waiting to become real.

It looks bad no matter how you view it. A prime fighter holding a major belt trying to strong-arm a fifty-year-old pensioner with a fake deadline is embarrassing theater. Giving Mayweather an ultimatum, as if Ryan is the A-side dictating terms to an icon old enough to be his father, makes Garcia look ridiculous rather than intimidating.

The optics are awful on every level. Floyd has not taken a genuine professional punch since Barack Obama was in the White House. His last legitimate pro test was an already-diminished Pacquiao over a decade ago, and his official retirement bout was a glorified sparring session against a debuting MMA fighter. Everything since has been low-effort exhibitions against kickboxers, reality stars, and YouTubers where nobody gets hurt.

Now you have Ryan, sitting in his physical prime, strutting around like he is doing the boxing world a favor by offering to beat up an inactive senior citizen. Demanding that Floyd hurry up and sign before February 6 only proves Ryan is desperate for the biggest possible check with the lowest possible threat level.

If Ryan really wanted to act like a world champion, he would be issuing ultimatums to Teofimo Lopez, Jaron Ennis, or the killer sharks at 140 and 147. Instead, he is publicly hounding a retired hall of famer to step into the ring so he can cosplay as the guy who conquered Mayweather’s record. Fans see right through it, and issuing a countdown clock to a grandfather only underlines how paper-thin the bravado is.

Sports.title: Oleksander Usyk Weight Cut Excuse Ready For Benavidez Bout
Sports.content:
David Benavidez spent years chasing Canelo Alvarez without ever landing the opportunity. Oleksandr Usyk could hand him the defining blockbuster that eluded him. Usyk takes on the physical risk, stepping down to 200 pounds after a long reign at heavyweight to face a younger, relentless pressure fighter built to break down tired opponents.

Usyk wants a return to cruiserweight for his next outing to target Benavidez, according to advisor Serhii Lapin speaking to Mike Coppinger of The Ring. Benavidez must handle business first against Michal Cieslak on December 5 in Glendale, Arizona, with three cruiserweight belts on the line. The potential clash with Usyk remains an ambitious goal instead of a signed deal.

The appeal for Benavidez stretches far past picking up more hardware. Taking down Usyk offers massive historical prestige, plus the distinct advantage of meeting him at cruiserweight instead of stepping up into heavyweight territory.

Usyk deserves credit for entertaining the idea. Past brilliance at 200 pounds offers no guarantee that his body responds well to another cut. He sits at 39 and turns 40 in January. Dropping weight after so long at heavyweight brings real volatility that glossy promotional hype easily ignores.

In top condition, Usyk possesses the foot speed and angles to keep Benavidez resetting, off balance, unable to plant his feet for heavy combinations. A sharp Usyk can disrupt incoming fire, spin his man, reset the pocket.

Trouble starts if cutting weight robs Usyk of his legs or tank. Benavidez thrives on grinding opponents down, making every exchange costly with dedicated work to the body through the championship rounds. Nobody can call Usyk depleted right now, but assuming the cut goes smoothly is just as reckless.

The built-in weight excuse angle is hard to ignore for Usyk, especially in modern boxing where fighters guard their reputations with an iron fist.

If Usyk drags Benavidez up to heavyweight and gets caught, battered, or outworked by a younger man, there is no safety net. He would lose as a heavyweight champion in his own division, full stop. By dropping to cruiserweight, his camp instantly constructs a built-in narrative cushion: he is almost 40 years old, he gave up size, he sacrificed his body to squeeze back down to 200 pounds for the fans, and he was depleted.

If he wins, he looks like an immortal wizard who conquered two divisions back and forth. If he loses, the media immediately frames it around the brutal weight cut rather than Benavidez simply beating him.

The physical reality makes the cruiserweight decision even more absurd. Benavidez has spent his entire career boiling down from heavyweight proportions. He rehydrated into the 180s and 190s just to bully super middleweights, and at cruiserweight he walks around comfortably above 215. Usyk weighed in the mid-220s for his heavyweight fights.

There is zero reason this fight could not happen at heavyweight, or at least a sensible catchweight, other than the tactical gamesmanship of the narrative.

Benavidez also plays along because he wants no part of heavyweights right now. Facing Usyk at 200 gives Benavidez the biggest brand name in the sport without having to step into the heavyweight ring against giant punchers. It lets Benavidez bypass the true divisional ruler, Jai Opetaia, avoid the terrifying risk of prime cruiserweights, and cash in against a depleted legend.

Both camps know exactly what they are doing. It provides Benavidez a shortcut to a massive scalp and gives Usyk a pre-packaged alibi if his legs fail him down the stretch.

Jai Opetaia belongs in this conversation too. The Ring previously reported Benavidez might target their cruiserweight champion after Cieslak. Moving toward Usyk creates a massive spectacle, yet it sidelines the most dangerous active force currently ruling the division.

Toppling Usyk creates an incredible legacy moment. It still leaves questions about true cruiserweight supremacy if Opetaia stays undefeated on the sideline.

Benavidez gets a crack at an all-time great. Usyk wagers his body can handle the scales without losing the stamina needed to survive deep water. That specific tension turns this matchup into must-see theater.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Looks Shaken At Weigh-In: Body Language Betrays Former King
Sports.content:
Christian Mbilli plans on doing far more than just hanging onto his WBC super middleweight title against Canelo Alvarez in Riyadh. He claims he intends to beat the former champion at his own game, a risky declaration against a technician who thrives on catching aggressive punchers reckless enough to leave gaps.

Canelo answered at Friday’s weigh-in by pointing directly to his 21 years in the ring. The clash boils down to a classic style collision: Mbilli trying to swamp the veteran with sheer volume versus Canelo using veteran ring savvy to time incoming attacks.

That was not the swaggering, unflappable Canelo who used to smirk on the scales and mentally dismiss opponents before the opening bell even sounded.

The body language told the real story. When a fighter has to constantly recite their resume like a rehearsed script, it usually means they are trying to convince themselves just as much as the crowd. Canelo repeating that he has been doing this for 21 years sounded less like an intimidating warning and more like a fighter clinging to past glory to mask present doubt.

The physical reality is staring him right in the face. Canelo knows his gas tank is not what it used to be; his punch output drops every year, and resting on the ropes against a relentless engine like Mbilli is asking for trouble.

Mbilli throws punches in bunches, does not care about reputation, and attacks the midsection with bad intentions. Canelo looked like a veteran who fully realizes he signed up for an absolute grueling night at the office, where his mind might know the right counters to throw, but his legs and reflexes might not respond in time.

“You’re going to see on Saturday what’s going to happen. Tomorrow night, I’m going to beat him in every way. The better the technique, the better the punch. It will change my life a lot. After the victory, my life will change more. Fight of the year, an amazing fight. It will be incredible,” Mbilli stated at the scales.

A victory over Canelo brings instant worldwide credibility that owning a belt by itself never secures. Still, trying to prove he can outbox the Mexican star inside the pocket invites trouble. Mbilli operates best when crowding opponents, digging to the ribs, and forcing a relentless pace that drains older legs.

“This is very important for me. I’ve been doing this for 21 years. It’s important for me to take this title. Well, my experience is obviously very different. He’s never fought anyone like me. Tomorrow, he’s going to fight me,” Canelo said.

Ring mileage only works if Canelo makes Mbilli second-guess his charges. Sharp counterpunches can blunt the champion’s momentum and carve out breathing room between exchanges. Should Mbilli walk through those shots without blinking, ring wisdom alone will not generate the work rate needed to capture rounds on the cards.

Both men made weight without incident. Canelo tipped the scales at 167½ pounds, while Mbilli checked in at 167¾.

If Canelo cannot hurt Mbilli in the first four rounds and force him into retreat, he is in for a miserable evening trying to survive a non-stop wave of pressure.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Crawls Back To Bob Arum After Zuffa Disaster
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson catching up with Bob Arum feels like a smart play on familiar ground. Walking the free agent path lets him call his own shots, yet he still requires deep pockets to bankroll his ring returns plus a broadcaster ready to air them. Sitting idle for nearly twelve months makes those requirements impossible to brush aside.

Stevenson posted a picture flashing a wide grin next to his former promoter out in Houston. Coming off a quiet stint with Zuffa Boxing that failed to deliver an actual ring appearance, seeing Arum in person beats trading insults online over his market value.

🥊‼️Shakur Stevenson meeting with Bob Arum who has Raymond Muratalla the WBO MANDATORY on his stable‼️😳 https://t.co/Y7IRu55hBC — Hassan (@Hassanwellss) October 30, 2026

What Arum will do is facilitate business that serves Top Rank. The WBO ordering Shakur to face Raymond Muratalla at 140 pounds handed Arum all the cards. Muratalla is Top Rank’s guy. Arum can either negotiate a single-fight arrangement to put Shakur on a Top Rank card or push the bout to a purse bid, daring Shakur to find outside financiers willing to outbid ESPN’s ecosystem.

A permanent reunion will happen only if Shakur accepts a massive haircut on his financial expectations. If he still insists on purses detached from gate receipts and pay-per-view buys, Arum will simply use him for the Muratalla mandatory and let him drift back into the market to test reality all over again.

Arum bringing him back under a full, multi-fight promotional banner is another story entirely. Bob knows Shakur’s ceiling down to the exact dollar. Top Rank famously offered him a five-fight deal worth roughly $3 million a bout before he walked away, an offer Shakur rejected because he fancied himself a bona fide pay-per-view attraction. Arum will not bid against himself, nor will he overpay for a style that struggles to move tickets or drive commercial subscriptions.

What matters now is an official fight confirmation. Stevenson has spent enough time arguing about his worth from the sidelines. Whether Arum signs on for the long haul or just finances one night, sitting down together might finally get him back under the arena lights.

For the fighter, the upside makes total sense. Steering his own promotional ship grants creative freedom, but it leaves him hunting for funding, television clearance, plus opponents willing to accept realistic paydays. Total freedom never guarantees an actual fight night on its own.

Arum understands Stevenson’s talent inside the ropes, having spent years selling his headline slots. At the same time, he knows the financial ceiling. If Shakur continues demanding the massive purses reserved for pay-per-view draws, lunch together will not magically fix that gap.

Still, that photo blows up the narrative that Stevenson ran off every ally in boxing. Arum traveled to check in on him, and Shakur made sure the entire sport took notice.

Shakur found out the hard way that self-promotion requires somebody willing to write the check. He rode the wave on Turki Alalshikh cards against Zepeda and Teofimo Lopez, banking huge paydays while assuming that level of funding was the new industry baseline. Then came the Zuffa Boxing detour.

Dana White and company quickly realized what others already knew: paying an artist who fights safety-first eight figures while waiting out catchweight demands makes zero business sense. Zuffa cut their losses, showing him the door without staging a single fight.

Sitting inactive since January with zero broadcast platform and asking for money nobody wants to guarantee leaves him backed into a corner. That Houston photo with Arum was pure PR damage control. Shakur desperately needs the public to believe he has suitors, options, and warmth from the old guard, rather than looking like an isolated fighter out on an island.

Sports.title: Pointless Warburton Clash Wastes What Little Time Carlos Adames Has Left
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames begins his Zuffa Boxing journey with a matchup tailored to set up future UK bouts rather than create instant box office excitement. Ring Magazine officially confirmed that the WBC middleweight champion will meet Gerome Warburton on November 14, headlining Riyadh Season Zuffa Boxing 13 in Saudi Arabia.

This non-title contest takes place above the middleweight limit. Former bantamweight champion Jason Moloney meets Andres Teran on the undercard. News of the matchup leaked on October 19, so today’s press release simply rubber stamps what everyone already knew.

Adames (25-1-1, 18 KOs) gets his chance to make an impression with his new promoter. Building real buzz with Warburton in the opposite corner remains a tough sell. The Welsh fighter sits at number seven in the WBA middleweight rankings, though that ranking looks better on paper than it resonates with mainstream fight fans.

Warburton (18-2-2 KOs) comes into the fight with back-to-back wins over Nathan Heaney. Those victories opened the door for this spot, yet Adames marks a massive upgrade in difficulty. With only two knockouts on Warburton’s entire resume, the promotion cannot rely on a knockout artist angle.

The real motive here seems clear. Zuffa wants to prep Adames for bouts against stablemates Denzel Bentley and Aaron McKenna. Warburton serves as the first British obstacle before Zuffa rolls out bigger names from across the pond. While neither matchup is official, the blueprint makes sense.

Zuffa already has these fighters under contract. Adames gives Bentley and McKenna a legitimate champion to target. A dominant showing against Warburton hands the promotional team fresh footage to roll out for the next phase.

Still, convincing audiences to tune in for the current plan is a different story. Bentley and McKenna give British spectators a hometown reason to care, but domestic ties do not guarantee a massive gate or monster television ratings. In the United States, neither matchup feels like a breakout attraction for Adames.

Bentley’s status complicates things even further. He risks losing his WBO belt after failing to secure a date with mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez. Strip away that belt, and an Adames clash loses much of its luster.

McKenna presents another route, yet the middleweight division continues struggling with star power. Matching in-house talent creates reliable action, but it rarely draws casual viewers into the weight class.

This is classic in-house recycling that completely ignores both the clock on Adames’ career and what actual ticket-buying fight fans care about.

Adames is 32, fights roughly once a year, and carries zero commercial crossover. Handing him Gerome Warburton in a non-title catchweight does nothing. It does not sell tickets, it does not draw eyes to a broadcast, and it certainly does not move the needle for casual viewers who have never heard of the guy. Fans know a glorified sparring session when they see one, so they simply tune out.

The logic of using Warburton as a stepping stone to Denzel Bentley or Aaron McKenna is just as flawed. That entire sequence assumes the public is clamoring to see Adames clean out the British domestic scene. They are not. Bentley and McKenna are solid operators, but neither is a global draw capable of transforming Adames into an attraction.

If the payoff at the end of the tunnel is lukewarm to begin with, burning four to six months on a preliminary warm-up against Warburton makes zero promotional sense.

Time is working against them. With his history of lengthy layoffs, Adames cannot afford to spend prime months ticking boxes for low-profile regional setups. If Zuffa wanted to make a real statement with their middleweight investment, going after recognized names like Tim Tszyu or Vito Mielnicki Jr. would have delivered immediate legitimacy.

Putting Adames in with names fans actually follow forces attention onto the division, creates genuine stakes, and gives Zuffa an immediate return on their money.

Instead, they went the safe, budget-conscious route. The problem is that safety breeds indifference. When the opening move fails to capture anyone’s imagination, the matches lined up behind it end up dead on arrival anyway.

Sports.title: Ben Davison: Help Or Hindrance To His Heavyweights?
Sports.content:
It is rare for a trainer to attract as much publicity as his fighters. However, that is precisely what Ben Davison has succeeded in doing this year. For the uninitiated, Briton Davison is the trainer of heavyweights Moses Itauma, Fabio Wardley and Anthony Joshua.

Ben Davison’s profile as a trainer of heavyweights, though, really skyrocketed when he trained Tyson Fury from 2017 – 2019. During this time, many credited Davison for being responsible for The Gypsy King’s successful return to the ring after an absence of two and a half years, which Fury spent battling his demons and putting on weight.

Indeed, Davison was Fury’s trainer for his world title fight against Deontay Wilder in Los Angeles on 01 December 2018, resulting in a draw, and Wilder retaining his WBC title as the defending Champion. Fury performed well in this fight, proving that he is a talented boxer.

However, he felt there was something missing, and adjustments needed to be made. This fight demonstrated Fury’s skills as a boxer. The Gypsy King was, though, astute enough to know that just being a good boxer was not going to win him any rematch with The Bronze Bomber, famous for his legendary right hand.

Fury therefore changed trainer, enlisting the help of SugarHill Steward, the nephew of the famous Emanuel Steward, who had trained former World Heavyweight Champions Lennox Lewis and Wladimir Klitschko. The Brit did this in the hope that he would be not just a skillful boxer, but also become a ferocious puncher to combat the threat Deontay Wilder posed.

This plan worked. When Fury fought Wilder in their rematch on 22 February 2020 in Las Vegas, Fury beat Wilder by TKO in the 7th Round to win the WBC world title and the vacant The Ring heavyweight title.

Then, again with SugarHill Steward as his trainer, Fury successfully defended his WBC world title and The Ring heavyweight title against Deontay Wilder. This time, Fury went one better and beat Wilder by knockout in the 11th Round of their world title fight on 09 October 2021, also in Las Vegas.

Up to Fury’s last two fights against Wilder, The Gypsy King was not known to have the punch power to become a knockout artist. Under Steward’s tutelage, this situation changed, and Fury’s decision to leave Ben Davison was vindicated.

After Tyson Fury, Davison became the trainer of former World Champion Anthony Joshua. This is where things become interesting, as Davison was in AJ’s corner for his challenge for the IBF world title against then-champion Daniel Dubois. This all-British clash took place on 21 September 2024 at Wembley Stadium in London, England.

Joshua was having trouble in this fight, suffering knockdowns in the 1st, 3rd and 4th Rounds. In the break between the 4th and 5th Rounds, Davison seemed to advise Joshua to take a chance, coming out with the now-infamous “roll the dice” comment to his fighter.

When Davison was questioned about what he meant by this comment in a recent interview with the boxing commentator Spencer Oliver, Davison informed Oliver that the intention was for Joshua to throw a double jab and then a right uppercut at Dubois. Doing this, however, would leave Joshua’s chin exposed.

As the insightful YouTube channel Chris Talks Boxing explains, it would have been better for Davison to have advised AJ at that stage to stay out of trouble for a couple of Rounds, and rely on the jab, giving both trainer and fighter a chance to review tactics at the end of the 5th Round. In this way, Joshua would have conserved energy for the later Rounds, which was necessary, given that he had been in the wars up to that point.

As we know, however, Joshua tried to throw a right uppercut early in the 5th Round, but was caught on the chin by Dubois, forcing the former two-time World Champion to the canvas, and unable to beat the count in the same Round. It would therefore appear that Ben Davison’s tactics in this fight were at best clumsy, and at worst reckless.

Turning now to Moses Itauma, Davison has been his trainer since 2023, and was in Itauma’s corner for his fight for the vacant IBF world title against Filip Hrgović on 29 August at The O2 Arena in London, England. Up to this fight, Itauma had not been past the 6th Round in any professional fight.

Further, Itauma admitted publicly that he had not sparred 12 continuous Rounds, which is bizarre to say the least. On fight night, Itauma ran out of gas and lost to Hrgović by TKO in the 9th Round. In his recent interview with Spencer Oliver, Ben Davison mentioned that Moses Itauma is inexperienced, inferring that this is a possible reason for his loss to the Croatian.

As Chris Talks Boxing again rightly states, however, Itauma may be inexperienced, but it is his trainer Ben Davison’s responsibility to “manage” this lack of experience to get the best out of his fighter. Inexperience on the part of Itauma is therefore no excuse for Davison not preparing the young man adequately for a 12 Round fight.

Finishing with Fabio Wardley, Ben Davison was his trainer for both Wardley’s world title fights against Daniel Dubois this year. Both fights ended in TKO losses for the Ipswich man. Wardley lost his WBO world title to Dubois by TKO in the 11th Round on 09 May at Co-op Live in Manchester, England.

It was a respectable performance by Wardley. However, the rematch on 17 October at The 02 Arena in London, England was a much more one-sided affair, with Dubois winning by TKO in the 2nd Round. This last fight prompted former three-weight World Champion Duke McKenzie to go on the record saying that Ben Davison should seek help from “someone more technically minded” in training Wardley – hardly a ringing endorsement of Davison as a trainer.

Taking Davison’s record with all these heavyweights into account, it is clear that a pattern is emerging. The pattern is that Ben Davison seems unable to step up to the plate when it comes to training heavyweights for world title fights. Boxing is a results-driven sport, or at least it should be. In this regard, Davison has been found wanting, with one draw and four losses in all the Heavyweight world title fights he has been a trainer in.

This represents an 80% loss ratio with not one win. It is, of course, easy to criticize. In his last two Heavyweight world title fights, however, Ben Davison has thrown in the towel to save his fighters from further punishment. You don’t need to be a rocket scientist to come to the conclusion that there is definitely room for improvement.

Ultimately, though, it is for Davison’s heavyweights to decide whether he stays or goes!

Romer Cherubim

Freelance journalist

UK

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Must Get Ben Whittaker’s Next Move Right
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn needs to find Ben Whittaker a fight that prepares him for a world title shot, and Conor Wallace remains the obvious choice. At 29, Whittaker needs meaningful rounds against opponents who can expose his weaknesses, followed by evidence that he can correct them.

Anthony Yarde is among the opponents Hearn has mentioned for Whittaker, although the meeting does not establish that a fight between them is being negotiated.

Plotting what’s next 🌎 https://t.co/AWWFNVJk3p — Eddie Hearn (@EddieHearn) October 29, 2026

Whittaker earned his IBF mandatory position by beating Wallace on October 3, but the closing rounds weakened the case for sending him straight into a title fight. He controlled much of the contest before fading and getting hurt late, leaving a very different impression from the one he had built earlier.

“For me, no, he needs another fight,” Hearn said after the bout, naming Yarde, Wallace and the Joshua Buatsi–Willy Hutchinson winner as possibilities.

That leaves Hearn with a decision about what Whittaker actually needs. Another quick stoppage against an overmatched opponent would offer little preparation for championship opposition. Wallace forced him to work over the distance and exposed weaknesses that a better fighter could punish earlier.

A rematch would give Whittaker the chance to show he can finish strongly against someone who already knows how to hurt him. Wallace would have reason to attack sooner, having allowed Whittaker to collect too many of the early rounds before making his strongest effort.

Trainer Andy Lee cited COVID during the buildup to their first fight. If illness contributed to Whittaker’s late decline, facing Wallace again would provide an opportunity to demonstrate the difference a healthier preparation makes. It would also address the controversy surrounding a chaotic final round in which Whittaker went to the canvas three times without a knockdown being scored.

Yarde would bring a bigger domestic name and a heavier punching threat. That makes him an interesting option, but potentially a dangerous choice for someone who just struggled when Wallace increased the pressure. Whittaker would need to retain his concentration and defensive discipline when tired.

The Buatsi–Hutchinson winner would provide another demanding route. However, Hearn should be careful about treating any of these opponents as a convenient bridge to a title shot. Whittaker’s last performance showed why he needs the work.

Moving away from Wallace could also carry a cost with fans. Hearn has mentioned the rematch, but choosing someone else would leave the impression that his unbeaten fighter is leaving unfinished business behind.

Whittaker has time to improve at 29. His next fight needs to show that improvement, and beating Wallace more decisively would give Hearn something firmer to sell when the world title opportunity arrives.

At Whittaker’s age, a fighter does not develop an engine or an iron will out of nowhere. Those traits are either built into the foundation during the amateur days, or they simply do not exist. Whittaker entered the professional ranks with massive fanfare, an Olympic pedigree, and a style built entirely around showboating, reflexes, and athletic arrogance.

That works beautifully against overmatched opposition or journeymen who stand frozen in front of him. The moment a fighter stops watching the dancing, plants their feet, and marches forward with hard physical pressure, the entire facade begins to crack.

Liam Cameron proved it first. Cameron is a gritty, durable operator who made Whittaker uncomfortable by simply refusing to respect the theatrics, dragging him into physical trench work until that bizarre spill out of the ring brought a premature end. Instead of treating that as a warning light on the dashboard, Matchroom went right back to soft touches.

The Popeye Rivera matchup in Brooklyn was prime evidence of Hearn trying to protect the investment with harmless opposition rather than preparing him for genuine world caliber operators.

Conor Wallace brought that reality back to the surface in vicious fashion. It was not just a case of getting tired. Whittaker looked completely depleted, mentally rattled, and physically incapable of handling heavy incoming fire once the fight entered the championship rounds. Spending the twelfth round touching the canvas multiple times without the referee counting knockdowns was embarrassing for a guy calling out the division’s elite.

Whittaker does not possess the luxury of two or three developmental years to rebuild his gas tank and learn how to fight inside a phone booth. If he steps into the ring with a puncher like Anthony Yarde, or goes anywhere near the division monsters like Artur Beterbiev or Dmitry Bivol, the outcome is predictable. Those men do not wait around for nine rounds before turning on the pressure. They hunt you down from the opening bell.

If Hearn sends him into a rematch with Wallace and Whittaker runs out of gas again, the entire promotional work pops for good. What we saw down the stretch on October 3 might simply be Whittaker’s absolute ceiling under real pressure.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Gets Showcase Treatment Against Nikita Zon
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia against Nikita Zon looks thin for a pay-per-view co-feature. Munguia supplies the name recognition, but Thursday’s press conference offered little proof that his challenger can keep the second biggest bout on Saturday’s Riyadh card competitive.

Richard Schaefer confirmed Munguia against Zon will take place immediately before Canelo Alvarez faces Christian Mbilli. That gives the WBA super middleweight title bout a prime broadcast position, yet the promotional pitch leaned on Zon entering with twelve victories and ten knockouts.

“I watched some of his fights. He’s strong, incredible power, as obviously 10 knockouts show,” Schaefer said during the media session. “I call him actually the new Siberian Rocky.”

Schaefer praised Zon’s power and stoppage record without naming a single credible opponent who proves he belongs in the ring with Munguia. Buyers heard he possesses danger, yet received zero evidence to evaluate that claim.

From a competitive standpoint, it is a gross mismatch. Munguia has logged 48 professional bouts, headlined major cards, and shared the ring with elite competition. Zon has exactly 13 fights, spent his entire career on regional Russian cards, and has never faced anyone remotely close to world class.

Slapping the moniker “the Siberian Rocky” on a completely untested fighter does not make him a threat. It is a fabricated sales gimmick designed to distract from the reality that Zon has done nothing to earn a shot at a belt on a massive international stage. Munguia should blow right through him inside five rounds, and anything less would actually look bad for Munguia.

“I came here to win and I’m leaving with nothing less than a victory. I will become the new world champion,” Zon said through a translator.

That served as his loudest quote, delivering standard bravado expected during fight week. He provided zero tactical detail on what vulnerabilities he intends to target against Munguia.

Munguia kept his comments just as brief. Asked if taking on a challenger with twelve bouts invites complacency, he pointed to his work with trainer Eddy Reynoso.

“I can just say that I’m ready. I had a great camp along Eddie. We prepared strongly,” Munguia stated through a translator. “It will be a great fight. You will see the best version of Jaime Munguia.”

The fighters offered little interest for the event. Schaefer tried filling that void by selling Zon as a raw puncher receiving a life-changing shot against an established Mexican name.

For viewers spending money on the broadcast, that pitch sounds empty. Munguia scoring a routine knockout over an untested opponent helps his record, but a premium slot requires legitimate drama. Watching an established contender cruise through a soft assignment leaves little intrigue.

As for why this fight is happening, it comes down to this. It is about keeping Munguia winning while minimizing any real risk. After picking up the WBA title against Armando Resendiz in May, his team wants him active and collecting paydays without putting him anywhere near dangerous 168-pound contenders like Osleys Iglesias, Diego Pacheco, or Hamzah Sheeraz.

Zon represents the path of least resistance for Munguia: an opponent with zero profile who will stand in front of him and provide highlight-reel footage. Boxing fans are completely exhausted by this specific brand of cynical matchmaking, which is exactly why the fight has generated virtually zero pulse online or in ticket sales.

Promoters seem to operate under the delusion that casual fans will see a gaudy knockout record, hear a goofy nickname like the “Siberian Rocky,” and instantly buy in. Today’s boxing public is far too savvy for that trick. Everyone recognizes an artificially manufactured record compiled in remote regional shows when they see one.

Ghana News.title: MTN Ghana reports 44.4% growth in mobile money transactions as digital services expand
Ghana News.content:
MTN Ghana has reported a 44.4 per cent year-on-year increase in the value of Mobile Money transactions for the first half of 2026, alongside plans to invest US$1.1 billion over three years to expand its network infrastructure and digital services across the country.

The company disclosed this at a Regional Media and Stakeholder Engagement in the Volta Region, where management outlined its financial performance, network expansion plans and digital financial services.

MTN Ghana’s General Manager for Southern Ghana, David Gyimah Boadi, said the company had earmarked approximately US$380 million for investment in 2026 as part of the three-year programme.

He said the investment was intended to improve network capacity, service quality and infrastructure resilience amid growing demand for digital services.

As part of the expansion, MTN plans to deploy 500 new network sites across Ghana in 2026, with the Volta Region among the areas expected to benefit.

The company is also upgrading existing rural network infrastructure to extend 4G connectivity to underserved communities.

The Senior Manager for Sales in the South East, Princess Owusu Nyarko, said the expansion involved identifying communities with coverage gaps, constructing new sites and upgrading existing infrastructure to improve service delivery.

She said the company was also working with technology innovators and industry partners to prepare for emerging connectivity needs.

Financial performance

MTN Ghana also reported growth in its financial performance for the first half of 2026.

Service revenue reached GH¢15 billion, representing a 32.3 per cent increase, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation rose by 47.1 per cent to GH¢9.3 billion.

Profit after tax increased by 46.8 per cent to GH¢5.1 billion, according to figures presented by the company.

MTN further reported that Mobile Money transaction volumes and revenue each grew by 23.3 per cent during the period, while the number of active users increased by 3.1 per cent.

The company said it was strengthening security measures and customer education to address fraud risks associated with the growing use of digital financial services.

Support for businesses

On support for businesses, MTN Ghana’s Network Manager for the South East, Duku Samuel, said the company was providing tailored products for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

These included specialised voice bundles, the SME bundle and JIMAPA, a package designed for women in business.

He said the company was also expanding fibre broadband services and digital payment solutions for businesses, households, enterprises and government agencies.

Investment in education and healthcare

Beyond telecommunications, MTN Ghana highlighted its investments in education, healthcare and digital skills development.

The company said the MTN Ghana Foundation commissioned and handed over an Accident and Emergency Centre valued at GH¢15.4 million to the Ho Teaching Hospital in March 2026.

It also reported that its Girls-in-ICT programme had trained 1,000 girls and 100 teachers in the Volta Region in basic information and communications technology (ICT), digital skills and work readiness, in collaboration with the Ministry of Communications, Digital Technology and Innovation.

Nationally, the company said its Skills Academy had equipped more than 100,000 young people with digital literacy, financial skills and career-readiness competencies.

Sustainability initiatives

MTN Ghana also outlined measures under its sustainability strategy, including the use of solar power at selected network sites, waste separation, recycling and responsible water management.

The company’s Media Relations Adviser, Shiela Sorinye, said sustainability had been integrated into its Ambition 2030 strategy, with measures aimed at reducing its environmental footprint.

The company also reported paying GH¢5.6 billion in direct and indirect taxes and GH¢384.7 million in fees and levies during the first half of 2026.

MTN Ghana, which is marking 30 years of operations in the country, said it would continue investing in network expansion, digital financial services, customer experience and business solutions as part of its growth strategy.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest woman, offer GH¢100,000 reward for Sakumono murder suspect
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service has arrested a 47-year-old woman in connection with the killing of two relatives at the NTHC Estate, Sakumono, in the Greater Accra Region, and declared the principal suspect wanted.

The suspect, identified as Beatrice Mumuni, is believed to have led Samuel Christopher Osei Anto to the residence of the deceased before the murders, according to a police statement

The victims, George Atuguba, 57, and his 47-year-old niece, Irene Atuguba, were killed on Friday, October 30, 2026.

The police have declared Osei Anto wanted to assist investigations and are offering a reward of GH¢100,000 for credible information leading to his arrest.

Police appeal for information

In a statement announcing the arrest, the police urged anyone with information about the whereabouts of Osei Anto to report to the nearest police station.

The public may also contact the police through the emergency numbers 191 or 18555.

The arrest follows preliminary police findings that the killings may have been triggered by a financial dispute involving George Atuguba, who allegedly owed GH¢500,000.

The police had earlier said Osei Anto reportedly went to the victims’ residence with Mumuni to demand repayment of the money, after which a misunderstanding allegedly occurred and the two victims were shot.

The circumstances surrounding the killings remain under investigation.

The police have appealed for public assistance as efforts continue to locate Osei Anto and establish the full circumstances of the incident.

Ghana News.title: Ghana and Burkina Faso seek stronger trade and industrial cooperation at SIAO 2026
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening trade and investment relations with Burkina Faso through a proposed bilateral trade agreement aimed at promoting industrial cooperation, cross-border trade and value addition.

The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, announced this during the opening ceremony of the 18th International Arts and Crafts Fair of Ouagadougou (SIAO 2026) on Friday, October 30.

Delivering the Guest of Honour address, she highlighted opportunities for the two countries to collaborate in handicrafts, agro-processing, shea, cotton, leather and agricultural value chains.

Ghana, which is participating as Guest of Honour alongside Mali and Niger, is showcasing products from all 16 regions at the fair.

The exhibition features a range of Ghanaian products, including Kente, Adinkra, fugu, Bolgatanga baskets, beads, pottery, leather goods and contemporary fashion.

Madam Ofosu-Adjare disclosed that formal trade between Ghana and Burkina Faso exceeded US$1 billion last year.

She stressed the need to strengthen border management, harmonise product standards and facilitate the movement of goods between the two countries to further expand trade.

The proposed bilateral agreement is expected to provide a framework for advancing cooperation and creating opportunities for businesses in both countries.

Ghana News.title: Savannah College of Education teachers decry 19 months without payroll migration
Ghana News.content:
About one hundred and seventy striking workers of two local associations at the Savannah College of Education, namely, the Colleges of Education Teachers Association of Ghana [CETAG] and the Colleges of Education Non-Teaching Staff Association of Ghana (CENTSAG), say the unresolved issues surrounding staff remuneration, recruitment and migration of members to the government payroll are a threat to their welfare and the smooth administration of the college.

"Our concern is not to undermine government efforts or disregard the progress made since the college became a public institution. Rather, we seek to draw attention to the unresolved issues surrounding staff remuneration, recruitment and migration onto the government payroll, which continue to threaten staff and the smooth administration of the college," they indicated.

In a joint press conference in Daboya in the Savannah Region, members of the associations said the transition of the college into the public system can not be deemed complete while staff continue to work without government-paid salaries and a clear roadmap for their migration.

Established in 2022, the Savannah College of Education was, among other things, to contribute to teacher preparation and help address the shortage of professional teachers in the region and beyond.

But in 2024, the college came under mounting pressure from the student body regarding its private status. In response, the government subsequently absorbed the college in March, 2025 after an assessment by the Ghana Tertiary Education Council (G-TEC) in the public colleges of education.

Fast forward, students were put on an allowance, no fee stress, and a pick-up vehicle to the college. But the teachers said they have yet to realise the benefits of the public status of the college.

According to the press statement signed by the leadership of the two associations, Abdalla Abdul-Rahim for CENTSAG and Franklin Aguuri of CETAG said they recognised the importance and the need to integrate it into the public teacher education system and are yet to reap its full benefits.

"The absorption raised legitimate expectations that the college would gradually enjoy the same institutional support, administration arrangements, and staff remuneration framework as other public colleges of education."

"Unfortunately, while some aspects of the transition have progressed, the situation regarding staff remuneration and migration remains unresolved."

While acknowledging government financial obligations to students, the workers expressed concern over what they described as government inconsistencies in the implementation of the transition.

"Particularly the apparent disparity between the support extended to students and infrastructure and the unresolved welfare of staff."

"Our greatest concern, however, is the fact that no staff member of the Savannah College of Education has received salary from the Government since the college's absorption in March, 2025.

"Our staff is not asking for special treatment but for the fair and timely remuneration that should accompany our service in a public institution," they indicated.

One other major grievance that the teachers have attributed as an obstacle driving their plights is the delay in resolving the staff migration challenge in establishing the College's Management Unit.

"The creation of the Management Unit is critical to providing the administrative framework required for the effective management of the college and the processing of staff migration. Despite efforts by the leadership of the college and other stakeholders to address the situation, the process has not progressed as expected."

The striking, however, lamented that the continued uncertainty has created considerable anxiety among staff, particularly because the Management Unit is closely connected to the prospects of resolving their remuneration and migration, not forgetting the lack of a governing council for the college.

Ghana News.title: Changfans on River Tano have reduced thanks to NAIMOS – NAIMOS Spokesperson
Ghana News.content:
The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says the number of changfan machines operating on the River Tano has reduced significantly following sustained enforcement under its Operation Water Shield campaign against illegal mining.

In a Facebook post on Friday, October 30, 2026, the NAIMOS spokesperson, Paa Kwesi Schandorf, said a team of 15 journalists had accompanied officials to the river earlier in the day to assess the impact of the operation.

He said the visit gave the journalists an opportunity to observe and independently assess the progress of the anti-galamsey campaign along the river and its surrounding areas.

“The most crucial development to report is that changfans on River Tano HAVE GREATLY REDUCED,” Mr Schandorf wrote, crediting the sustained operations led by the Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K. S. Appiah.

Sustained operations

Mr Schandorf said NAIMOS would maintain surveillance on the Tano and other critical water sources as the government pursued efforts to restore polluted water bodies to their natural state.

He cautioned, however, that the reduction in mining equipment did not mean the river had already been restored to its original condition.

“The destruction of hundreds of changfans on the Tano River doesn’t immediately make it pure, but it’s a crucial starting point,” he said.

He added that further measures would be taken under the leadership of the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, to protect and restore affected water bodies.

Operation Water Shield

Operation Water Shield is a sustained, intelligence-led enforcement campaign launched by NAIMOS in September 2026 to protect major rivers, watersheds and other critical water resources from illegal mining.

The campaign seeks to move beyond isolated raids by targeting illegal mining activities along river systems, dismantling the machinery used in the operations and preventing miners from returning to areas cleared by security teams. Its priority water bodies include the Birim, Ankobra, Tano, Bia, Pra and Offin rivers, as well as affected sections of the Black and White Volta systems.

The operation has already seen enforcement action along the Tano River. On October 19, for example, NAIMOS destroyed 92 changfan machines and arrested three suspected illegal miners during an operation at Asemkrom in the Aowin Municipality of the Western North Region. The operation targeted mining platforms and equipment operating directly on the river near the Jema-Asekrom Forest Reserve.

NAIMOS has said the broader strategy includes sustained patrols and surveillance to prevent illegal miners from reoccupying cleared areas, alongside action against the networks and equipment suppliers that facilitate illegal mining.

Focus on water-body recovery

The latest assessment comes amid continuing concerns over the environmental damage caused by galamsey, including pollution of rivers and the degradation of surrounding land.

Mr Schandorf said the reduction in changfans was an important step but indicated that further work would be needed to secure the river and support its recovery.

He said NAIMOS would continue its surveillance and enforcement efforts in line with President John Dramani Mahama’s vision of restoring water bodies to their natural condition.

The challenge now is to sustain the gains, prevent illegal mining from returning and establish measurable improvements in the condition of the River Tano.

Ghana News.title: Yagbonwura appeals to Mahama to intervene in Savannah College of Education staff strike
Ghana News.content:
The Overlord of Gonjaland and Life Patron of the Savannah College of Education, Yagbonwura Bii-Kunuto Jewu Soale I, has appealed to President John Dramani Mahama to intervene in the ongoing strike by teaching and non-teaching staff of the institution.

According to him, the industrial action, which has entered its fifth day, is a major concern for the college and the Savannah Region, and requires urgent presidential intervention to get the workers back to work.

"I know and believe that my Son, the President, says yes, the challenges will be solved. So, what we need to hear from him now is to talk to his officers to address the workers' grievances, if not all, but the major ones."

The Overlord appealed in an interview with JoyNews through the Secretary to the Wasipe Traditional Council, Jantonwura Peter Awusi Yakubu, in Daboya.

The Overlord is particularly concerned about the impact of the strike on students, with kitchen staff also joining the industrial action.

He says the situation has disrupted food services at the college, leaving students without meals prepared on campus.

"I heard the cooks are also on strike, and it becomes a double problem because the chiefs I sent to the college came back and told me that the school doesn't even have food to feed the students. This is very serious."

About 170 teaching and non-teaching staff, drawn from the Colleges of Education Teachers Association of Ghana and the Colleges of Education Non-Teaching Staff Association of Ghana, are participating in the strike.

The workers are demanding their migration onto the public payroll system, saying they have not received payment for their services since the college was absorbed by the government in March 2025.

They are also demanding the establishment of the college Management Unit to work on their migration to the public payroll.

They also claim the situation has contributed to the departure of 17 teachers to other colleges of education.

A visit by JoyNews to the college’s kitchen revealed that both the kitchen and pantry had been locked, leaving students to make alternative arrangements for their meals outside the campus.

The strike has heightened tension on campus and raised concerns about the welfare of students and the need for an urgent resolution to the dispute.

Ghana News.title: Debibi United President fires back at GoldStars coach over cassava pitch comment
Ghana News.content:
Alexander Ababio

Debibi United Chief Executive Officer, Alexander Ababio, has hit back at the coach of Bibiani GoldStars Petros Koukouras over his comments about the club's playing pitch, describing the remarks as reckless and unreasonable.

After Gold Stars suffered a 1-0 defeat to Debibi United in the 2026/27 Ghana Premier League Matchday 7, the Greek coach expressed his displeasure over the state of the Debibi Presby Park, describing the playing surface as more suitable for cassava farming than football.

Speaking to Nhyira FM, Mr Ababio expressed his displeasure with Perto’s statement, questioning the reasoning behind the comparison involving cassava cultivation in his country.

“If that’s how they grow cassava in his country [Greek], then I don’t know how they feed them,” Ababio said.

The Debibi United CEO further urged the coach to concentrate on his professional responsibilities instead of making comments he considers inappropriate.

“He should think about his job and stop saying nonsense. It was a reckless and unreasonable statement,” he added.

Ababio's response comes amid discussions surrounding the condition of the playing surface in Ghana football. Petros is one of the foreign coaches who have criticized the state of pitches in the country.

Premier League debutants Debibi United top of the bottom three in the league after eight games with 7 points. On Sunday, Debibi United will face Hearts of Oak at the Debibi Presby Park.

CEO Alexander Ababio said they are focused on remaining in the league.

"Our target is to remain in the league despite our poor start to the season,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Niece and uncle shot dead at Sakumono over alleged GH¢500,000 debt
Ghana News.content:
The police have launched investigations into the killing of a 57-year-old man and his 47-year-old niece at the NTHC Estate, Sakumono, in the Greater Accra Region, following a reported dispute over a GH¢500,000 debt.

The deceased have been identified as George Atuguba and Irene Atuguba.

A statement signed by Chief Superintendent Juliana Obeng, Head of Public Affairs at the Accra Regional Police Command on Friday, October 30, 2026, said officers were dispatched to the residence after the Sakumono District Police Command received information about the incident.

The bodies of the two relatives were found lying in a pool of blood, the statement said.

Debt dispute

Preliminary police investigations suggest that the incident may have been triggered by a financial dispute involving George Atuguba, who had allegedly borrowed GH¢500,000 from a suspect but failed to repay the amount.

The police identified the suspect as Samuel Christopher Osei Anto.

According to the statement, the suspect reportedly went to the deceased’s residence on the morning of the incident with a woman identified as Beatrice Mumuni to demand repayment.

A misunderstanding allegedly ensued, during which the suspect shot and killed George Atuguba and his niece, Irene Atuguba.

The circumstances surrounding the reported shooting are still under investigation.

Bodies sent for autopsy

The police said the two victims were rushed to a hospital, where a medical officer pronounced them dead.

Their bodies have since been deposited at the Police Hospital mortuary for preservation and autopsy.

The Accra Regional Police Command said efforts were being made to apprehend the suspect and bring him to justice.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: US judge orders ethics inquiry into Trump lawyers over golf course case
World.content:
Judge Ana Reyes calls on US government lawyers to explain contradictory statements about the East Potomac Golf Links.

Share US judge orders ethics inquiry into Trump lawyers over golf course case on social media

A United States federal judge has opened a “formal inquiry” into whether US government lawyers misled the court over plans to transform a historic public golf course in Washington, DC.

Friday’s manoeuvre escalates an ongoing legal fight over President Donald Trump’s efforts to reshape the US capital.

Judge Ana Reyes of the US District Court for the District of Columbia announced she would appoint a special master to examine whether government officials withheld information or made misleading assertions concerning the East Potomac Golf Links.

The inquiry will not establish whether government lawyers committed misconduct. It will instead determine whether their conduct breached professional or ethical obligations.

The inquiry follows a series of contradictory statements by administration officials about plans to renovate the course, notably after Trump announced he would proceed with the project on social media.

Reyes questioned Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward Jr for more than two hours during Friday’s hearing, repeatedly comparing his testimony with the president’s online announcements.

She also asked him whether a National Park Service official had been instructed to omit details from a court declaration.

Trump’s posts, which began earlier this month on his Truth Social account, indicated the course would close for 15 months, starting on November 15, to accommodate a major redevelopment.

Yet officials from various government agencies – including the Interior Department, Justice Department and National Park Service – had previously been unable to confirm the existence or scope of any plans when questioned by the judge.



Earlier this year, Reyes had ordered the government to provide advance notice of substantive construction work at the site.

But despite her order, the dispute intensified earlier this month after more than 400 trees were removed from the golf course. Reyes subsequently extended her injunction against the government making any further “irreversible” changes to the site.

On Wednesday, the Justice Department informed the court that the National Park Service would submit a design from golf course architect Tom Fazio to the National Capital Planning Commission on Friday.

But Justice Department lawyers had, up to that point, declined to acknowledge any plans with regards to the golf course.

Even before Wednesday’s submission to the court, Trump had posted about commissioning Fazio “to build a World Class Championship Golf Course” on the park site, which currently includes biking and walking paths.

The DC Preservation League, which filed the lawsuit in February, has argued the redevelopment could violate environmental protections and damage a historically significant public space.

The case marks one of two legal battles unfolding over Trump’s plans for Washington, DC, on Friday.

Another US judge is due to hear a separate challenge to the White House’s proposed construction of a 75-metre (250-foot) memorial arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

The lawsuits raise broader questions about the limits of presidential authority over federal land and public monuments.

David Super, a professor at the Georgetown University Law Center, told The Associated Press news agency that the cases reflect a shift in how the administration approaches legal constraints on executive power.

“There was always the assumption that you would try to do things that were legal,” Super said. “What we’re seeing here now is that if you think the federal courts can’t stop you”, you can break the law.

World.title: Swiss supreme court upholds Liberian ex-rebel commander’s 20-year sentence
World.content:
Alieu Kosiah killed civilians and unarmed soldiers, and ordered lootings and other crimes against humanity.

Switzerland’s supreme court upheld a 20-year jail sentence for former Liberian rebel commander Alieu Kosiah on Friday, but overturned a conviction for crimes against humanity.
