He described Mr Hamzat as a candidate with experience in public service and the private sector, adding that his time as deputy governor had prepared him for the state’s top office.

Former Lagos Deputy Governor Sarah Sosan, speaking on behalf of the state’s Governors’ Advisory Council, also endorsed Mr Hamzat, describing him as a committed public servant with experience as a commissioner and deputy governor.

Mrs Sosan said Lagos should build on its existing development record rather than abandon policies and projects that had worked.

“Lagos is not for experiment,” she said.

She said the manifesto should address the needs of residents in areas including roads, transportation, education, healthcare, security, housing and the environment.

The APC leaders called on party members to mobilise support for Mr Hamzat ahead of the governorship election.

World.title: Chris Okafor: Doris Ogala remains in custody as court postpones bail ruling
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Lagos on Friday adjourned the bail hearing of actress Doris Ogala until 6 November in the case involving her and Chris Okafor, founder of the Mountain of Liberation and Miracle Ministry.

PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that Justice Akintayo Aluko ordered the remand of Ms Ogala, the African Action Congress (AAC) governorship candidate in the forthcoming Abia State election, at Ikoyi Correctional Centre.

The actress appeared before the court over allegations bordering on cyberstalking, cyberbullying and attempted extortion, lawyers representing both parties told this newspaper.

Ife Ajayi, who represents Mr Okafor, and Nzeakor Atulomah confirmed that the judge adjourned the bail hearing to 6 November, leaving Ms Ogala in custody pending the court’s decision.

“The case was adjourned till 6th Nov 2026 for ruling on her bail application. She continues to remain in the correctional facility, Ikoyi Prison”, Mr Ajayi said.

Mr Atulomah expressed confidence that his client would secure bail when the court resumed proceedings.

“My juniors were in court. The bail application was taken today and adjourned to 6 Nov for ruling. We’re hopeful the court would admit the defendant to bail. As we argued before the court, the charges are ‘bailable,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ruling

Meanwhile, Justice Aluko said the actress’s actions disrupted the court’s schedule, leaving more than seven other cases listed for that day unheard.

He revealed that he initially considered committing her for contempt following the incident but eventually spared her, despite believing that her behaviour justified such a punishment.

According to the judge, Ms Ogala could have faced at least two months in prison for obstructing the court’s proceedings.

Justice Aluko said, “She should have been given some form of imprisonment, right, on that day, but I kept my cool, and I rose. Why do you have to start shouting and start singing in the open court? You conducted yourself in a manner that forced the court to rise. That’s what you did, and it’s already recorded.”

The judge also criticised the defence counsel for failing to acknowledge the incident and explain the defendant’s conduct before presenting arguments in support of the bail application.

He recalled that he had personally ordered an expedited hearing of the application and taken steps to ensure that the court heard it within 48 hours.

He said he was disappointed that Wednesday’s disruption occurred despite his efforts to fast-track the proceedings.

Ogala speaks

Speaking after the court ordered her return to prison, Ms Ogala alleged that Mr Okafor and others had deliberately frustrated her bail hearing.

She maintained that she neither feared nor felt intimidated by anyone involved in the case.

She further alleged that some individuals had politically motivated her continued detention to distract her from her campaign to become Abia State governor.

“This thing here is already prepared, but one thing you must know about Doris Ogala is that I am not perturbed. They said the bail ruling is on Friday, but that Friday, they will still send me back. You know why? Because they don’t want me to come out. First, they don’t want me to campaign. This is politically motivated. More than four pastors and the government come together to keep me down here.

“But whether they like it or not, bail is my right. They will leave me. If they like, let them keep me here for 10 years; I am not afraid of them. You see this court? I’m disappointed that our judicial system has reduced itself to this level. Imagine a judge doing the bidding of a pastor who did not even attend school. I am ashamed of the judicial system of this country”, said the actress.

Disappointment

The actress further expressed displeasure with the Ministry of Justice over its involvement in what she called a “boyfriend and girlfriend” affair.

She maintained that prison differed from what people generally imagined and stressed that she remained unconvicted. She accused influential figures in the case of using the law as a weapon against her.

“I’m ashamed of the Ministry of Justice to reduce themselves to this level of now fighting boyfriend and girlfriend matters in the name of the federal government. This case is between the federal government and Doris Ogalla. I am not afraid of them. Every powerful man you see in this life has gone into prison, and they came out strong. Doris is not afraid. I am going back to prison.

“I’m not afraid of Chris Okafor. And you will not bend me. I want you guys to know that it is Doris today. It will be you tomorrow. You are sitting down there saying that Doris is guilty. I am not guilty. If Chris Okafor is not afraid, why don’t he stop putting me in prison with his resources and come let us face the court. Let’s go to the trial and see who is guilty. But you see this matter? I will not stop it. I will get to the end of it. You know me now.”

Ms Ogala vowed to get to the root of the matter and urged her fans and supporters not to listen to the negative things people are saying.

“They cannot intimidate me. Alex Otti, I am not afraid of you.”

World.title: Organisers reveals how Kane edged Mbappe to Ballon d’Or win
World.content:
England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane kisses the trophy on stage after receiving the Ballon d’Or award for the best male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP)

Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or by the smallest margin under its current voting system when he edged Kylian Mbappe by 28 points, France Football which runs the awards, revealed on Friday.

The magazine published a breakdown of the votes in its Friday edition.

Bayern Munich’s Kane, the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, received 40 first-place votes from the 100 jurors and a total of 1,055 points. France captain Mbappe of Real Madrid was placed first 23 times and finished with 1,027 points.

The previous smallest margin was 41 when Rodri, then of Manchester City, edged another Real player Vinicius Junior by 41 points in 2024.

Last season, Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele totalled 1,380 points as he finished 321 points ahead of Lamine Yamal of Barcelona.

This summer, Yamal won a World Cup with Spain but he finished third in the voting on 881 points, 174 behind Kane.

The Ballon d’Or is awarded following a vote by journalists (one per country) representing the top 100 nations in the FIFA rankings for men, and the top 50 for women.

World.title: Gunmen attack ADC guber candidate’s convoy in Sokoto, candidate escapes
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Sokoto State, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, has reportedly escaped unhurt after suspected gunmen opened fire on his convoy near the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport on Friday night.

The incident occurred at about 9pm on October 30, 2026, shortly after Dan’iya had escorted former Sokoto State Governor and Senator representing Sokoto South, Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, to the airport.

The candidate’s bulletproof sports utility vehicles were reportedly damaged in the shooting.

Confirming the incident, the Sokoto State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmad Rufae, said the command had received a report of the incident at the airport and would take necessary action.

He added that anyone found culpable would be dealt with in accordance with the law.

In a statement issued by his media aide, Aminu Abdullahi, Dan’iya alleged that personnel of the Sokoto Marshal and the Sokoto State Community Guard blocked his convoy and prevented it from passing through the airport area.

According to the statement, the personnel claimed they were acting on directives from their superiors not to allow ADC members into Sokoto State.

It further alleged that attempts by members of Dan’iya’s security team to resolve the confrontation failed before gunshots were fired, damaging the candidate’s bulletproof vehicles.

The statement also claimed that two Department of State Services (DSS) operatives attached to the candidate’s security team were detained during the confrontation.

Dan’iya described the incident as a threat to his personal safety and a development capable of undermining democratic freedoms, political participation and peaceful coexistence in the state.

The ADC candidate also alleged that earlier on Friday, his team had observed unusual deployments of Sokoto Marshal and Community Guard personnel at various entry points into the state, where vehicles bearing ADC inscriptions were allegedly stopped from entering.

He said what initially appeared to be routine security operations had raised concerns about a possible attempt to restrict the movement and political activities of opposition members.

“If security personnel can block a gubernatorial candidate, fire gunshots during a confrontation, damage his vehicle and detain officers assigned to his protection, then the people of Sokoto deserve urgent answers.

“No one should be above the law, and no security outfit should be used to threaten political opponents,” Dan’iya was quoted as saying.

The candidate disclosed that he had visited the Commissioner of Police in the state to formally report the incident, present his account of what transpired and seek intervention.

He called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the DSS and other relevant security authorities to investigate the incident, identify those responsible and determine whether any unlawful orders had been issued.

Dan’iya also demanded the immediate release of the two DSS operatives, if they remained in custody, and urged the authorities to preserve available video footage, operational records, eyewitness accounts and other evidence for an impartial investigation.

He appealed to the Federal Government, the National Assembly, human rights organisations and the international community to pay attention to the security situation in Sokoto, warning that political intimidation and violence could threaten the credibility of the democratic process.

The ADC candidate also challenged the Sokoto State Government to clarify the alleged directives attributed to the security personnel and ensure that state-controlled security outfits operated within the law and without political interference.

“Sokoto is not the property of any government or political party. Every Nigerian has the right to enter the state, move freely and participate in lawful political activities. Any order intended to exclude ADC members from Sokoto would be unacceptable and must be investigated,” he said.

Despite the incident, Dan’iya urged his supporters to remain calm, avoid provocation and refrain from retaliation, insisting that neither intimidation nor violence would make him or the ADC abandon their constitutional and democratic rights.

He said he would continue to pursue his political ambition peacefully and lawfully, while urging security agencies to protect citizens irrespective of their political affiliations.

The allegations contained in the ADC statement had yet to be independently verified as of the time of filing this report.

There was also no official response from the Sokoto State Government, the Sokoto Marshal or the Community Guard explaining their account of the incident.

The police and other relevant security authorities are expected to clarify the circumstances surrounding the reported shooting, the alleged detention of the DSS operatives and the damage to the candidate’s convoy.

World.title: NDLEA: No payment for drug tests by Interior Ministry recruits
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has announced that applicants undergoing recruitment into four agencies under the Ministry of Interior will not be required to pay for the mandatory Drug Integrity Test (DIT).

The agencies are the Nigerian Correctional Service, Nigeria Immigration Service, Federal Fire Service and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps.

The NDLEA said arrangements had been concluded for the exercise, adding that the Ministry of Interior had made bulk payment to cover the testing of all new recruits.

Consequently, candidates and personnel participating in the exercise were advised not to make any payment to NDLEA officials, testing centres or through any other payment channel.

The agency’s spokesman, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement, explaining that candidates would be required to access the NDLEA Drug Integrity Test portal through a designated link or access point to be provided on their respective institutional portals.

He said the arrangement was designed to ensure a seamless and orderly testing process.

According to Babafemi, the portal would enable candidates to complete the necessary registration and documentation before proceeding with the test without making additional payments.

The statement added that the agency appreciated the cooperation of the Ministry of Interior and remained committed to ensuring a smooth, transparent and efficient implementation of the exercise.

World.title: Sowore, police differ over attack in Ekiti
World.content:
Omoyele Sowore, presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), and the Ekiti State Police Command have given conflicting accounts of an incident at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, on Friday.

While Sowore insisted that he and members of his team were violently attacked, the police described the incident as an altercation with some individuals, saying the activist sustained a minor injury.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Sunday Abutu, said the command received an alert that Sowore was having issues with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti and immediately deployed operatives to the scene.

Abutu said the operatives rescued the AAC presidential candidate and took him to the Police Hospital, Ado-Ekiti, where he was receiving treatment.

However, Sowore, in a statement published on his social media accounts, rejected the police description of the incident as an “altercation”.

“There was no altercation! We were attacked!” he declared.

He accused the Ekiti State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS) of attempting to suppress evidence relating to the incident.

Sowore alleged that security operatives seized CCTV footage from the restaurant where the incident occurred, claiming that the attackers were captured on camera and accusing the agencies of attempting to shield those responsible.

He also faulted the state Commissioner of Police, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, for describing the incident as an altercation, saying the police commissioner had visited the scene and seen the injuries sustained by the victims but subsequently played down their severity.

Sowore further alleged that DSS operatives had been trailing and harassing him since his arrival in the state on Thursday.

He claimed that the operatives also threatened the manager of a restaurant where he and his team had earlier eaten, warning him against allowing them to use the premises again.

He said the attack occurred shortly after he concluded an interview at MIDAS FM 90.5 in Ado-Ekiti on Friday.

Sowore also alleged that some of the attackers came from the Ekiti State Government House and received operational support from DSS operatives.

Police Response

The police, however, denied reports that the activist was kidnapped, following a social media post claiming that he had been seized by armed thugs and his whereabouts were unknown.

Abutu said in a statement that the command wished to clarify that Sowore was not kidnapped but was rescued by police operatives after they received information about the incident.

“The command wishes to categorically clarify that Mr. Sowore was not kidnapped. Rather, preliminary information indicates that he had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, following which the police were immediately alerted.

“Upon receiving the report, police operatives swiftly mobilised to the scene and successfully rescued him. He, however, sustained a minor injury and is currently receiving medical attention at the Police Hospital, Ado-Ekiti,” the statement read.

The police spokesman said the Commissioner of Police, Michael Falade, had ordered a discreet investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, identify those involved and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice.

The command urged members of the public to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information capable of creating panic and tension.

World.title: Hakimi bags hat-trick as Paris Saint-Germain rip Le Havre to pieces
World.content:
PSG’s Moroccan defender #02 Achraf Hakimi (R) celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s fifth goal during the French L1 football match between Le Havre Athletic Club and Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) at Stade Oceane in Le Havre, north-western France on October 30, 2026. (Photo by Guillaume SALIGOT / AFP)

Achraf Hakimi rose to the occasion scoring a glorious hat-trick on Friday as a heavily rotated Paris Saint-Germain thumped rock-bottom Le Havre 5-1 in Ligue 1.

PSG’s nearest Ligue 1 rivals Rennes lost 5-2 at Nice to allow the champions to open a four-point gap atop the table with 20pts after nine games.

Lille host Lens later Friday and can close to within two points of PSG should they win, while Monaco can do the same if they win at Paris FC on Sunday.

Le Havre gave PSG a game early on as they suddenly surged forward in numbers with the PSG backline scampering in retreat before striker Josh Maja hammered in the opener against the run of play on 18 minutes.

Pushing for a second, Le Havre were carved open in a quick-fire move with Belgian winger Mika Godts racing onto a Hakimi through-ball to level on 26min.

Two minutes later Hakimi left the defence trailing and his blistering low drive just inside the near post made it 2-1.

The European champions were running the Normandy side ragged before Hakimi scored his second with a fierce free-kick that curled low past the ‘keeper Arnaud Bodard to put PSG 3-1 up.

On a lightning break the hosts poured everyone forward in a brave but naive effort to get back into the game, only for PSG to burst back, catching the home goalkeeper way off his line with not a single defender in his half.

Senny Mayulu ran around the horrified stopper, and his cool long-range finish hit the back of the net with nobody in the box effectively ending the contest, just after the hour.

Hakimi’s hat-trick arrived when he threaded a shot through a forest of players on 69 minutes and had hardly finished a triumphant celebration when coach Luis Enrique subbed him off.

Luis Enrique left stars Desire Doue, Vitinha and Joao Neves on the bench while Ousmane Dembele and Georgian attacker Khvicha Kvaratskhelia were missing through injury.

World.title: Fake soldier arrested for attacking employer, stealing car
World.content:
By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi

The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested a 26-year-old man, John Umar Shehu, for allegedly impersonating a Nigerian Army personnel, assaulting a prospective employer and stealing his vehicle in Bauchi.

The suspect, a resident of Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, was also accused of criminal breach of trust and theft.

The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Habib Nafiu, disclosed this in a statement issued on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, on Friday in Bauchi.

According to the statement, the suspect was arrested following a petition received by the command on October 22, 2026, from one Salisu, a resident of the Gida Dubu area of Bauchi.

The petitioner reportedly told the police that the suspect had contacted him on October 18, seeking employment as a driver at his pure water factory. He was subsequently invited for an interview and driving assessment.

However, during the assessment on October 22, the suspect allegedly attacked the factory owner and his neighbour’s son before fleeing with the employer’s vehicle.

The stolen vehicle, a white H-Jet motor vehicle with registration number AE-278-ALK, was later recovered by police detectives in Jos, Plateau State.

The police also recovered a green Infinix Smart 5X phone allegedly stolen alongside the vehicle.

Nafiu said a search conducted on the suspect led to the recovery of various Nigerian Army uniforms and items, including desert and green camouflage uniforms, a jungle hat, an Army raincoat, a camouflage vest and an Army sweater.

He added that the suspect allegedly presented himself as Private Umar Shehu, with service number NA/22/82/1064, claiming to be attached to the 7 Division, Maimalari Barracks, 134 Special Forces Battalion, Borno State.

The police spokesman said the arrest followed an intelligence-led investigation by detectives of the command.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, condemned the alleged impersonation, warning that the command would not tolerate the use of the identities and uniforms of security agencies to perpetrate criminal activities.

Aliyu assured that the suspect would be thoroughly investigated and charged to court.

He urged residents to exercise caution when engaging strangers for employment, particularly in sensitive positions, and advised members of the public to verify the identities and credentials of individuals claiming to be personnel of security agencies.

The commissioner also called on residents to promptly report suspicious activities to the police, assuring them of the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state.

World.title: 2027: Rivers ADC seeks Ikwerre Elders’ support for Atiku, Amaechi
World.content:
By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt

The Rivers State chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has met with leaders of the Ikwerre ethnic nationality to seek support for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and his running mate, Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The party’s leadership, led by its state chairman, Dr. Chukwudi Dimkpa, visited Ogbakor Ikwerre, the apex socio-cultural organisation of the Ikwerre people, to present its candidates and solicit the elders’ support.

Dimkpa told the elders and community leaders that the party considered it important to present its candidates to them as respected statesmen and custodians of Ikwerre cultural heritage.

He said an Atiku-Amaechi presidency would focus on moving the country forward, adding that the ADC chose the duo because of their experience and readiness to turn around the nation’s fortunes.

The state chairman also used the opportunity to formally present the party’s governorship candidate, Dr. Gabriel Pidomson, his running mate, Mr. David Okumgba, as well as its senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly candidates of Ikwerre extraction, seeking the elders’ prayers and support.

“The ADC as a party recognises Ogbakor Ikwerre as a foremost socio-cultural institution representing the identity, heritage and collective interests of the Ikwerre ethnic nationality,” he said.

In his address, Pidomson reminded the elders of the significance of Amaechi’s vice-presidential candidacy, describing him as an illustrious son of Ikwerre who is running alongside Atiku on the ADC presidential ticket.

He expressed hope that the Atiku-Amaechi ticket would emerge victorious in the 2027 presidential election, with Atiku becoming president and Amaechi vice-president.

Pidomson described the prospect of an Ikwerre son occupying the nation’s second-highest political office as significant to the political history and national participation of the ethnic nationality.

He also pledged inclusive governance if elected governor of Rivers State.

“If I am elected Governor of Rivers State, I promise to be a governor for all Rivers people, irrespective of ethnic background, political affiliation or other differences.

“We will build a new Rivers State that will reflect the collective aspirations of its people, with emphasis on inclusive governance, unity, development and the wellbeing of citizens,” he said.

In his remarks, the ADC Deputy National Chairman and Chairman of the Rivers State Governorship Campaign Council, Senator Andrew Uchendu, commended Ogbakor Ikwerre for its contributions to the development and continued existence of Rivers State.

Uchendu recalled the roles played by prominent personalities, including centenarian Prof. Otonti Nduka, Chief Samson Agbaru and Prof. Augustine Ahiazu, in the struggle for greater recognition, inclusion and political representation for the Ikwerre people.

He said their sacrifices and sustained efforts contributed to the emergence of three governors of Rivers State from Ikwerre extraction.

The ADC delegation was received by the President-General of Ogbakor Ikwerre Cultural Organisation Worldwide, HRM King Godspower W. Onuekwa, PhD; its First Vice-President, Prof. Hilary Wordu; Prof. Otonti Nduka; Chief Samson Agbaru; Prof. Augustine Ahiazu and other prominent members.

The Ogbakor Ikwerre leadership welcomed the ADC delegation and offered prayers, blessings and advice.

World.title: Lagos warns residents of impending extreme heat
World.content:
Sanwo-Olu

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has warned residents to prepare for possible extreme heat and associated environmental and public health challenges as climate outlooks indicate rising temperatures across parts of Africa, including Nigeria.

The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, gave the advisory on Friday, urging residents to take preventive measures to protect their health and wellbeing.

Wahab said the strengthening El Niño climate pattern, alongside the seasonal transition into the dry season, could contribute to unusual temperature conditions, increased heat discomfort, dry spells, dust and deteriorating air quality.

He noted that although the intensity and local impact would depend on prevailing weather patterns, residents should take the emerging climate risks seriously.

According to him, Lagos, as a densely populated and rapidly urbanising coastal city, could face heightened exposure to extreme heat.

“The concentration of buildings, roads and other heat-absorbing infrastructure, coupled with limited green spaces and inadequate ventilation in some neighbourhoods, could intensify temperatures in built-up areas,” he said.

Wahab warned that prolonged exposure to excessive heat could lead to dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke, with potentially serious consequences.

He identified children, older persons, pregnant women, outdoor workers, street traders, construction workers, waste handlers and people with underlying health conditions as particularly vulnerable.

The commissioner urged families, employers, schools and community leaders to pay special attention to these groups and ensure that protective measures were put in place.

He also cautioned that extreme heat could worsen air-quality challenges during the dry season, when dust and haze increase respiratory irritation.

He added that increased reliance on petrol and diesel-powered generators during power interruptions could further worsen local air pollution.

Wahab urged residents to avoid open burning of refuse and adopt environmentally responsible practices.

He advised residents to drink sufficient water regularly, wear lightweight and breathable clothing, seek shade and well-ventilated spaces, and reduce strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest periods of the day.

He also encouraged schools, markets, workplaces and other public facilities to provide adequate ventilation, access to drinking water and shaded areas.

The commissioner urged residents to watch out for warning signs of heat-related illnesses, including excessive sweating, dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea and muscle cramps.

“Anyone experiencing these symptoms should be moved to a cooler environment, given appropriate cooling assistance and taken for medical attention where necessary.

“Sudden collapse or loss of consciousness should be treated as medical emergencies requiring immediate attention.

“Residents with respiratory conditions are also advised to limit exposure to dusty environments and follow relevant health and air-quality advisories,” he said.

Wahab stressed that preparedness must go beyond individual precautions, calling for stronger collaboration among government agencies, environmental experts, health institutions, businesses and community stakeholders.

He urged residents and businesses to support efforts to reduce urban heat by protecting existing trees, promoting tree planting, preserving green spaces, ensuring proper waste disposal and discouraging environmental degradation.

The commissioner said environmental sustainability and climate resilience required collective responsibility, particularly as Lagos continued to address the impacts of climate change and rapid urbanisation.

He assured residents that the ministry, through its relevant agencies, would continue to engage stakeholders and promote public awareness.

He added that the ministry would work with the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), Lagos State Ministry of Health and Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) to strengthen preparedness and response.

World.title: Imo NYSC Members’ Kidnap: Bus Driver, Witness Identify Five Suspects Arrested by DSS
World.content:
The driver of the bus conveying the 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) kidnapped in Imo State on Independence Day has identified five suspects arrested by the Department of State Services (DSS) as the persons who allegedly attacked the bus and abducted the passengers.

Another prosecution witness, Mr Light Timothy, also told the Imo State High Court that he saw two of the five suspects wielding AK-47 rifles shortly after the abduction along the Owerri–Mgbidi–Onitsha Expressway.

The witnesses gave their testimonies on Friday at the resumed trial of the five suspected kidnappers.

Both witnesses maintained during their evidence-in-chief and cross-examination that they saw the defendants allegedly commit the offences of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of arms.

The bus driver, who testified as the third prosecution witness, told the court that he could clearly identify the first defendant as the person who initially approached his bus on the day of the attack, clutching an AK-47 rifle.

He also told the court that the first defendant was the person he saw marching the 20 prospective corps members into a nearby bush after taking them hostage.

In his testimony, Timothy said that, aside from sighting the first and second defendants after the abduction, he also identified both men as those who attacked the bus during an identification parade conducted at the DSS state office.

During cross-examination, defence counsel requested the bus driver’s identity card.

The trial judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, confirmed that the colour photograph on the identity card presented by the driver looked very much like him.

Thereafter, the testimonies of both witnesses, alongside the driver’s identity card, were admitted in evidence.

Justice Orafu adjourned the trial to November 3, 4, 5 and 6, 2026, for continuation of hearing.

World.title: Okpella Monarch Unveils Support for Small-Scale Business Owners, Free Electricity for the Elderly
World.content:
The Okuokpellagbe of Okpella, Edo State, King Michael Olorunfemi Sado, has unveiled an initiative aimed at providing monthly financial support for small-scale business owners in the community, in a move designed to stimulate local economic activities, strengthen livelihoods and promote grassroots development.

The monarch, who made the disclosure in a video currently circulating on social media, said the initiative was conceived to help small businesses thrive while extending support to elderly residents who may be struggling to meet their daily needs.

According to him, the intervention is part of a broader effort to improve the welfare of residents and create an enabling environment for economic activities to flourish in Okpella.

In the viral video, the traditional ruler explained that the proposed initiative would provide regular financial assistance to small-scale business operators, with the objective of helping them sustain and grow their businesses.

He said: “We have designed an initiative that will give monthly support to small-scale businesses, as the initiative is designed to make businesses in Okpella thrive.”

The monarch further disclosed that consideration had also been given to elderly men and women in the community, particularly those who may no longer have the strength to engage in strenuous activities or travel long distances in search of basic necessities.

“I have also thought about how the old men and women can benefit from this initiative in Okpella. So therefore, through this initiative, we have come to the conclusion that Okpella will no longer pay light bills starting from now,” he declared.

The announcement of free electricity, alongside the proposed monthly financial support for small businesses, has attracted considerable attention on social media, with the video generating reactions from residents and other viewers.

The initiative, as outlined by the monarch, places economic empowerment and social welfare at the centre of his development agenda for the community.

For small-scale business owners, regular financial support could provide an opportunity to improve their operations, replenish stock, meet essential business expenses and explore ways of expanding their enterprises.

Similarly, the proposed electricity intervention could offer relief to households and businesses by reducing the burden of electricity bills, although details regarding its implementation, coverage and commencement are yet to be provided in the publicly circulated video.

King Sado has been widely praised by the people for what they described as efforts to accelerate development in Okpella since ascending the throne.

Within his first year, the monarch has been associated with efforts to improve basic amenities and infrastructure in the community, including road construction projects undertaken through the palace initiative.

World.title: Cyberstalking: Doris Ogala Kneels Before Judge, Apologises for Outburst, Remains in Custody
World.content:
Court reserves ruling on actress’s bail application till November 6; defence counsel faults prosecution

Wale Igbintade

Nollywood actress, Doris Ogala, yesterday knelt before a Federal High Court in Lagos to apologise for her unruly conduct during an earlier sitting but was returned to the Kirikiri Correctional Centre after the court reserved ruling on her bail application till November 6, 2026.

Ogala, who is facing charges bordering on alleged cyberstalking, cyberbullying and attempted extortion involving Pastor Chris Okafor, expressed remorse before Justice Akintayo Aluko, promising not to repeat the conduct that disrupted proceedings on Wednesday.

Her apology came as her counsel, Marshal Abubakar, announced plans to petition the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, seeking the withdrawal of the charges, which he described as arising from a private disagreement between former lovers.

During Friday’s proceedings, Ogala personally appealed to Justice Aluko for forgiveness, expressing regret over her behaviour at the previous sitting.

“I am very sorry, my Lord. I apologise for my bad behaviour. I have never been to prison before and I wasn’t expecting that I would do that,” she told the court.

She added: “I regret my action and I apologise to my Lord. I tender my apologies wholeheartedly. Sorry, this will never happen again going forward.”

Her apology followed the judge’s expression of displeasure over the incident, during which the actress allegedly shouted and sang in the courtroom, forcing the court to suspend proceedings.

Justice Aluko said her conduct prevented the court from hearing more than seven other cases scheduled for that day.

The judge disclosed that he had considered committing her for contempt but eventually decided against it, despite believing that her conduct warranted punishment.

“She should have been given some form of imprisonment, right, on that day, but I kept my cool and I rose,” the judge said.

He further observed that the actress could have faced at least two months’ imprisonment for obstructing court proceedings.

Justice Aluko also faulted the defence counsel for failing to acknowledge the incident and explain his client’s conduct before proceeding with arguments on the bail application.

He recalled that he had personally directed an accelerated hearing of the application, taking steps to ensure that it was heard within 48 hours.

The judge expressed disappointment that the disruption occurred despite the court’s efforts to expedite the determination of the bail application.

Abubakar also apologised to the judge, describing the incident as regrettable and assuring the court that such behaviour was inconsistent with his client’s character.

Following the apologies, the court proceeded to hear arguments on the bail application.

Moving the application, Abubakar urged the court to admit Ogala to bail, arguing that the prosecution had effectively acknowledged her entitlement to bail by proposing conditions for her release in its counter-affidavit.

He submitted that the prosecution’s position indicated that it was not opposed to her release but was concerned about the conditions to be imposed.

The lawyer urged the court to exercise its discretion judicially and impose reasonable conditions that would not unnecessarily restrict the actress’s liberty pending trial.

However, prosecution counsel, Tolulope Mokolu, urged the court to impose stringent bail conditions, citing concerns about the defendant’s social media activities and their potential impact on witnesses.

Mokolu argued that Ogala’s continued use of social media could influence witnesses and interfere with the administration of justice.

Although acknowledging her constitutional right to freedom of speech and expression, the prosecution maintained that such rights were not absolute and must be exercised within the limits of the law.

It urged the court to restrict her contact with witnesses and access to their addresses, as well as prevent her from making social media publications capable of influencing witnesses or undermining the proceedings.

The prosecution further argued that any breach of the proposed bail conditions should attract appropriate sanctions.

After listening to the submissions of both parties, Justice Aluko reserved ruling on the bail application till November 6, 2026.

Ogala was subsequently returned to the Kirikiri Correctional Centre pending the court’s decision.

Speaking after the proceedings, Abubakar faulted the prosecution of his client, arguing that her arrest, investigation and subsequent arraignment constituted an infringement of her fundamental rights, particularly her constitutionally guaranteed right to freedom of expression.

He insisted that the dispute should not have been brought before a criminal court, maintaining that allegations of defamation should ordinarily be addressed through civil proceedings.

The lawyer argued that the disagreement arose from a private relationship between Ogala and Pastor Okafor, whom he described as former lovers.

He said: “I strongly believe that the arrest of Doris Ogala, the investigation as far as this matter is concerned, and the subsequent filing of charges against her are an affront to her fundamental rights.

“The subject matter that led to this entire transaction in this matter was purely a matter between a boyfriend and a girlfriend. Where former lovers who fell apart, and one of the lovers felt cheated, and she reacted through the platform that she has.”

Abubakar argued that the state should not ordinarily intervene in private disagreements by deploying criminal law against individuals expressing their grievances.

According to him, democracy accommodates dissent and criticism, including expressions that may be considered offensive or vulgar.

“The idea of criminalising free speech in this country has been contemptuous. We will never shy away from condemning the idea behind having a law that seeks to, or has, a chilling effect on Nigerians as it relates to how they should express themselves in a democracy,” he said.

The defence counsel also called for the removal of provisions of the Cybercrimes Act which, according to him, criminalise freedom of expression.

He recalled that legal challenges were instituted against provisions of the Cybercrimes Act 2015, particularly Section 24, in 2022.

He said two separate judgments had declared the provisions unconstitutional on grounds that they violated the right to freedom of expression and the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights.

He alleged that despite the National Assembly’s subsequent amendment of the Act in 2024 to address concerns surrounding the criminalisation of free speech, security agencies had continued to apply the law without adequately reflecting the amendments.

Abubakar maintained that anyone who considered himself defamed should institute a civil action rather than resort to law enforcement agencies to arrest and prosecute critics.

He said he would formally petition the AGF to discontinue the prosecution, insisting that the charges ought not to have been filed in the first place.

Ogala was arraigned on Wednesday by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation on three counts bordering on alleged cyberbullying, cyberstalking and attempted extortion involving Pastor Okafor.

According to the prosecution, the alleged offences were committed between September 2024 and March 2026.

Mokolu told the court that Ogala allegedly published nude and intimate photographs of Okafor on her social media accounts without his consent, exposing him to embarrassment, emotional distress and reputational damage.

The actress, however, pleaded not guilty to the charges.

World.title: APC Youth Stakeholders Back Dayo Israel, Warn Against Undermining His Office
World.content:
Folalumi Alaran in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress (APC) National Young Stakeholders Forum has passed a vote of confidence on the party’s National Youth Leader, Hon. Dayo Israel, warning against attempts to undermine his office or create parallel centres of influence within the party.

The forum also defended Israel’s facilitation of campaign mobilization vehicles for selected youth leaders, describing the initiative as part of efforts to improve the reward system within the party’s youth wing ahead of the 2027 general election.

The forum stated this in a press conference addressed by its National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Shehu Attah, at the Progressive Institute, Garki, Abuja, on Thursday.

It expressed concern over what it described as persistent attempts by some vested interests to weaken the party’s national youth structure for personal and other considerations.

The forum, comprising young stakeholders and founding members of the APC across the six geopolitical zones, said the party’s strength depended not only on electoral victories but also on respect for established institutions, internal democracy, fairness and the rule of law.

It commended Israel for establishing the APC Youth House and Nest Resource Centre, which it said had pioneered digital skills development, capacity building and vocational training, alongside town hall meetings and empowerment programmes.

The forum also highlighted the Renewed Hope Conversations initiative launched in tertiary institutions, describing it as a platform for bridging the gap between the Federal Government and young Nigerians by bringing students, policymakers and senior government officials together to discuss government policies and obtain feedback.

According to the forum, more than 100 party youths and some youth leaders across the country have benefited from overseas capacity-building and training programmes over the past two years.

It said the programmes were among efforts to address demands for an improved reward system within the party’s youth wing.

The forum further commended Israel for facilitating campaign mobilisation vehicles for selected youth leaders and distributing buses to others, saying the initiatives would encourage young party members to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

“This has sent a strong signal within the youth wing that the era of ‘monkey dey work, baboon dey chop’ is gone with the wind,” the statement said.

The forum warned that attempts to weaken the office of the National Youth Leader through factional manoeuvres or personal power struggles would be resisted.

It urged aggrieved party members to channel their complaints through appropriate party authorities rather than engage in actions capable of provoking tensions or deepening divisions.

The forum acknowledged that disagreements and competing interests were normal in a large political organisation such as the APC but maintained that such differences should be resolved through established procedures.

It called on APC youths nationwide to close ranks behind Israel and focus on mobilizing support for Tinubu’s re-election rather than engaging in internal disputes.

World.title: At Umrah, Tinubu Prays For Sustainable Peace, National Unity, Stability And Harmony In Nigeria
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Friday morning performed Umrah in the holy city of Makkah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, offering prayers of gratitude to Almighty Allah and seeking His continued guidance and protection for Nigeria.

During the spiritual exercise, the president circled the Holy Ka’abah at the Grand Mosque, Masjid al-Haram, in worship, devotion, and thanksgiving to Almighty Allah for His blessings on Nigeria and her people.

Fielding questions from newsmen shortly after the spiritual exercise, Tinubu said: “I believe this Umrah is very significant for the love of our people, commitment to the job and our country, Nigeria; commitment to the will of Allah that His words must prevail, and that there’s no other God but Him and He’s the only one that makes a human being what he can be and what he would be in life.”

He prayed for sustainable peace, national unity, harmony and stability in Nigeria, asking Almighty Allah to guide the country’s leaders with wisdom, strengthen the bonds of brotherhood among Nigerians, and grant the nation lasting relief from insecurity and other challenges.

“I am grateful to Allah for being able to perform this Umrah. We have just prayed for our nation, for everyone to live in peace and harmony, happiness and faith in God Almighty,” the president said.

He expressed hope that Nigeria would continue to make progress towards economic prosperity, social development, and a more secure future for all its citizens.

Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to building a peaceful, united, and prosperous nation where every Nigerian, regardless of faith or background, can live in safety, dignity and harmony.

The president also called for sustained commitment and collective efforts towards nation-building, emphasising the need for Nigerians to harness the country’s diversity as a source of strength in advancing national development, peace and security.

He stressed the importance of drawing on the nation’s collective strengths and shared aspirations to build a more secure and prosperous country.

“Our strength is our diversity, and we continue to build on that for the prospect and security of the country,” the president stated.

Tinubu also reflected on the spiritual significance of the pilgrimage, saying: “And we are giving it to our minds and our spirits in every way possible.”

On the president’s entourage during the Umrah were top government officials including Governors of Niger, Mohammed Umaru Bago; Bauchi, Bala Mohammed; Katsina, Dikko Umaru Radda; and Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, among others.

Tinubu had arrived Saudi Arabia Thursday night via the King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah, where he was received by Nigeria’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and Saudi Arabia’s Head of Royal Protocol, Ahmad bin Thafir.

His visit to Makkah is devoted to performing the religious rites associated with Umrah and offering prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability and continued progress.

President Tinubu is expected to return to Nigeria next week following the completion of the spiritual exercise.

World.title: 2027: Adeleke Inuagurates Campaign Committee for Sen. Oyewumi’s Re-election
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has inaugurated the campaign committee for the re-election of the Osun West Senatorial District lawmaker, Senator Lere Oyewumi.

The governor, represented by his deputy, Prince Kola Adewusi, described Oyewumi, who is the Deputy Minority Leader of the Senate, as a responsible lawmaker who has made the administration and the state proud through quality representation.

He charged members of the newly inaugurated committee to work with total loyalty and commitment to secure victory for the party.

The governor said, “Senator Oyewumi is a responsible person and we are proud of what he is doing in Osun West. We are calling on our people to re-elect him come January 16, 2027.

“I want to appeal to the members of the campaign committee to work hard and ensure the victory of Senator Lere Oyewumi. There is nothing like 99.9 percent loyalty. Your loyalty should be 100 percent.”

In his acceptance remarks, Senator Oyewumi thanked Governor Adeleke for his leadership, which he said has made campaigning easy for Accord candidates.

The lawmaker said, “Adeleke is a pathfinder, and his re-election has shown that Osun people love him, and that love will translate to victory for all Accord Party candidates in the general election.

“In my three and a half years in the red chamber, I have learned a lot. What I thought was not possible has been proven to me to be possible. So I am more prepared, more equipped and more determined to give my best to every community in Osun West Senatorial District.”

Oyewumi also promised to consolidate on his achievements, stating, “For the people of Osun West, more development is coming – better roads, improved schools and hospitals, clean water, and solar streetlights that will light up every corner of the district.

“When I contested in 2023, I didn’t have money to give anybody, both in my primary and general elections, yet they voted for me overwhelmingly. That is one encouragement that is pushing me to ensure I do not disappoint them.

“Our students will get more empowerment. We will not forget our artisans, market women, farmers and the elderly.”

Earlier, the Director General of the campaign committee, Adesoye Oyetunde, said the senator has not disappointed his constituents.

He said, “Oyewumi has not disappointed us. Out of the 10 local governments we have in this senatorial district, the Senator tarred roads in eight of them. In the remaining two, he has already flagged off construction.

“There is no local government in Osun West where Oyewumi has not built classrooms. In terms of healthcare, farm inputs and other interventions, the Senator has done a lot for his people, and I know he will do more.”

World.title: Enugu LG Chairmen Pledge Support for Mbah’s Devt Agenda
World.content:
The 17 Local Government Area chairmen in Enugu State have pledged their support for Governor Peter Mbah’s development agenda, describing his administration’s achievements in education, healthcare, infrastructure and economic growth as significant milestones.

The Chairman of Igboeze South Local Government Area, Honourable Ugo Ferdinand Ukwueze, stated this while reacting to the governor’s presentation of his administration’s mid-term performance update on its manifesto and social contract with the people.

Ukwueze said the achievements demonstrated the administration’s commitment to transforming Enugu State through innovation, strategic investments and improved service delivery.

He identified the construction of 268 Smart Green Schools and 260 Type Two Primary Healthcare Centres across the state’s wards as major interventions aimed at strengthening education and healthcare delivery.

The council chairman also commended the recruitment of 2,250 health personnel to improve access to medical services and support round-the-clock operations at primary healthcare facilities.

He noted that the establishment of advanced diagnostic services, including MRI, CT scans and mammography, would help reduce medical tourism and position Enugu as a destination for specialised healthcare.

On economic development, Ukwueze cited the revitalisation of United Palm Products Limited, the return of Sunrise Flour Mills to full operation through a public-private partnership, and investments in aviation, agriculture, energy and animal husbandry as initiatives expected to create jobs and boost the state’s economy.

He also highlighted ongoing tourism projects, including the development of the Nsude Pyramid, Ovu Lake Resort, Akpofu lakeside development and Akwuke Beach Resort, saying the initiatives would strengthen the state’s tourism potential and attract investments.

On the development of the state’s coal resources, the chairman said the proposed energy projects could open new opportunities for industrial growth.

Addressing concerns over taxation, Ukwueze urged residents to disregard what he described as misleading narratives about the introduction of new taxes.

He explained that the government was harmonising statutory charges and implementing reforms to address multiple taxation.

According to him, the state government has pledged to publish the harmonised charges for public scrutiny, while small businesses would benefit from measures designed to simplify tax administration.

The chairman also pointed to the reported increase in the state’s internally generated revenue from N25 billion to N400 billion, describing it as evidence of improved revenue mobilisation.

He called on residents to sustain their support for the governor’s development programmes, stressing that the success of the administration’s agenda required collective responsibility.

Speaking on behalf of his colleagues, Ukwueze said the 17 council chairmen had adopted the governor’s manifesto as a shared social contract, with measurable performance indicators to guide implementation at the grassroots.

He added that local government councils, in line with their constitutional responsibilities, would work with the state government to deepen development, improve service delivery and strengthen Enugu’s position as an investment destination.

The event was attended by political leaders, religious and traditional institutions, private-sector representatives and other stakeholders, who also expressed support for Mbah’s administration.

World.title: Tinubu Writes Senate, Seeks Confirmation Of Six Executive Directors For NMDPRA
World.content:
* Okays appointment of Jumoke Gafar as board secretary/legal adviser



Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has nominated six executive directors for the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).

Presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, in a release issued on Friday, disclosed that the president has forwarded a letter to the Senate for the confirmation of the six executive director-nominees.

Three nominees are being reappointed, while three are new and once the Senate approves them, all nominees will serve a five-year term.

The renominated executive directors are Mr Abiodun Adeniji, Executive Director, Finance and Accounts; Mr Ogbugo Kalu Ukoha, Executive Director, Distribution Systems, Storage and Retailing Infrastructure; and Dr Mustapha Lamorde, Executive Director, Health, Safety, Environment and Community.

The new executive directors are: Mr Mobolaji Tajudeen Musa, Executive Director, Hydrocarbon Processing Plants, Installations and Transportation Infrastructure; Ms Ogechukwu Modie, Executive Director, Economic Regulations and Strategic Planning; and Mr Said Abutalib, Executive Director, Corporate Services and Administration.

The president urged the Senate to consider the nominations expeditiously to ensure institutional continuity and strengthen the Authority’s oversight capacity.

Tinubu also approved the appointment of Mrs Jumoke Gafar as Secretary to the Board/Authority and Legal Adviser, subject to completing the statutory processes under Section 46 of the PIA.

In April, the president had appointed Rabiu Abdullahi Umar as the agency’s chief executive.

World.title: UWC commits to flying Pride Flag
World.content:
The University of Western Cape (UWC) has committed to flying its Pride Flag, which it claims represents inclusion, equity and social justice.

The institution is also celebrating the first anniversary of an LGBTIQA forum led by staff.

UWC PROUDLY FLYS PRIDE FLAG

On its social media platforms, UWC shared its pride in flying the LGBTQ+ Pride Flag, which represents different parts of the community.



“It serves as a visible reminder of the University’s ongoing commitment to inclusion, equity and social justice”, the university shared.

The university shared that the flag also marked another significant milestone: the first anniversary of Queer Dubs, a staff-led forum that has hosted discussions affecting the LGBTQ community, on issues related to gender, sexuality and social justice.

“The Pride Flag remains an important symbol of that work. More than a marker of visibility, it represents the ongoing pursuit of a university community grounded in respect, accountability and inclusion. It serves as a reminder that creating equitable spaces requires continual engagement and collective effort”, the university said of its stance.

BISHOPS BACKLASH

Unlike UWC, another Cape Town learning institution, Bishops Diocesan College has come under fire for flying the Pride Flag.

The Cape Town all-boys school has made headlines after members of the Old Diocesan Committee (ODC) called for their alma mater to take a “neutral” stance.

In recent months, actor and comedian Anton Taylor, an alumnus, challenged a committee of Old Boys who have rejected the school’s decision to fly a Pride flag for just two days in the year, during Pride month in June.



Despite being served with a cease-and-desist letter from the ODC after his public criticism, Taylor responded that he would not be silenced.

World.title: Leon Schuster shares health update: ‘One more fall and I could die’
World.content:
Leon Schuster has given an update on his health. Images via Facebook

Leon Schuster has given the public an update on his deteriorating health, which he blames on a taxing career as a filmmaker and actor.

The beloved South African comedian is working on a new movie, set to be released via Netflix.

LEON SCHUSTER TALKS HEALTH

Speaking to SABC’s Leanne Manas, Leon Schuster reflected on his longstanding film career, for which he has received numerous accolades.



He also spoke about his ailing physical and mental health.

He said: “At least 70% of my health problems got to do with the fact that I worked too hard in my life – I made 17 moves and 30 CDs

“I made movie after move, and I got clapped and moered, and I fell back on my back, and I don’t care because I was young and was fit.

Schuster – who revealed that he once played rugby for the Free State – shared that he now suffered from chronic neck pain and was in dire need of a hip replacement and another back surgery

He added: “Young people…you can take risks with money. That’s a different story. But don’t take risks with your body, which I did.

“I can’t take those claps anymore. One fall on my back and I can die.



“I’ve got to be wheels around the airport, because if I stand up for too long I get severe pain”.

NEW MOVIE LOADING

Appearing on the studio at KwaZulu-Natal digital radio station PlayZN last month, Leon Schuster said he was in Durban to work on the screenplay for an upcoming production.

When pressed for details, the beloved TV actor said, “I’m writing a movie now. We’ve got a contract from Netflix. It’s a very difficult movie, but I pitched the idea, and they liked it”

Referring to his ailing physical health, he continued: “I’m going to play it 50% in the wheelchair, because I can’t walk far with my back.

Schuster’s last movie was Mr Bones 3, released in 2024, during which he injured his back.

He revealed his new movie would also see him take on a character similar to his own personality

World.title: Which Kruger National Park camps have swimming pools?
World.content:
With summer approaching, visitors heading to Kruger National Park may be looking for more than just wildlife sightings.

After spending hours in a safari vehicle in the Lowveld heat, a swimming pool can be a welcome way to cool off, particularly for families travelling with children.

SANParks currently lists swimming pools at 11 Kruger camps, although one of those pools, at Punda Maria, is currently unavailable because of renovation work. Skukuza has two pools.



Which Kruger camps have swimming pools?

Kruger camp Swimming pool Berg-en-Dal Yes Letaba Yes Lower Sabie Yes Mopani Yes Olifants Yes Orpen Yes Pretoriuskop Yes Punda Maria Currently unavailable – renovations Satara Yes Shingwedzi Yes Skukuza Yes – two pools

Skukuza stands out from the other main camps because it has two swimming pools.

This can make it particularly attractive to families and visitors planning a longer stay, especially during the hot summer months.

Skukuza is also one of Kruger’s largest and best-equipped camps, with restaurants, shops and other facilities, making it a convenient base for visitors who want to combine game drives with some downtime.

Can day visitors use the Kruger swimming pools?

Generally, the swimming pools at the camps are intended for camp residents.

However, SANParks says there are additional swimming pools available to day visitors at the Skukuza and Letaba Day Visitor Areas.

This means visitors spending the day in Kruger National Park do have options for cooling off, but they should not assume that every camp pool is available to day visitors.



Which Kruger camps are best if you want a pool?

For families, Skukuza is an obvious option because it has two pools and extensive facilities.

Berg-en-Dal is another good choice, with a swimming pool for overnight residents as well as restaurants, a shop and other facilities.

Mopani also has a swimming pool alongside a restaurant, shop, filling station and other facilities.

For visitors exploring the central and northern parts of the park, Letaba, Olifants, Mopani and Shingwedzi provide options for combining game viewing with a swim.

Kruger National Park’s summer months can be hot, with visitors spending much of the day in vehicles while searching for wildlife.

A swimming pool gives visitors a chance to take a break from the heat between game drives. It can be especially useful for families with children, who may not want to spend an entire day in a safari vehicle.

That makes a pool worth considering when choosing accommodation, particularly if you are planning to spend several nights at the same camp.

However, visitors should remember that swimming pools are an extra facility rather than a substitute for following the park’s safety rules. Wildlife is still present around the camps, and visitors should remain within designated areas.

World.title: The Kiffness: ‘I lost money, my life was threatened’
World.content:
The Kiffness has spoken about his decision to step away from his X account after receiving death threats over his controversial views.

The Cape Town musician – real name David Scott – is known for his quirky sampled songs as well as bold views on topics like politics, race and religion.

THE KIFFNESS ON LEAVING X, RECEIVING DEATH THREATS

In an interview with News Day, The Kiffness spoke about gaining international recognition for his songs, sampling animal sounds and silly viral moments.



He also delved into making headlines over his controversial views.

Over the past year, the Durban-born artist, who lives in Cape Town, deactivated his X account over his controversial views, which many labelled “racist” and “Islamophobic”.

The artist mentioned his comments about the Middle East conflict, which led to a call to boycott his concert at Kirstenbosch Gardens in Cape Town last December.



He said: “They were all coming after me because I have a reasonable belief that a nation like Israel has a right to exist and defend itself from terrorists. I also believe that someone like [Gift of the Givers CEO] Dr [Imtiaz] Soliman, who is supposed to be a humanitarian, shouldn’t be going on stage and using violent rhetoric and saying things that are political when you are supposed to be a non-aligned NGO”.

The Kiffness shared that he had received numerous death threats, referencing the assassination of US conservative Charlie Kirk. He was also losing brand deals due to the backlash of his views.

For the first time, the 38-year-old had to hire private security to protect him.



He continued: “I lost money; my life was being threatened.

“You’re allowed to disagree with me. But if you start threatening my family and me, that’s when the line gets crossed.

“There was a point where I thought that this show isn’t actually worth it. There’s a very real possibility that someone could take me out. That’s the reality of the world we live in, where being outspoken comes wth a massive cost. But I’m going to keep doing it because we need to speak the truth.



“I’m just someone who cares about the truth, regardless of the consequences.

The Kiffness added that fatherhood – with another little one on the way – had put things into perspective for him.

“I want my kids to grow up with their dad, but the reality is the whistleblowers and truth-speakers are unfortunately taken out a lot of the time. 

“I walk this tightrope where we need to be bold and not be intimidated by those who intimidate us.

“The truth is the biggest disinfectant. It can shine a light on the rot in society and in these organisations that are trying to silence voices like mine. The more emboldened other people will become, the more they’ll lose their foothold. We can’t let them intimidate us”.

‘TRIED TO CANCEL ME’

Last month, The Kiffness publicly supported UK musician Ed Sheeran, who has come under fire for his decision not to “pick sides” in the Israel-Palestine conflict.



Sheeran tearfully apologised for his previous “complicit”, apolitical views, calling the conflict “unjustifiable”.

In a Facebook post, The Kiffness shared that he had related to the backlash on a personal and professional level.

Tagging the UK singer, he shared: “Dear Ed Sheeran. I’m not sure if you’ll ever see this, but I wanted to send some encouragement your way. Last year, a small but very vocal group of Pro-Palestine activists tried to cancel me, too, but they failed. The online noise and intimidation tactics were intense, and there were definitely moments I wondered if doing the show I was booked for was worth it, but I’m glad I followed through.



He continued: “Please don’t let them win. You’re an incredible talent and a genuinely good person. When I faced backlash, I at least expected it because I’ve been vocal about my Christian views in the past. It’s so much more unfair that you’re receiving this hate simply for choosing to stay out of it and mind your own business.

“You have a massive amount of support behind you. Don’t let the noise bring you down!”

World.title: Saturday tide times: When will the sea rise and fall along SA’s coast?
World.content:
High and low tide times for South Africa’s coastal cities on Saturday. Image: Pexels

If you’re heading to the coast on Saturday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Water levels change throughout the day, while wind, waves, swell and the shape of the seabed also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

When will high and low tides occur on Saturday?

According to the South African Weather Service, spring tides bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.



These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing along the coast. Higher tides may cover rocks and reefs, while lower tides expose more of the shoreline.

Beachgoers, anglers and other coastal visitors should check tide times and sea conditions before heading out.

Beachgoers should also watch out for:

Strong currents: Rip currents can pull swimmers away from the shore, even when the sea looks calm.

Rip currents can pull swimmers away from the shore, even when the sea looks calm. Unexpected waves: Larger waves can catch people off guard, particularly near rocks and tidal pools.

Larger waves can catch people off guard, particularly near rocks and tidal pools. Rising water levels: The incoming tide can quickly reduce the amount of beach available for walking or fishing.

The incoming tide can quickly reduce the amount of beach available for walking or fishing. Slippery rocks: Wet rocks and exposed reefs can make walking along the shoreline dangerous.

Check the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Andre Estherhuizen gives peek at dream beach home
World.content:
Andre Esterhuizen is building his dream house. Images via IG

Springbok Andre Esterhuizen has given the public a look at his dream home, being built in the coastal resort village of Umdloti in KwaZulu-Natal.

The 32-year-old, his wife Mabea and three children live in the province, where he plays for the Sharks.

The rugby player has recently made headlines over a news report of a racial slur he made at the age of 18 years old.



ANDRE ESTERHUIZEN SHARES PEEK OF DREAM HOME

On his social media platforms, Andre Esterhuizen showed off a peek at his dream family mansion being built on the Salta Sibaya Estate in Udloti.

In a video clip, the property was seen being excavated before the foundation was likely put in.

“Start of a chapter: A new home for our family”, he shared.



Andre also shared a 3D visualisation of what the home would look like both on the exterior and interior. The picture-perfect home featured plenty of palm trees and a stunning view of the beach.

IS DURBAN HIS FOREVER HOME?

In 2013, Andre Esterhuizen moved to Durban at the age of 19 years old, to pursue a career with the Sharks.

During 2020–2024, Andrew played for the Harlequins in the UK.

He returned to KwaZulu-Natal, where he remains under contract until 2030.

World.title: Rooibos plant seeds on course for launch into space
World.content:
In a few months' time, seeds from the rooibos plant will head to the International Space Station for experimentation. Images via Canva @Mizina/@Ablestock.com

South Africans know that rooibos tea is simply out of this world – and in a few months’ time, this will become a literal reality.

For the first time in history, more than 17 000 rooibos plant seeds will be flown to the International Space Station (ISS) for scientific experimentation.

ROOIBOS: FROM SA TO NASA

As part of the South African Rooibos Council’s (SARC’s) “Rooibos in Space” initiative – in collaboration with MaxIQ Space – a total of 17 346 rooibos seeds will be flown to the ISS located over 400 kilometres above Earth’s surface.



According to IOL, the seeds will be transported to Voyager Technologies in Texas. Here, the seeds will be prepped for spaceflight and subsequently placed within a compact laboratory module known as a Nanolab.

The Nanolab will then be placed aboard the Cygnus NG-25 commercial resupply spacecraft. Originally, the launch was slated for an October launch. As of writing, the spacecraft is set to launch between December 2026 and January 2027 following a change in the Voyager/NASA flight schedule.

PURPOSE OF EXPERIMENTS

Rooibos is the pride and joy of South African culture. The tea made from this indigenous plant is chock-full of anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, plus it’s caffeine-free.



Now, rooibos will serve an important role in space science. Thanks to the Nanolab’s compact nature, researchers aboard the ISS will be able to carry out experiments on the seeds. This includes exposing them to microgravity and space radiation.

Because the seeds are divided into three groups – untreated seeds, scarified seeds, and seeds that have been scarified and treated with a protective agricultural coating – the researchers can examine the contrast between each group’s performances.

Researchers aboard the ISS can examine the contrast between each seed group’s performances. Image: Pexels

After four-to-six weeks, says the SARC, the seeds will return to Earth – specifically, returning to Mzansi. Back on home soil, they will be planted alongside a group of control seeds. This will form part of “a comparative study examining germination, growth, resilience and yield.”



“The experiment will be carried out by learners from seven schools in the Cederberg region – the birthplace of Rooibos. Working with local rooibos farms, learners will collect and analyse data as part of a structured scientific investigation. A parallel experiment at Parklands College will provide additional comparative data.”

ROOIBOS: A NEW FRONTIER

The implications of this groundbreaking initiative are great. It gives us an opportunity to learn more about the rooibos plant’s capabilities. What’s more, it will also push the boundaries of science.

“Rooibos has long been part of South Africa’s agricultural heritage,” says Dawie de Villiers, SARC director. “This project places it within a broader scientific context, where plant biology, space research and education intersect. It also reflects the importance of investing in scientific literacy and skills development for the next generation of researchers and innovators.”



Are you excited about South Africa’s unique foray into space travel? Let us know in the comments below!

World.title: Which Kruger National Park camps are best for families with children?
World.content:
Taking children to Kruger? These are the camps to consider. Image: wikimedia commons

A Kruger National Park holiday with children can be an unforgettable family adventure, but choosing the right rest camp can make the experience considerably easier.

While all of Kruger’s main rest camps offer access to the park’s wildlife and self-drive routes, some are better suited to families because of their facilities, location, swimming pools, restaurants and range of activities.

SANParks’ main rest camps generally offer facilities including shops, restaurants or cafeterias, braai facilities and swimming pools at selected camps.



Here are some of the Kruger camps worth considering for a family trip.

1. Skukuza

Skukuza is one of the most convenient choices for families visiting Kruger National Park for the first time.

It is the park’s largest rest camp and has a wide range of facilities, including restaurants, shops, a petrol station, laundry facilities and swimming pools.



Importantly for families, Skukuza has two swimming pools, giving children somewhere to cool off after a morning spent on a game drive.

The camp also has a day visitor area and is well positioned for exploring the southern part of the park.

Its location also makes it a practical base for families who want plenty of facilities without giving up the feeling of staying inside a national park.



2. Pretoriuskop

Pretoriuskop is another good option for families, particularly those entering through Numbi Gate.

The camp has a swimming pool as well as restaurant and shop facilities, making it possible to spend several days in the park without having to travel far for basic supplies.

Its relatively close proximity to the Numbi and Phabeni gates can also make it convenient for shorter family breaks.



3. Berg-en-Dal

Berg-en-Dal is particularly worth considering for families who want a combination of wildlife, facilities and activities.

The camp has a swimming pool for overnight residents, a restaurant, shop, filling station, laundromat and day visitor picnic area.

It also offers a seasonal Kids Educational Programme, which can give younger visitors an opportunity to learn more about the park and its wildlife.



The camp is also known for its rhino sightings, making the surrounding area particularly interesting for young wildlife enthusiasts.

4. Lower Sabie

Lower Sabie is a good choice for families who want a scenic camp with plenty of wildlife-viewing opportunities.

The camp has a swimming pool, restaurant, shop and other facilities, while its position overlooking the Sabie River gives visitors a chance to watch wildlife from around the camp.



The swimming pool can be particularly useful during hot weather when children need a break from the car and the midday heat.

5. Satara

Satara is one of the most popular camps for visitors interested in seeing big cats and other plains game.

For families, it also has the practical facilities needed for a longer stay, including a swimming pool, restaurant, shop, filling station and laundry facilities.



Its location in an area known for open grassland can make game viewing relatively rewarding, particularly for visitors hoping to spot lions.

6. Letaba

Letaba is another family-friendly option, particularly for visitors exploring the central and northern parts of Kruger National Park.

The camp has a swimming pool, restaurant, shop, filling station and other facilities.



It also has a major attraction for children and adults alike: the Letaba Elephant Hall, which focuses on elephants and their biology and history.

There is also a swimming pool available to day visitors at the Letaba Day Visitor Area, although overnight guests have access to the camp pool.

What should families look for when choosing a Kruger camp?

Families should consider more than just how close a camp is to the animals they want to see.



A swimming pool can make a major difference, particularly during the hotter months, while a restaurant and shop can make it easier to manage meals and forgotten essentials.
