It is also worth considering how far the camp is from the entrance gate and how much driving children will have to endure each day.

For families with younger children, a camp with plenty of facilities can be more practical than a remote bush camp.



SANParks says its bushveld camps are more remote and do not have shops or restaurants, making the larger main rest camps a more convenient option for many families.

World.title: Complaints upheld against Swiss TV commentary on Israeli bobsleigher
World.content:
BERN - Switzerland's broadcasting complaints authority announced Friday that a TV commentary questioning the legitimacy of an Israeli bobsleigher competing at the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics had breached discrimination rules.

The Independent Complaints Authority for Radio and Television (ICA) said it had upheld four complaints about the commentary on Swiss French-language public broadcaster RTS concerning Adam Edelman.

The commentator said Edelman's supportive comments of Israel's bombardment of the Gaza Strip, which has resulted in the deaths of over 70,000 people and the destruction of most of the Palestinian territory's infrastructure, should have resulted in him being barred from the Games.

Live as the Israeli team made its descent at the Olympics on February 16, the commentator on RTS2 "spent the entire run discussing statements made on social media" by Edelman, regarding the Gaza war, the ICA said.

The authority upheld the complaints by five votes to four.

"A majority of the members concluded that the commentary, which appeared to have been prepared in advance, suggested that the Israeli athlete should be excluded from the Olympic Games due to his political views," the ICA said in a statement.

"They found that this conveyed a stigmatising, and therefore discriminatory, message directed at him, in contrast to the 25 other athletes competing that day.

"The members determined that the sports commentator had subjected the Israeli athlete to unequal treatment, thereby violating the prohibition against discrimination."

The ICA will at a later date publish the written reasoning for its decision, detailing the measures it has requested.

Generally, when the ICA finds a breach of the rules, it directs the broadcaster to take "measures to prevent any further violations" and to subsequently report on the steps taken.

At the time, Edelman called the commentary a "diatribe" and said he gave it no credence whatsoever.

Israel's embassy in Switzerland said it was "deeply appalled by the blatant abuse" and demanded decisive action and a clear apology.

RTS has removed the sequence from its website.

The nine-member ICA rules on complaints against radio and television programmes, determining whether any violations of the relevant laws have been committed.

"This includes compliance with the requirements of appropriateness and diversity, observance of fundamental rights, protection of minorities and the prohibition of glorification or extenuation of violence," it says.

Appeals against ICA decisions can be lodged directly with Switzerland's Federal Supreme Court.

World.title: Competition Commission says Heineken in apparent breach of sale conditions
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Heineken Beverages is under pressure after the Competition Commission said it is in apparent breach of the conditions attached to a 2023 merger.

The owners of Strongbow cider said they have been disadvantaged by Heineken's efforts to push the Hunters and Savanna brands.

Heineken merged with local company Distell in 2023.

But the Competition Commission only approved the sale on condition that Heineken sell the licence to sell Strongbow to a black-owned firm called Cider House Investments.

That was to prevent all three cider brands - Hunters, Savannah and Strongbow - remaining under one company.

Cider House complained last year that Heineken broke the conditions of the deal by undermining Strongbow before the deal was completed.

It said this was due to the way Strongbow was priced, marketed and given limited access to retail fridge space.

World.title: Meta settles, leaving Snap sole defendant in new social media trial
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Meta reached a settlement in a landmark case over the alleged harms of social media, the plaintiffs’ lawyers said Friday, leaving Snap as the only defendant in a trial set to open in Los Angeles next week.

"We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client," Emily Jeffcott, a lawyer representing one of the young women suing both companies, said in a statement.

Jury selection began on Wednesday, and opening statements are scheduled for November 4.

The terms of the agreement are confidential, but sources close to Meta told AFP the company decided to settle for business reasons.

"Trials, dismissals and settlements are all common in the bellwether process, and this litigation is no exception," a Meta spokesperson said, referring to the series of test cases against the company being tried in Los Angeles.

If Snap does not settle, the trial will go ahead next week.

Snap did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

TikTok and YouTube were also named as defendants in the case, but both had already reached settlements with the plaintiffs, known by their initials SJ and KDB, their lawyers said.

Meta had also previously settled with SJ.

A California state judge consolidated the two cases into a single trial.

Snap, which makes Snapchat, will defend itself against the claims of both SJ and KDB.

Lawyers for SJ and KDB will argue that their clients were exposed to "addictive and problematic" social media apps when they started using them at ages 13 and 15, respectively, according to court documents.

"We believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs' experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed," a Snap spokesperson said in a statement earlier this week.

-Avoiding trial-

Thousands of lawsuits have been filed in recent years in local, state and federal courtrooms across the country with various claims about alleged harms to children and teenagers caused by social media companies.

The cases, the first of which went to trial earlier this year in Los Angeles, have taken twists and turns.

Meta and YouTube lost the first so-called bellwether case earlier this year, when a jury found them collectively liable for harming a young user known by the initials KGM, and ordered the tech companies to pay a combined $6 million penalty.

Snap and TikTok settled with KGM ahead of that trial.

Months later, Snap, TikTok and YouTube settled another case that was set to go to trial in August; that plaintiff, known as RKC, then withdrew their remaining claims against Meta, allowing the Instagram and Facebook maker to avoid trial without a settlement.

By settling before a trial kicks off, the social media companies contain costs from lawyer fees and potential penalties; another benefit is that it shields their executives from testifying in court.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Instagram chief Adam Mosseri were expected to be called as key witnesses in the upcoming Los Angeles trial.

Snap CEO Evan Spiegel is expected to testify if the trial proceeds without another settlement.

In August, Meta agreed to pay more than $18 billion in penalties, in addition to making changes to Instagram and Facebook for teens, when it settled with 52 attorneys general several days into a trial held in California.

That settlement came just a day after Mosseri testified, and before Zuckerberg had been called to the stand.

Meta has faced other trials, though.

Earlier this month, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in a case where the company was found liable for deceiving users in the state about how their data was used in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

A New Mexico jury also found the social media giant liable for harms to children, leading to a combined penalty of $942 million earlier this year.

By Sara Bloomberg

World.title: Tears, fear, anger: relatives of Spain train crash dead await fate
World.content:
URDA - Marisa Liebana could barely hold back her tears as she sought news about her nephew Francisco Jose, one of the 69 victims of this week's high-speed rail crash in Spain.

Francisco Jose, 32, worked in Madrid and had caught a train south to the region of Andalusia on Wednesday to spend a few days with his parents. He was never seen again.

"The outcome has been very tough and very sad," Marisa said in the central city of Toledo, which has received most of the bodies from the collision outside the village of Urda.

"He was in the prime of his life," added Marisa, who said she felt "powerless" as she accompanied her brother Cecilio outside a reception centre for the victims' relatives in Toledo.

Inside the building, Civil Guard officers confirmed the dreaded news that their nephew had been found dead.

"We are devastated," Cecilio said, echoing the sentiment of the dozens of families affected by one of Europe's deadliest train disasters this century.

His sister, Francisco Jose's mother, could not come to Toledo. "She is distraught. She is seeing psychologists, receiving treatment, and she's in a really bad way," explained Marisa.

- 'Frustrated, outraged' -

Forensics teams are working around the clock and have identified 12 bodies, but for many relatives the wait is proving unbearable.

Esther San Emeterio, who is waiting for news of her brother Pepe, said the "anxiety" her family was experiencing was "crossing a line".

"Last night I went to bed incredibly frustrated, outraged, ashamed that no one is telling us anything."

Javier Barrio, whose wife Carmen de Santana had caught the train as one of her final work-related trips before her retirement, said "we are doing what we can, crying."

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.

World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: Sakaja protests release of 14 suspects linked to Eastleigh collapsed building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has protested the release of suspects linked to the collapsed building in Eastleigh.

While pushing for the county to have prosecutorial powers, Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court.

Sakaja in statement posted on his X account (formerly Twitter) said City Hall had taken enforcement action against those involved after establishing change of user from a residential property to a commercial had been approved.

According to Sakaja, architectural plans required to authorise construction had not been approved.

The Governor said County officers arrested the suspects and handed them over to Kamukunji Police Station because county governments no longer hold prosecutorial powers they previously held.

“We enforced the law and arrested those involved. However, because we do not have prosecutorial powers, the suspects were handed over to Kamukunji Police Station. They were reportedly released on a cash bail of Sh50,000 without being taken to court,” Sakaja said.

“We want the police to explain why the suspects were released without being presented in court and why construction was allowed to continue. These are serious questions that must be answered,” he added.

A police occurrence book entry from Kamukunji Police Station indicates that 14 suspects were booked into custody on June 17, 2026, over the alleged offences relating to contravention of city planning laws.

Enforcement action and arrests were made severally by the county officials and most recently in July after failing to comply with the enforcement order below. However the suspects were released on a 50k bail at Kamukunji police on the very same day. Prosecution of the same was also denied. We have repeatedly asked for the resumption of the power to prosecute such violations of such county and county related laws after this was taken away from County governments in 2024 (one such letter to the office of the DPP is attached). Meanwhile, several such cases have either been rejected by prosecutors (who are independent of the County), dismissed by the justice system or have had minimal fines imposed. Fining a developer 50k for an illegal development with hundreds of millions without orders to stop and remove the offensive development is completely unreasonable. I raised this in the Senate a fortnight ago and we shall keep pushing for a review of this position. All of these instances, where enforcement action has been curtailed, blocked or interfered with, will be published to the public. October 25, 2026

The entry, recorded under OB No. 98/17/06/2026, names the suspects and states that they were booked by Nairobi City County officers before being placed in police cells.

A separate Kenya Police Service record indicates that 10 suspects were subsequently released on a cash bail of Sh50,000.

The entry, recorded at 9.44pm, states that the release was carried out on the instructions of the Officer Commanding Station (OCS), identified in the record as C.I. Onyapidi, through Corporal Awadh.

The record references receipt number 2039434 and states that the suspects left the station without complaints.

However, the documents do not, on their own, establish the specific charges against the suspects, the legal basis for the bail arrangement or whether they were subsequently presented in court.

The discrepancy between the 14 suspects recorded as booked into custody and the 10 named in the release entry also raises questions about the subsequent status of the other suspects. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Sakaja said a June 2025 enforcement notice adds another dimension to the questions surrounding the property and the enforcement of planning regulations.

The notice, issued by Nairobi City County over alleged construction works undertaken without the required development permission, cited the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019, and county by-laws.

It directed the recipient to stop the works and remove the development described as illegal, warning that the County could undertake the required action and recover the costs if the directives were not followed.

The notice also provided for an appeal to the County Physical and Land Use Planning Liaison Committee.

Sakaja clarified that approval to change a property’s use from private to commercial-cum-residential does not amount to approval of architectural plans authorising construction.

He said the County approved the change of use but did not approve the architectural plans, yet construction proceeded.

I have seen some people peddling a fake approval document alleging that the Eastleigh development was approved. It is telling that this is the same document that the Eastleigh developer used to get NCA approval. They allege that the development was approved in January of 2024. This is not true. The application for development as shown below was made in November of 2024, it could not have been approved in February of the same year. Also, there is a difference between a change of user approval and a development approval. The developer applied for change of use from residential to residential & commercial in August of 2024. Change of user was approved in October of 2024. Development approval has never been granted. The developer went on to build with impunity and without building approvals despite enforcement action by the county and arrests. — Sakaja Arthur Johnson (@SakajaJohnson) October 25, 2026

“If the building had been approved for construction, I would have named the officers who approved it so that action could be taken against them,” he said.

Sakaja, in his argument, said the current arrangement creates a gap between enforcement and prosecution, leaving counties dependent on other agencies after taking action against alleged offenders. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Under his proposal, appropriately authorised county prosecutors would be able to pursue qualifying county offences through the courts, subject to the law and the constitutional authority of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

He said county prosecutors previously had a better understanding of technical offences involving planning, construction and other county regulations, enabling them to handle such cases more directly.

“We want to be able not only to enforce regulations and make arrests, but also to take offenders to court and prosecute them. When counties had prosecutorial powers, we had prosecutors who understood the nature and seriousness of county offences and could ensure that appropriate legal action was taken,” he said.

World.title: Pregnant woman rescued from collapsed Eastleigh building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Red Cross workers after rescuing a man who trapped in the rubble.

A pregnant woman was on Saturday evening rescued from the multi-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi’s Eastleigh estate on Friday, October 23 and rushed to the Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) for treatment.

She is the second person to rescued as earlier in the afternoon the Kenya Red Cross society announced the rescue of a man from the ill-fated building.

The man was also taken to KNH for treatment with the society saying that the rescue followed hours of work put in by the search and rescue multi-agency team.

“After hours of painstaking work alongside multi-agency partners, our search and rescue teams in Eastleigh brought a trapped man out of the rubble,” said Red Cross.

The rescue comes even as the fate of six people who were reported missing on Friuday remains unknown with rescue teams still continuing with the search at the site of the collapsed building along Yusuf Haji Avenue.

The society said that 66 of the 67 construction workers who were at the site had been traced and accounted for but the search continues for people who may have been near the site of the collapsed building.

The development comes as police announced that they had launched a manhunt for the for the owner and contractor of a building.

Police spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said that officers had launched a probe in collaboration with relevant bodies to establish the cause of the collapse and determine criminal liability.

“Any individual or entity found culpable of negligence or of violating building regulations will face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement.

Nyaga called on members of public to stay completely clear of Yusuf Haji Avenue and 9th Street to give access to heavy excavators, specialised canine units and rescue personnel to perform their duties.

Earlier Saturday, at least 31 families reported their relatives missing as coordinated rescue efforts entered their second day.

No deaths have been reported so far.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) on Friday evening identified the developer, contractor, architect and structural engineer listed for the collapsed building.

The Authority has faced scrutiny over its oversight role, as Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja said the project had failed to comply with construction guidelines.

He said the county had forwarded relevant information to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations for further investigation.

In a statement, the NCA said the building was registered on July 30, 2025, as a proposed development on 9th Street in Eastleigh.

It identified 9th Street Plaza Limited as the developer and Stromax Holdings E.A. Limited as the contractor.

Emmanuel Mwangi Maina was listed as the project architect, while Joseph Muturi Mugu was named as the structural engineer.

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: An Arab political earthquake reshapes Israeli elections
World.content:
While both Benjamin Netanyahu and his political opposition claim victory following Israel’s latest elections, the immediate reality remains unresolved. Neither faction secured the 61-seat parliamentary majority needed to form a government, leaving Israeli politics at a complete standstill—unless the opposition and far-right enter a broad national unity coalition, a prospect rendered unlikely by deep ideological divides.

Instead, the true political shockwave came from inside the Arab electorate. Securing nearly 19 seats across two main blocs—the Joint List and Mansour Abbas’s United Arab List (Ra’am)—Arab parliamentarians now hold decisive leverage in Israel’s complex coalition math.

Historic turnout and political leverage

This historic parliamentary gain was driven by an unprecedented voter turnout among Arab citizens of Israel, which neared 80%. Galvanized by ongoing military operations in Gaza, escalating West Bank tensions, and systemic domestic discrimination, Arab voters turned out with a clear mandate: removing Netanyahu from power.

Mathematically, Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc falls well short of the governing threshold. If the Arab parliamentary factions maintain a unified stance without making early concessions, they hold the power to effectively end Netanyahu’s political tenure—possessing structural leverage that regional diplomatic efforts have struggled to achieve.

Coalition barriers and demands

Fearing this political reality, Netanyahu previously campaigned on the divisive slogan “The Right or Palestine,” warning that Arab voters would dictate Israel’s political future. Opposition figures, including Gadi Eisenkot, initially laid out rigid conditions for Arab support—demanding explicit recognition of Israel’s Jewish character, acceptance of mandatory military conscription for Palestinian citizens, and formal condemnation of resistance groups.

However, political realities have shifted the balance of power. To form a viable administration, opposition leaders cannot bypass Arab representatives:

The Joint list (holding 10+ seats): Maintains a principled position centered on Arab national identity, combating institutional discrimination, and advocating an immediate end to military operations in Gaza and the West Bank.

The United Arab list (Ra’am): Focuses primarily on pragmatic, civic-minded concessions—targeting socioeconomic improvements, infrastructure funding, and policing in Arab municipalities.

Strategic opportunity vs. political compromise

The surge in parliamentary representation offers Arab citizens of Israel a powerful platform to challenge discriminatory policies and assert political agency. However, maximizing this moment requires strategic discipline.

Settling for marginal budget increases for Arab towns while ignoring broader Palestinian political rights risks squandering an unprecedented opportunity. If Arab lawmakers leverage their position effectively—securing tangible policy shifts on domestic equality and regional peace—this election could mark a structural turning point in Arab political engagement within Israel.

Author’s bio

Abdel Allah Abdel Salam is the managing editor at Al-Ahram newspaper where he writes a daily column titled “New Horizon.”

He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Journalism from the Faculty of Mass Communication, Cairo University (1987).

He began his journalistic career at Al-Wafd newspaper, then moved to the Middle East News Agency before settling at Al-Ahram newspaper in June 1991. He founded the Al-Ahram electronic portal and served as its editor-in-chief from 2010 to 2013.

In 2013, he was the executive editor-in-chief of the Al-Masry Al-Youm website.

Salam also worked as managing editor of the Al Ain (UAE) portal in 2016, and managing editor of the “Al-Watan” (Egyptian) newspaper’s website in 2017.

World.title: When Arabs tracked the Israeli ballot box
World.content:
Across the Arab world, the recent Israeli elections were monitored with unusual intensity. Many tracked the returns minute by minute, almost expecting Tel Aviv’s ballot boxes to deliver what regional diplomacy and domestic governance have failed to achieve: a shift in hostile policies, the downfall of Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, or a viable opening for Palestinian statehood.

This collective fixation warrants reflection. Across the region, where civic spaces for political self-determination remain constrained to varying degrees, many found themselves placing misplaced hope on a democratic process unfolding within a hostile state—guided by voters who neither share Arab priorities nor support a just resolution for Palestinian rights.

Voter surge and the reality of power

Voter turnout reached approximately 77.7%—the highest level recorded since 1999—reflecting deep domestic polarization rather than a decisive political shift. While Netanyahu’s bloc secured a plurality, it fell short of a clear governing majority. Meanwhile, Arab-led parties scored notable gains, positioning their parliamentary bloc as a crucial factor in coalition negotiations amid the prospect of prolonged gridlock or yet another snap election.

High voter participation underscores a fundamental truth: Israeli citizens view their electoral process as a meaningful tool to shape governance, identity, and national security. For the broader region, the lesson is clear: democracy is built through institutional framework, political competition, and civic efficacy—the belief that an individual vote carries weight, even when outcomes diverge from personal preferences.

The limits of external expectations

Hopes that leadership changes in Israel will yield radical policy shifts towards Palestinians require a dose of geopolitical realism. Removing Netanyahu from office does not erase the broad internal consensus governing Israeli security and territorial policies. Even with increased parliamentary representation, Arab parties face structural barriers when attempting to leverage seats into policy influence within right-dominated coalitions.

Democracy, viewed externally, reveals its inherent limitations. While Israeli elections reflect the will of participating voters, they systematically exclude Palestinians living under occupation from exercising equal self-determination over their daily lives and political future.

Relying on external electoral outcomes is not a viable strategy. While tracking political shifts in neighboring states remains necessary, it must serve as a catalyst for internal reform rather than passive anticipation. External political shifts may open temporary diplomatic windows, but they cannot replace regional agency and institutional self-reliance.

World.title: Why the CBE raised interest rates by 1% amid currency pressures
World.content:
The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) defied market expectations on Thursday by raising its key interest rates by 100 basis points (1 percentage point), aiming to anchor inflationary expectations and mitigate escalating domestic and external economic pressures.

The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) increased the overnight deposit, overnight lending, and main operation rates to 20.0 percent, 21.0 percent, and 20.5 percent respectively. The credit and discount rate was also raised to 20.5 percent.

The surprise rate hike caught many bankers and analysts off guard, as market consensus had favored maintaining current rate levels.

Inflation threats and exchange rate pressures

Speaking to Al-Masry Al-Youm, banking expert Hany Aboul Fotouh explained that the decision reflects heightened concerns over persistent inflationary risks and shifting global macroeconomic dynamics.

“Global interest rate trajectories—particularly decisions by the US Federal Reserve and major central banks—remain a critical variable for Egyptian monetary policy,” Aboul Fotouh noted, emphasizing the CBE’s push to preserve the appeal of local debt instruments and mitigate hot money outflows.

Aboul Fotouh pointed to the US dollar approaching EGP 56 in local banking channels as a key catalyst. The currency pressure poses immediate cost-push inflation risks for imported food commodities and essential production inputs.

Geopolitical uncertainties and supply chains

Escalating regional geopolitical tensions have further compounded market uncertainty, heightening risks of disruption across global energy markets, trade corridors, and supply chains.

The central bank reiterated that the tighter monetary stance aims to counter pass-through effects from rising food and energy costs, safeguarding domestic purchasing power amidst an unfavorable global economic environment.

World.title: Police Scotland Probe alleged human trafficking involving Jeffrey Epstein and former Prince Andrew at Royal estate
World.content:
Police Scotland have opened an investigation into a 1999 visit by convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and Andrew, brother of King Charles III, to the Balmoral royal estate in Scotland, following allegations of human trafficking involving women transported to the residence.

Scottish law enforcement confirmed receiving information regarding the stay of Epstein, Andrew, and Epstein’s associate Ghislaine Maxwell at the royal castle, adding that inquiries remain in their early stages.

Royal estate visit under scrutiny

Epstein visited Balmoral Castle in 1999 upon the invitation of Andrew, who held the title of Prince Andrew at the time.

Photographs released as part of US Department of Justice filings show Epstein and Maxwell relaxing inside Glen Beg lodge on the estate grounds, alongside images showing Andrew and Epstein participating in a shooting trip in the area. British media outlets report that the new probe specifically addresses suspicions of sex trafficking involving women brought to the Highland retreat.

A Police Scotland spokesperson stated that all investigations remain evidence-based and centered on survivor needs, declining to provide further details regarding active inquiries.

The National Police Chiefs’ Council (NPCC) confirmed that several UK forces—including Thames Valley Police, London’s Metropolitan Police, and Surrey Police—are actively investigating leads stemming from the unsealed “Epstein Files.”

Historical context and legal fallout

Balmoral Castle, acquired privately by Queen Victoria in 1852, serves as a traditional summer residence for the British Royal Family and was the site of Queen Elizabeth II’s death in September 2022.

The former Duke of York was stripped of his royal titles by King Charles III following further disclosures regarding his ties to Epstein. In February, Andrew was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office over allegations of sharing sensitive information with Epstein during his tenure as a UK trade envoy. He was questioned under oath and released under investigation, maintaining a denial of all wrongdoing.

Unsealed email disclosures include a message sent from Balmoral in August 2001, signed “A,” asking Maxwell whether she had located any “inappropriate friends” for him.

World.title: EgyptAir expands UK presence with 4 weekly direct flights between Cairo and Birmingham
World.content:
Flag carrier EgyptAir has officially launched non-stop service between Cairo International Airport and Birmingham Airport, expanding its footprint in the United Kingdom as part of its newly inaugurated winter schedule.

Operating four times weekly—on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Fridays, and Sundays—the route utilizes the carrier’s modern Boeing 737 MAX 8 fleet. The addition makes Birmingham EgyptAir’s third UK destination, joining established daily operations to London Heathrow and Manchester.

Strategic bridge to the Midlands

The new connection serves two primary strategic goals: unlocking direct travel for the substantial Egyptian diaspora residing across the West Midlands, and serving Birmingham’s role as a major UK economic and industrial center.

By linking central England directly to Cairo, the route facilitates seamless one-stop connections across EgyptAir’s broader network spanning Africa, the Middle East, and Asia.

According to airline leadership, the expansion addresses rising commercial and leisure travel demand between Egypt and the UK, while offering regional UK passengers an efficient transit alternative through Cairo’s international hub.

World.title: 19 countries welcome Egyptian passport holders without prior visas
World.content:
Egyptian passport holders can travel to dozens of global destinations without securing a visa prior to departure, though entry conditions, stay durations, and electronic travel authorizations vary across regions.

According to passport indexing data cited by Reach Immigration, the Egyptian passport currently ranks 93rd globally, offering visa-free or visa-on-arrival entry to 52 destinations worldwide. Among these, 19 countries allow visa-free entry, while 33 offer visas on arrival or electronic travel authorizations upon landing.

Full list of destinations

Egyptian passport holders can enter the following destinations either visa-free or via visa-on-arrival/e-Visa arrangements:

Albania, Benin, Burundi, Bolivia, Burkina Faso, Cambodia, Cape Verde, Comoros, Cook Islands, Dominica, Ecuador, Gambia, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Haiti, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Iran, Jordan, Laos, Lebanon, Macao (SAR China), Madagascar, Malaysia, Maldives, Marshall Islands, Mauritania, Mauritius, Micronesia, Mozambique, Nepal, Nicaragua, Nigeria, Niue, Palau, Rwanda, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Samoa, Senegal, Seychelles, Somalia, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Timor-Leste, Togo, Tuvalu, Uganda, Yemen, and Zimbabwe.

World.title: Israel’s election will inevitably impact Gaza for Palestinians who have no vote
World.content:
Palestinians in Gaza had no vote in Israel’s election. But its outcome will shape their future.

More than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since the Hamas-led October 7 attacks of 2023, with Israeli strikes a near daily occurrence, despite a nominal ceasefire agreed a year ago. Meanwhile, the humanitarian catastrophe continues to deepen, with severe food shortages, widespread displacement, and collapsing basic infrastructure.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition and his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, both centered their election pitches on ending Hamas rule there.

But for many in the enclave, who wins the election is moot. Here’s what three people in central Gaza told CNN.

Ahed Ferwana: “The programs announced by the Israeli parties — whether parties of Netanyahu’s camp or parties of the opposition — all agree that there will not be an independent Palestinian state. They will not withdraw from the Gaza Strip and will continue military campaigns both in the Strip and even in the West Bank, as is currently seen in the city of Hebron.

“Therefore, these elections are not expected to produce significant results in favor of the Palestinian cause, especially since Eisenkot recently said frankly that he might return to war on the Gaza Strip because there is no quicker option, as he puts it. … As for Netanyahu’s camp … it has been committed to the war for more than three years.”

Musa Ubeid: “I do not count on the right, nor the left, nor anyone in Israel, because they consider our children terrorists, so how can we want or count on any party? They are two sides of the same coin.”

Tareq Abu Eweimeh: “Trump and Netanyahu have one policy, which is wars and their continuation and bloodshed. Therefore their goals are united and they are walking on one path.”

World.title: It’s getting no better for Trump one week from midterms
World.content:
The United States may be within a week of momentous political change in midterm elections that could destroy the Republican Party’s monopoly on Washington and hand Democrats power to check President Donald Trump.

But take a beat.

It’s far too early to size up any Democratic wave. There’s no guarantee there’ll even be one in an election season characterized by political volatility, redrawn districts, a gusher of outside cash — including hundreds of millions of dollars of GOP funding from Elon Musk — and ambiguity over who will turn up to vote.

Pundits may be increasingly bullish that Democrats will give Republicans a shellacking.

But at this point, what is the purpose of speculating?

More than 31 million early votes are already banked. And after years of apprehension over American democracy, voters will take part in a noble biennial ritual next Tuesday to deliver the only verdict that matters.

What conventional wisdom expects

Still, almost everyone involved in politics expects Democrats to erase the Republican majority and win back the House, in a classic rebuke to a sitting president who seems to have forgotten he promised to cut the cost of living on the 2024 campaign trail.

But given Trump’s past triumphs, Democrats would be foolish to take a big night for granted. And the wrinkles of the US political system mean that polls showing a wide Democratic lead on the generic congressional ballot might translate into a more equivocal result than expected.

The 10 or so races that will meanwhile decide the Senate’s destiny are mostly neck-and-neck. This means Democrats could run close in all of them but still miss most of their targets. Disengaged GOP voters might also respond to Trump’s appeals for one last rodeo and turn out in higher-than-expected numbers.

And Democrats are trying to do something spectacular and rare on what was long considered a prohibitive Senate map this cycle. They need an unlikely winning streak through solid GOP territory to find the net gain of four seats needed for the majority.

But there are certain signs that may bode ill for the GOP.

President Donald Trump throws a hat to the audience as he takes the stage during a campaign rally at Crossroads Arena on October 26 in Corinth, Mississippi. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images

Many Republican lawmakers suddenly find themselves in closer races than they expected. And Trump’s campaign blitz is mostly focused on red America as he tries to rescue them. On Monday, for example, he held a rally in Mississippi, where he won by 23 points two years ago. Now, incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith is facing an unexpectedly strong Democratic challenge.

“You know, I’m here because Cindy’s doing great, but I just got to make sure. I can’t take a chance,” Trump said.

None of this proves that Democrats are poised for a victory lap. But it explains why Republicans, with one week to go, seem to be building a last line of defense.

The administration also seems to be preparing contingency plans. Its preemptive legal maneuvers in Alaska and California could foreshadow possible voting challenges. And they recall the president’s previous bid, in 2020, to deny voters’ right to choose their leaders after an election he lost.

There is one, however, undeniable indicator amid all the uncertainty: The gruesome political environment for Republicans only two years after Trump’s stunning comeback is not abating. If anything, it’s worsening by the day.

Voters are desperate for relief from high prices for groceries, gasoline and housing and still haven’t got the answers Trump promised in 2024. And with his war in Iran and his tariffs, the president seems to have handed voters a tangible demonstration that his decisions are making the cost of living crisis worse.

His bizarre antics are hardly helping. If an unpopular president had set out to design a strategy to hurt his own side, it might look little different from Trump’s approach. The billionaire in chief keeps insisting that the country is basking in a historic economic golden age. With gasoline averaging more than $4 a gallon, he celebrated oil company profits on Sunday.

And instead of empathizing with tight family budgets, he waxes on about trivialities at his increasingly out-of-touch rallies — like his new obsession with the rear ends of Ohio Sen. Jon Husted and rapper Nicki Minaj.

What we know

Election forecasters are almost universally predicting that Democrats will take the House of Representatives, despite polls showing they’ve yet to win back public trust. That would mean an onslaught of investigation against Trump and senior administration figures — and almost certainly two years of performative showdowns and legislative gridlock in Washington.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries speaks to the press on the steps of the US Capitol on September 30, in Washington, DC. Finn Gomez/Getty Images

Hakeem Jeffries, the probable speaker in any Democratic majority, was sufficiently confident last week to tell CNN’s Manu Raju that his party is “very likely” to regain control, saying that the “environment is clearly on our side.” Indeed, it would be a stunning surprise and a departure from history if the GOP clings on to a majority that has barely functioned in recent months. Incumbent presidents almost always get a bloody nose in midterm elections, and Trump’s approval ratings are particularly low.

Still, even as Democrats target more Republican seats, years of gerrymandering and the uncertainties introduced by Trump’s redistricting campaign this year mean that of the House’s 435 seats, perhaps only four dozen or so are considered truly competitive, even with a political storm lining up for the GOP.

So Democrats could pile up millions more votes but only win by a few seats.

The Senate is a toss-up.

Insiders in both parties think North Carolina may already effectively be in the Democratic column. And former Ohio Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown is well-positioned to return to Washington. If networks make an early call for Democrats in a state where Trump romped home by 11 points two years ago, the rout could become reality.

Democrats also think they can unseat Alaska Sen. Dan Sullivan. But then the road to a majority quickly gets bumpy. Republican Sen. Susan Collins, for instance, is threatening another act of political escapology in Maine.

And it’s measure of an extraordinary political year and the mountain that Democrats must climb that a CNN analysis last week deemed Texas — which last elected a Democratic senator in 1988 — the fifth most likely seat to change hands. Democratic nominee James Talarico has emerged as a rare political talent, and Trump did him a favor by muscling scandal-plagued state Attorney General Ken Paxton through the Republican primary. But the mirage of a statewide Democratic victory in the Lone Star sate has shimmered before. No one will believe it until it happens.

A true blue wave might bring Trump-country seats in Kansas and Iowa within reach for Democrats. And even in South Carolina, Sen. Darline Graham can’t be certain of keeping the seat she inherited from late brother Lindsey Graham.

But Democrats have their own worries. Their Senate dreams may be dashed if Michigan nominee Abdul El-Sayed fails to win a margin-of-error race to retain retiring Sen. Gary Peters’ seat in a contest that is testing the progressive movement’s potential in a purple state.

An attendee holds a ripped “47” sign during a campaign event with former US President Donald Trump, not pictured, in Greensboro, North Carolina, on October 22, 2024. Cornell Watson/Bloomberg/Getty Images

What we don’t know

All year, there have been signs that Trump’s 2024 is coalition is splintering. Multiple polls show he’s alienated Latino voters, who helped put him back in the White House, with high prices and a ferocious immigration purge. Polls now show that Democrats have reversed Trump’s gains among younger voters two years ago.

The limited insight that can be gained from early voting statistics also looks favorable for Democrats. The party’s voters seem more enthusiastic than their GOP counterparts in Texas, for example. CNN reported Tuesday that returns suggest turnout among the youngest Republican voters in Georgia, Iowa and North Carolina is well behind 2024. In several key states, Democrats make up a larger share of early voters than at the this point two years ago. All this is encouraging for the party. But Democrats could still fall short of Election Day expectations.

Conservative media is clinging to the hope that polls are underestimating Republican turnout, as has been the case several times in the Trump era. The president is beseeching GOP voters to pretend he’s on the ballot — even though Democrats also want a referendum on an unpopular president.

There’s one other possibility: that this time, pollsters might have failed to fully capture Democratic turnout. That’s how a potential narrow win could become a landslide.

What on earth is Trump up to?

Trump has always been a singular political figure. But if his unorthodox midterm strategy saves his party, he’ll have busted expectations yet again.

The president’s repeated attempts to spring an October surprise, however, seem to be failing. There’s no sign that his promise of $5,000 for every American adult if the GOP wins is changing the race — or that voters take it that seriously. His sanctions-busting diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin put the US on the side of a ruthless tyrant with Ukraine’s blood on his hands, and may have done more political harm than good.

And the president has dived into the deepest gutter in politics by warning that El-Sayed, a Muslim, supports “terrorists” and would need to “go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate.” The president also backed an ad put out by Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy that cast doubt on alleged childhood abuse suffered by his opponent, Amy Acton.

President Donald Trump arrives to speak at a midterm election campaign rally at Sioux Gateway Airport in Sioux City, Iowa, on October 22. Kent Nishimura/AFP/Getty Images

In 2016, this kind of searing MAGA rhetoric helped Trump to shatter the playbook. But Trump has always been more effective in elections as an insurgent planning a shakeup than an incumbent judged on his record.

Now, he just seems oblivious to the nation’s sour mood.

Most people think they know what’s going to happen.

But until next week, no one can know for sure.

This headline has been updated.

World.title: Final Verdict: Swiss Supreme Court Upholds Alieu Kosiah’s 20-Year Sentence for Lofa War Crimes
World.content:
Court clears ex-ULIMO commander of crimes against humanity but leaves sentence intact

Monrovia – Former ULIMO commander Alieu Kosiah will serve the full 20 years in prison for atrocities committed in Lofa County during Liberia’s civil war, after Switzerland’s Federal Supreme Court upheld his war crimes conviction in a ruling made public Friday.

By Rodney Sieh



The decision makes final the first war crimes conviction ever handed down by a Swiss civilian court. It is also the first conviction anywhere of a Liberian for war crimes committed during the country’s two civil wars, which ran from 1989 to 2003 and killed an estimated 250,000 people.

Kosiah was found guilty of crimes committed in Lofa between 1993 and 1995, including killing civilians and ordering their killing, rape, using a child soldier, ordering pillage, cruel treatment of civilians, and desecrating the body of a dead civilian through an act of cannibalism.

The Appeals Chamber of Switzerland’s Federal Criminal Court had found that those crimes alone would justify 150 years in prison. The sentence was reduced to 20 years, the maximum allowed under Swiss law.

Crimes Against Humanity Charge Thrown Out

In a partial win for the defense, the Supreme Court acquitted Kosiah of crimes against humanity, a conviction the Appeals Chamber added in 2023. The court ruled that the crimes against humanity provision, which entered Swiss law in 2011, cannot be applied to acts committed between 1993 and 1995.

The acquittal does not affect his 20-year sentence or his expulsion from Switzerland once he has served it.

Lawyers for the victims welcomed the final conviction but criticized the acquittal.

“Today the survivors of Alieu Kosiah’s crimes have final justice, more than 30 years after they suffered and twelve years after his arrest,” said Alain Werner, Director of Civitas Maxima, the Geneva-based group that represents victims in the case. “When this case began, it was often their word against his, about events during a brutal and traumatic civil war. Today Switzerland’s highest court has confirmed that they were believed.”

Werner said his team was “deeply disappointed” by the acquittal, arguing that civilians in Lofa were deliberately targeted — killed, raped, looted and forced to carry loads for fighters — in a widespread and systematic attack.

“What happened in Lofa between 1993 and 1995 is the very definition of a crime against humanity,” he said.

Twelve Years in Detention

Kosiah settled in Switzerland in the late 1990s and was arrested in November 2014 after Liberian victims filed a criminal complaint through their lawyers. He has been in detention ever since.

Survivors traveled from Liberia to testify against him during the investigation and at both of his trials.

The case was built with the help of the Global Justice and Research Project (GJRP), a Liberian organization that has documented civil war crimes for more than a decade. Together, Civitas Maxima and GJRP have contributed to six criminal trials in four countries linked to Liberia’s civil wars, resulting in five convictions.

‘Our People Should Not Have to Keep Looking to Europe’

The ruling once again throws a spotlight on Liberia’s failure to try its own war criminals. More than two decades after the war ended, no war crimes trial has been held on Liberian soil. Armed groups recruited more than 21,000 children during the conflict.

Liberia has committed to establishing a War and Economic Crimes Court, but the court has yet to hear a case.

GJRP Director Hassan Bility thanked Swiss authorities for more than ten years of commitment that allowed Liberian survivors to take part directly in the trials, but said justice should be delivered at home.

“These crimes were committed in Liberia by a Liberian against Liberians, and the judgment was delivered thousands of miles away,” Bility said. “Our people should not have to keep looking to Europe or the United States for justice. It is more than time for these trials to take place in Liberia, and for the War and Economic Crimes Court to start its work.”

[OPTIONAL: Reaction from the War and Economic Crimes Court office, the Ministry of Justice, or Lofa County residents/lawmakers.]

World.title: Liberia: Bong County’s New Road Machines Could Open the Way from Farm to Market, Says EPA Boss Yarkpawolo
World.content:
GBARNGA, Bong County – The arrival of 30 pieces of heavy earthmoving equipment in Bong County is being greeted as a turning point for the county’s farmers, traders and rural families. The head of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) says the machines could turn isolation into opportunity.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

Dr. Emmanuel King Urey Yarkpawolo, the EPA Executive Director and a son of Zota District, said the yellow machines carry meaning far beyond the construction work they are expected to do. In his view, passable roads sit at the heart of food security, farm income and the daily survival of rural households.



In a statement marking the arrival, Dr. Yarkpawolo commended President Joseph Nyuma Boakai for placing roads at the center of his administration’s agenda. He argued that the initiative could begin to ease transportation problems that have long held back farming and trade in Bong, one of the country’s most important agricultural counties.

He leaned on a saying the President is known for: that people cannot eat a road, yet a road is what allows people to eat. “People do not eat road, but it is road that can make people eat,” he recalled. According to the EPA chief, the line captures what farmers across rural Liberia live with every season.

Farmers in Bong, he explained, put months of labor and money into growing rice, cassava, vegetables and plantains. But the work does not end at harvest. Getting crops out of the village and into a market is often the harder part, and where roads have deteriorated, that journey can fail altogether.

The rainy season makes matters worse. Mud, washed-out surfaces and damaged crossings can cut off whole farming settlements, leaving vehicles unable to reach them. Produce waiting by the roadside may rot before a buyer ever sees it, and the farmer absorbs the loss. “A farmer can grow rice, cassava, vegetables, and plantains, but without a reliable road to the market, that harvest may spoil before it can be sold,” he said.

The damage, Dr. Yarkpawolo noted, does not stop with the farmer. Market women struggle to get supplies, traders lose business, and families in towns and cities pay more because the cost of hauling food over bad roads gets passed along at the market stall.

That is why, he said, agriculture and infrastructure should not be treated as two separate items on the government’s to-do list. “A road connects the hands that grow our food to the households that need it,” he stated. He added that it also lets farmers earn the money to feed, educate and uplift their children.

Roads, he stressed, are also lifelines to schools and clinics. Children in remote communities can find it hard to reach the classroom, and patients needing urgent care may not reach a hospital in time when the only route is barely passable. More dependable roads throughout the year, he said, would ease those burdens. “Beyond food, better roads can help children reach school, patients reach hospitals, and businesses reach new customers,” he said.

His comments come amid an ongoing national conversation about road development and economic recovery, especially in rural counties where farming remains a main source of work and income. In Bong, many households rely on farming and small-scale trading to get by, and weak road links have historically made it harder to move goods and reach basic services.

Dr. Yarkpawolo believes sustained rehabilitation of rural roads could open doors for residents who have waited years. Farmers who can move crops quickly and cheaply stand a better chance of earning enough to enlarge their farms, buy inputs and improve conditions at home.

Traders would gain too. With better roads, he said, they could reach more villages, buy directly from producers and carry goods to bigger markets. Stronger ties between farmers and city consumers could also help bring down some of the transport costs that keep market prices high.

For Zota District and other rural parts of Bong, the stakes are personal.

“Today, as Bong County’s yellow machines arrive home, I welcome them with pride as a son of Bong,” he declared. He said the machines offer farmers, market women and cut-off communities a chance to turn isolation into access and hard work into income.

Yet the EPA chief was clear that delivery is not the same as results. He warned that the arrival of equipment does not fulfill the government’s responsibility, and called for practical steps to keep the machines running and ensure they produce measurable benefits.

Maintenance, he said, must be a priority. Without disciplined management and steady attention to servicing and operating needs, the machines’ usefulness will fade.

He also urged fairness in deployment, insisting that communities facing the toughest travel problems should get a real share of the benefit.

“Their arrival must now translate into results. We must maintain the machines, deploy them fairly, and ensure they serve the communities that need them,” he said.

Dr. Yarkpawolo said the program should not be judged by the number of machines parked in Bong, but by what changes on the ground. “Their true value will be measured in roads made passable, travel made easier, and livelihoods improved,” he said. Road work, in his words, must deliver tangible gains: easier movement, better market access and more earning opportunities for rural households.

World.title: Liberia: Ex-Mayor Jefferson Koijee Hands Over Disputed Sinkor Property to VP Koung, Vows Political Fight Continues
World.content:
The former mayor, who served under the administration of ex-President George Manneh Weah, used the statement to renew allegations of political persecution against the administration of President Joseph Nyuma Boakai and Vice President Koung.

Former Monrovia City Mayor Jefferson T. Koijee says handing over the 19th Street premises does not amount to surrender or an admission of guilt, accusing the Boakai-Koung administration of political persecution while declaring 2029 as his political destination.

Former Monrovia City Mayor Jefferson T. Koijee says he has officially handed over a disputed property on 19th Street, Coleman Avenue, in Sinkor, to Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung following an intervention by his spiritual adviser, Pastor Philemon A. Tarpeh.

In a public statement, Koijee said the decision was driven by his faith and commitment to peace, insisting that relinquishing the premises should not be interpreted as an admission of wrongdoing or a retreat from his political struggle.



“I have chosen peace. My faith remains unshaken. 2029 is our destination,” Koijee declared, signaling his intention to remain politically active ahead of the next presidential election.

The former mayor, who served under the administration of ex-President George Manneh Weah, used the statement to renew allegations of political persecution against the administration of President Joseph Nyuma Boakai and Vice President Koung.

At the center of his argument is the ownership dispute surrounding the Sinkor property.

Koijee recalled that on September 18, 2018, then Managing Director of the Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation, Mo Ali, publicly alleged that he had acquired a house valued at US$250,000 in less than nine months.

According to Koijee, the allegation followed him for years and was repeatedly used to portray him as corrupt.

However, he said a writ of summons issued by the Monrovia City Magisterial Court on October 13, 2026, identifies Vice President Koung as claiming the same property.

He questioned how the property could have been attributed to him in 2018 but is now being claimed by the Vice President.

“So which lie were they telling then, and which lie are they telling now?” Koijee asked, challenging the government to explain the circumstances surrounding the competing claims.

He said the Boakai-Koung administration owes the Liberian public an explanation, although the competing ownership claims and the legal status of the property remain matters requiring clarification through the appropriate legal process.

Koijee also revisited the international sanctions announced against him on December 8, 2023, saying his political opponents celebrated the development as the end of his political career.

He claimed that the sanctions resulted in repeated visa denials and other restrictions but credited Pastor Tarpeh’s prayers and spiritual support for helping him overcome the difficulties.

“The man they buried is still standing,” he said, invoking biblical passages to reinforce his message of resilience and faith.

The former mayor further rejected allegations linking him to criminal activities, including murder, accusing the current administration of using state institutions and public platforms to tarnish his reputation.

Koijee argued that despite nearly three years of accusations, authorities had failed to prove the allegations against him in court.

“They called me a criminal. They called me a murderer,” he said. “For almost three years the Boakai-Koung regime has controlled the police, the prosecutors, and the microphones, and not one case has been proven against me.”

He challenged the government to produce evidence supporting the allegations, including financial records and properties allegedly linked to him.

However, his claims about the absence of proven cases do not, on their own, establish that all allegations against him are unfounded. The specific status of any investigations or proceedings would need to be established through official records.

In defending his public service record, Koijee cited his tenure as Monrovia City Mayor, arguing that he prioritized public service over personal comfort.

He said he continued using an official vehicle purchased by his predecessor rather than requesting a new one, adding that he nearly lost his life in an accident involving the same vehicle on June 16, 2018.

Koijee maintained that throughout his six years as mayor, he never purchased a new official vehicle for himself and challenged critics to verify the claim through records at City Hall.

He also directed questions at Chairman George Sylvester Mulbah, demanding clarification over his alleged relationship with the Office of the Vice President.

“Seven statements, and still no answer. Are you employed in the Office of Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung? Yes or no?” Koijee asked.

He did not provide further details about the seven statements referenced in his challenge.

Despite handing over the disputed premises, Koijee said he would continue advocating for what he described as constitutional governance, independent courts and equal justice.

He framed the property handover as a decision to avoid confrontation rather than a withdrawal from the political arena.

“They can take a property, but they cannot take my voice, my faith, or the people’s hunger for change,” he declared.

Koijee concluded by reaffirming his political ambition ahead of the 2029 elections, describing the next presidential contest as the destination of his ongoing political struggle.

“I have handed over the premises. I have not handed over the truth,” he said.

The property dispute, the circumstances surrounding its handover and the competing claims of ownership are likely to remain subjects of public interest as the political exchanges between the former mayor and the current administration continue.
