World.title: Tourism Minister Welcomes Advent Price Caps Across Croatia
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – Tourism Minister Tonči Glavina has stated that he more than welcomes advent price caps announced across Croatia, hoping for higher winter visitor figures.

The tourism minister stated that ” for any Advent to be successful, its most important component in terms of the structure of guests, in terms of revenue, in terms of hospitality and so on, is precisely domestic consumption,”

Index reports that he added that this type of consumption depends most on the citizens who live in the municipalities and cities that organise Advent fairs. He recalled that Poreč, Pula and Split have introduced price limitations for part of the Advent offer. He pointed out that the Split model provides for the determination of part of the prices already in the public call that regulates the relations between the city and the tenants of the Advent stalls. At the same time, prices are limited only for a smaller part of the hospitality offer.

“In this way, they’ve very clearly ensured the conditions that Advent and the hospitality offer at Advent are absolutely accessible to everyone,” Glavina said.

split caps its advent prices for the first time ever

It’s worth noting that this year, Split has introduced limitations on the prices of part of the food and drinks at Advent stalls for the very first time. According to the public call published by the city company Žnjan, a portion of fritule of at least 150 grams may cost a maximum of four euros, while a hot dog and sausage of at least 80 grams may cost a maximum of three euros. Mulled wine and hot chocolate, in a quantity of at least two decilitres, may cost a maximum of three euros. For the same quantity of tea hospitality providers will be able to charge a maximum of €2.50, while half a litre of water must not be more expensive than two euros.

The limitations apply to the seven listed products, and not to the entire offer. A novelty is also that the City of Split will for the first time, when selecting tenants, score the quality of their hospitality offer, and not only the offered rent. This year’s Advent in Split will last from the 27th of November to the 6th of January, and Advent stalls will be set up on the Riva, Prokurative, in Đardin and Stobreč.

pula also caps its advent prices

A similar decision was made by Pula, where fritule, pancakes and Christmas cookies may cost a maximum of three euros per portion. For mulled wine, hot chocolate and cocoa the maximum price will be three euros, and for a hot dog, hamburger and bakalar five euros. Tea and water will be able to cost a maximum of two euros. Nevertheless, the limitations do not mean that all products at Pula’s Advent stalls will have prescribed prices. Hospitality providers will have to offer at least one product at a limited price, depending on the type of offer, while they will be able to determine the prices of other products independently.

Such a model has already been applied for years in Poreč, and things will be no different throughout the upcoming festive period, either.

Glavina emphasised that Advent as a tourist product is very important for the development of year-round tourism and tourist results in the months of December and January. He stressed that this year the Croatian National Tourist Board is for the first time conducting a national campaign with all key domestic Advent destinations, directed towards the main markets from which tourists come to Croatia.

“We’re making that transition towards year-round tourism and it is very important for us to have good content and programmes, and I am sure, because of the good prices, that the number of visitors at Advent will perhaps be higher than ever before,” he concluded.

World.title: Advent in Split Caps Prices Ahead of Christmas Festivities
World.content:
October the 30th, 2026 – Advent in Split has capped the prices of what it will sell during the upcoming Christmas festivities.

Ahead of the Christmas period and the different advent celebrations across Croatia, a new trend among local politicians is limiting prices for hospitality providers. The new city that has joined the wave is Split. Split hospitality providers who can apply for the tender for Advent stalls have been met with a limitation on the prices of food and drinks.

Poslovni reports that this new wave of price capping appeared after ever-increasing prices at Advent events across Croatia often caused dissatisfaction among visitors and locals alike. Split has therefore become the third city overall that has decided to introduce an upper limit on the prices of certain products. A hot-dog sold at Advent in Split will now cost a maximum of three euros, which is two euros less than up in Pula, which has also limited its own advent prices this year. Mulled wine in both of these cities will be available for a maximum of three euros, while fritule sold in Split will still be one euro more expensive than in Pula.

Poreč has otherwise been applying this model of price limitation for several years. The general public’s opinions on prices at festive events up and down Croatia are divided. While some believe that the offer often does not justify the amounts they have to pay, others point out that the entire Christmas period is an opportunity to enjoy the festive atmosphere, which is why prices are not always their primary concern.

World.title: How Much Do Tourists Spend in Croatia? Data Reveals Changing Habits
World.content:
October the 30th, 2026 – How much do tourists from abroad actually spend when they come to Croatia? The latest data on precisely this reveals just how much habits have altered.

The results of the national survey entitled “Attitudes and Expenditure of Tourists in Croatia – TOMAS Croatia 2025/2026” were presented at the Croatian National Tourist Board recently. Morski reports that this took place with the participation of the Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina, the director of the Croatian National Tourist Board Kristjan Staničić, the director of the Institute for Tourism Damir Krešić, members of the Tourist Council of the CNTB and various representatives of professional associations in tourism.

guests spend 15% more than they did in 2022

The research, conducted by the Institute for Tourism, covered 14,770 tourists across the whole of Croatia, and the results provide insight into the characteristics of tourist demand, expenditure, motives for arrival and guest satisfaction. One of the most important results is the growth in the average daily expenditure of tourists. On the Adriatic it reached €162 per person, which is 15 percent more than back in 2022, while in continental Croatia it amounts to €164, with a growth of 21 percent. At the same time, on the Adriatic an increase was also recorded in the share of expenditure on additional destination services, such as sports, cultural and entertainment content as well as excursions and local transport, which confirms the importance of a diverse offer in creating additional value of the tourist stay.

“Such research is important for understanding the profile of our guests, their expectations, expenditure and satisfaction with the tourist offer. Comparison with the previous research shows how tourists’ habits are changing and where we have the opportunity to further strengthen the competitiveness of Croatian tourism. This year’s results confirm to us that Croatia attracts guests who on average spend more, but also that their habits are changing. Our task is not only to increase tourist traffic, but to create greater value from every tourist arrival. That means strengthening the quality of the offer, encouraging longer stays, developing year-round tourism and better connecting accommodation with gastronomy, culture, sport and other content,” Glavina stated.

guests with deeper pockets are growing on the coast

A positive trend has also been recorded in the structure of Croatia’s guests. On the Adriatic the share of guests with higher purchasing power is growing, with 74 percent of tourists stating monthly household income higher than €4,000. At the same time, the share of foreign guests visiting Croatia for the first time increased from 14 percent in 2022 to 22 percent in 2025, while 60 percent of foreign guests have visited Croatia at least three times, which confirms a combination of the destination’s attractiveness to new guests and the loyalty of existing visitors.

“The results of the TOMAS research are an important basis for the further improvement of Croatian tourism and the quality direction of our promotional activities. In order to build competitive and sustainable tourism, it is important to understand who our guests are, what motivates them to come and what kind of experiences they are looking for. Exactly such research enables us to base our activities on concrete indicators and the real experiences of visitors. Our goal is to continue positioning Croatia as a safe, authentic and year-round destination that builds its competitiveness on the diversity of the offer, natural and cultural riches, hospitality and the quality of the overall experience,” Staničić said.

croatia still stands out

The results further show how Croatia stands out with the quality of the experience and an offer that attracts different profiles of guests. Among the elements with very high satisfaction ratings on the Adriatic, the beauty of the place and nature, personal safety, atmosphere and ambience stand out, while guests of continental Croatia particularly highly rate personal safety, the hospitality of the local population, the overall stay and the cultural and artistic offer. As many as 69 percent of guests of continental Croatia would almost certainly recommend the destination they visited, and on the Adriatic that share amounts to 58 percent.

World.title: Air Montenegro Introduces Zagreb Flights Three Times a Week
World.content:
October the 30th, 2026 – Air Montenegro is planning to introduce Zagreb flights which will operate three times a week as of next month.

Air Montenegro plans to operate on the route between Podgorica and Zagreb within the framework of the Public Service Obligation (PSO) programme in Montenegro. According to information Croatian Aviation received, the planned flights are currently scheduled from the 24th of November this year with three rotations per week.

Air Montenegro has otherwise been given the opportunity to operate flights on several international routes within the Montenegrin Public Service Obligation (PSO) programme, and among them is the route that will connect Podgorica and Zagreb. The very first rotation is currently planned, as stated, for the 24th of November this year. The flights are scheduled on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays, which means a total of three weekly rotations until the end of the winter timetable. The airline is also expected to continue operating the flights in the summer timetable period next year, which is the period from the end of March to the end of October 2027.

The arrival of the aircraft from Podgorica at Zagreb Airport has been planned for early in the morning, just after 08:00, while departure of the aircraft from Zagreb towards Podgorica is planned at 08:50. Embraer E195 aircraft with a capacity of 118 seats in the carrier’s fleet are planned for operating the flights on this route. This means that Air Montenegro will offer a total of 12,508 seats between Podgorica and Zagreb this winter on the 53 announced rotations.

The introduction of this route within the PSO programme is otherwise important in scope for the connectivity of the two capitals and opens up an additional travel option for passengers between Croatia and Montenegro, between which there is currently no direct air route. Zagreb and Podgorica have potential for travel by different categories of passengers, from business and institutional to tourist and those travelling to visit family and friends.

Details about ticket sales, exact times of return flights and the final implementation of the schedule depend on the carrier’s announcement and official information for the winter timetable 2026/2027. It is expected that the carrier will release tickets for sale soon, and in the event of administrative difficulties, a postponement of the date of the first rotation is possible, but there is no doubt that the route will soon be in operation.

Previously, Ryanair operated on the route between Podgorica and Zagreb. The route was introduced back in September 2021, operated mainly twice a week, on Thursdays and Saturdays, with A320 aircraft with a capacity of up to 180 seats. The route was discontinued at the end of October 2023, and Ryanair justified that move by the increase in airport fees in the capital of Montenegro. Croatia Airlines also previously operated on this route, in the period from the end of June 2008 to the beginning of the summer timetable 2013, three times a week with Dash Q400 aircraft with a capacity of 76 seats. After more than three years without flights, Air Montenegro will soon reconnect the two capital cities.

World.title: Croatia Might See Some Snow Next Week as a Weather Change Looms
World.content:
October the 30th, 2026 – Croatia may see some snow next week as a dramatic weather change looms, bringing far colder temperatures and plenty of rain.

Over the next few days across Croatia, the weather will be predominantly cloudy and markedly cooler temperatures will prevail, with occasional rain. Index reports that on the Adriatic coast and the islands there will be more sunshine, but also very strong bura. According to the latest forecast issued by the Croatian Meteorological and Hydrological Service (DHMZ), a further deterioration of the weather is expected at the beginning of next week, and the first snow could fall in the highlands.

Over the weekend, the weather will be changeable, mostly cloudy inland, and in places rain will fall, especially in eastern and mountainous areas of Croatia. A weak to moderate northeasterly wind will blow, and on the Adriatic a moderate to strong bura, under Velebit with gale-force, in places even hurricane-force gusts. The highest daily temperature will range from 10 to 14 degrees inland and from 17 to 21 degrees on the Adriatic coast and the islands, DHMZ states. Inland, it will be predominantly cloudy, in places with a little rain, primarily in the east of the country and in mountainous Croatia. On the Adriatic it will be partly sunny, but still windy, with a moderate to strong bora, and under Velebit a gale-force bura wind. Morning temperatures will range from 4 to 8 degrees, and on the Adriatic from 10 to 15. During the day, 9 to 13 degrees are expected inland and 16 to 20 by the sea.

No major change in the weather is expected on Saturday. Inland clouds will prevail, and in places there will also be rain, especially in mountainous Croatia and in the east of the country. On the coast, there will be more sunny periods, but the bura will continue to blow, particularly strongly under Velebit. On Sunday, the 1st of November, more rain is expected in other parts of the interior as well. It will be cloudy and cooler, with a northerly and northeasterly wind that will occasionally be strong. The change in the weather will also affect Dalmatia, where along with more clouds local rain and showers are expected. Temperatures will gradually fall, and the highest daily values inland will be around 10 degrees. In the highland areas, snow is also possible on Sunday.

According to the DHMZ forecast, unstable and colder weather continues at the beginning of next week. On Monday, the 2nd of November, rain is expected in a large part of the interior, and temperatures will fall even further. DHMZ maps also show the possibility of snow in the higher areas of mountainous Croatia, especially on Monday and Tuesday. In some more mountainous areas a snow cover could also form, but this is a forecast several days ahead that can still change.

On Tuesday, cold and predominantly cloudy weather will continue, with occasional rain, while snow is still possible in the highlands. According to current forecasts, from Wednesday, the 4th of November, a gradual calming of the weather is expected. There will be less precipitation, and in places sunny periods will appear. Nevertheless, temperatures will remain relatively low and feel far colder, especially inland.

World.title: Ingrid Neel out in WTA Tokyo doubles quarterfinals
World.content:
Estonian tennis player Ingrid Neel and her partner Giuliana Olmos (Mexico) were eliminated in the quarterfinals of the women's doubles competition at the WTA tournament in Tokyo Thursday.

Neel and Olmos went down 6-2, 6-4 to the pairing of Tereza Mihalikova (Slovakia) and Olivia Nicholls (Great Britain). Neel and Olmos had just one break point during the match but failed to convert it.

In the first round, Neel and Olmos had beaten Shuko Aoyama (Japan) and Liang En Shuo (Taiwan) in three sets.

Neel, 28, is an Estonian-American who has represented Estonia since 2023. She is a doubles specialist, and has ranked as high as 33rd in the world in her career so far.

World.title: Estonia's Russia expertise is respected by the US, says foreign minister
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said the United States has not made any proposals to Estonia to change its tone when discussing the Russian threat. He said Estonia is respected in America because the country is an expert on Russia.

On Friday, Reuters news agency, citing anonymous sources, reported that Pentagon officials had urged several NATO allies, including Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, to tone down their public rhetoric on the threat posed by Russia.

Tsahkna and outgoing Ministry of Foreign Affairs Secretary General Jonatan Vseviov pushed back on the media reports on Friday afternoon.

"The United States has not made any official proposal to us that we should in any way change our foreign policy or our communication," Tsahkna told ERR.

"These are anonymous sources. I cannot comment on them, and I do not want to comment on them. However, Estonia is highly respected in the eyes of the United States and more broadly within NATO, because we are, after all, experts when it comes to Russia. Likewise, we can see very far into Russia, and our expert assessments and intelligence are highly valued," the minister said.

He pointed out that Russia is "organizing terrorist attacks and acts of sabotage" against Europe and that Estonia has not been afraid to point this out, publicly.

"Estonia has always been very clear and honest when it comes to the Russian threat and Russia's aggression against Ukraine. Also about the fact that we do not currently see Russia preparing for large-scale aggression against NATO, because we do not see any major movements of Russian troops or increases in their capabilities beyond our borders. At the same time, however, we see Russia increasingly organizing terrorist attacks and acts of sabotage against Europe. And here, too, we have been very clear in publicly attributing these acts and punishing the perpetrators. However, what Russia is doing is trying to undermine Western unity. It is trying to play on that same fear of escalation, which Russia has constantly done, while continually accusing NATO and the Western world of preparing some kind of aggression against Russia, which is absolutely not true," Tsahkna said.

'Russia is provoking us'

One source told Reuters that Elbridge Colby, the Pentagon's top policy official, recently told an official from one of the Baltic states that Russia should not be provoked.

Tsahkna denied that Estonia is provoking Russia.

"We are in constant contact with the United States on security policy, on the deployment of their troops here and on NATO defense plans. And it is certainly not in our interests to provoke Russia in any way; rather, Russia is provoking us. So we are not under any pressure one way or the other. We discuss these matters together. The United States is a NATO ally and Article 5 works, so this communication takes place daily," Tsahkna said.

Tsahkna stressed that neither the Baltic states nor Estonia have been aggressive in their messages in any way. "This entire narrative is connected to Putin's desire to undermine the political unity of our Western world," he said.

Ministry of Defense spokesperson Ines Edur told ERR that the ministry does not comment on a story based on anonymous sources and that no such request has been received by the ministry through official channels.

World.title: MEP Marina Kaljurand not running in Riigikogu election
World.content:
SDE leader Lauri Läänemets confirmed that Kaljurand, who ran in the same electoral district (Harju and Rapla counties) in the previous Riigikogu elections in 2023, wlll not be running this time around, and outgoing Foreign Ministry Secretary General Jonatan Vseviov will take her place as a candidate.

"We have indeed taken Marina Kaljurand's wishes into account, as she has said that she will not be taking part in the Riigikogu elections this time," Läänemets said.

Kaljurand had said in an interview with ERR in April this year that she did not see herself continuing in politics after her current mandate at the European Parliament ends. Kaljurand, a former foreign minister and ambassador to both Russia and the United States, has been an MEP since 2019.

"As for the Harju and Rapla counties electoral district, that is where the prime ministerial candidate usually runs. If the party council confirms Jonatan Vseviov as its candidate for prime minister this Sunday, then naturally Jonatan Vseviov will also be at the top of the list in that electoral district," Läänemets said.

"And this also fits with the logic of having the prime ministerial candidate run in Harju and Rapla counties, so we will not have to make choices there, but can go into the elections with strong candidates competing against one another," Läänemets went on.

SDE is known for frequently placing its leading candidates at the bottom of its national list, even though this has backfired on the party on several occasions — for example, it led to former Riigikogu Speaker Eiki Nestor leaving politics.

Estonia's modified d'Hondt system means parties can position prominent names to maximize their share of compensation mandates – where candidates lower down on a list receive the excess votes from higher profile candidates who have already won a seat. With a higher profile candidate lower on a list, this cannot happen, however.

"The same procedure still applies in our party. The national list is discussed by the party's board, but this is the very last stage in the process of drawing up the electoral lists. This means we will get to that sometime around the beginning of January," Läänemets said.

Läänemets acknowledged that the Nestor case was not the party's greatest success, but said the system, established 15 years ago, has generally served the party by making candidates work harder and giving more people a chance of entering parliament.

Since Kaljurand is an MEP she did not take up the Riigikogu seat she won in any case; again, the next candidate on the list who has not won a seat in their own right gets that seat. In general this brings a situation where parties run high profile candidates with no intention of them taking up a Riigikogu seat if won, usually because they cannot – for instance if they hold a local government leadership position or, as in Kaljruand's case, a European Parliament seat.

SDE is to hold an electoral assembly in January, where its national list, district lists across all 12 districts, and platform will all be approved. Läänemets said experience shows minor and major changes alike are often needed at the last instant, hence the board's final decision on the national list coming relatively late – the election itself is March 7.

Vseviov was a long-serving Foreign Ministry secretary general and security expert who joined SDE earlier this month, meaning he will be stepping down from the secretary general post in November. He is also running as the party's prime ministerial candidate.

World.title: Official: Estonia should never even consider giving up its voice on Russia
World.content:
Outgoing Foreign Ministry Secretary General Jonatan Vseviov said he is not aware of any request from U.S. officials for Estonia to change its message on the threat from Russia, following a report published by Reuters news agency on Friday.

The story, citing anonymous sources, said Pentagon officials had urged several NATO allies, including Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, to tone down their public rhetoric on the threat posed by Russia.

"I am not aware of such official requests, but the fact that not everyone may like the content or style of Estonia's message is no kind of surprise to me," Vseviov told ERR Friday. "That anyone would have officially proposed that Estonia keep quiet — I am not aware of that. And perhaps also because a proposal like that would always and in any case get rejected."

"Estonia's voice is our most important trump card, the most important weapon for taking part in international politics. And while that voice must be used wisely and never belligerently, surrendering that voice is something we should never even consider," he added.

Vseviov declined to say whether such a request had been conveyed unofficially, but did not rule it out. "Unofficially, people talk all the time... I honestly can't find any news value in that in itself," he said.

He said he would not draw far-reaching conclusions from the Reuters article, as often only a fragment of what happened behind closed doors reaches the media. Asked whether Estonia should tone down its positions, he said everything said about Estonia internationally must be taken into account, but that Estonia must use its voice as well as it can.

"The time when going to Washington cap in hand, hoping to get the Americans to do our business for us, is over," Vseviov said, adding that Europe must stand on its own two feet and treat America as a pragmatic, balanced ally that "does not have to panic at every thought expressed there."

He said Estonia's official positions on the security situation have been accurate and have foreseen events. "It is no coincidence that after the start of the great war on February 24, 2022, a whole string of world leaders pointed out that Estonia and the other Baltic states should have been listened to earlier," he said.

On Friday, Reuters reported that one source said U.S. officials had taken issue with statements by European leaders suggesting Russia had been backed into a corner, and that Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby was one of those conveying the message. A Pentagon official said: "Private conversations among allies are just that, so we will not comment on these allegations."

Lithuania's Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said he too had no information about such a request. "What we speak is always based on facts. If a Russian drone flew in, we say that a Russian drone flew in," he said. "We state the facts and will continue to do so."

Vseviov announced last week that he was joining the Social Democratic Party and running in the Riigikogu elections, and is expected to be confirmed as the party's prime ministerial candidate. He steps down as secretary general next month.

World.title: Estonian Drama Theater limits ticket sales
World.content:
The Estonian Drama Theater has limited ticket sales to four per customer for a single performance, down from the previous eight, but an increase on the two tickets announced earlier this week.

The theater changed its proposed policy of two tickets per performance after an outcry from customers earlier this week.

"Since many theatergoers contacted us, we decided to change the restriction so that instead of two tickets, four tickets can be purchased for a single performance at a time. Hopefully, this will allow us to ensure a good purchasing experience for more people while not excessively restricting theater visits by families and groups of friends," the Drama Theater said in a newsletter.

Newspaper Postimees reported on Thursday that the theater would also discontinue group bookings because waiting lists are extremely long.

Drama Theater marketing manager Katre Väli said the decision had to be made because of exceptionally high demand.

"The waiting lists for group bookings for the most popular productions listed on our website are four to six years long, with thousands of people interested. We generally suspend group bookings when calculations show that fulfilling the orders would extend beyond two seasons," she explained.

Väli could not say when group bookings for these productions would reopen.

Group bookings started at 20 tickets, with a maximum of 50 tickets available for reservation.

World.title: Estonia's land value up a third in four years to €44.1 billion
World.content:
Estonia's total land value has grown 33 percent in four years, from €33.2 billion to €44.1 billion, according to the Land and Spatial Board's (Maa- ja Ruumiamet) regular valuation.

Harju County accounts for 57 percent of the total at €25.2 billion, far ahead of the next on the list, Tartu County at 11 percent, and Pärnu County at 7 percent. Values grew fastest in municipalities around Tallinn and Tartu.

The valuation gets carried out every four years and covers all of Estonia's roughly 780,000 cadastral units, using real estate transaction data and models based on location and land characteristics.

Commenting on the results, Marje Kolmar-Grüner, head of the land valuation department, said: "The biggest changes often appear in areas where previously unbuilt-on land has become a new living environment. For example, in Tartu near the former Raadi airfield, the assessed value of land has in some cases grown more than tenfold, and in Järveküla in Rae parish in Harju County, the assessed value has in some cases more than doubled."

Land value grew most rapidly among municipalities in the Tallinn and Tartu commuter belt, and of these it was Tartu Rural Municipality (as distinct from Tartu City Municipality to the south) which saw the most rapid growth, at an average of 59 percent.

Overall by county, growth was fastest in Rapla, Lääne and Võru counties, which were all above 40 percent, and was slowest in Ida-Viru County at 18 percent.

Nearly all cadastral units saw a land value rise — in 96 percent of cases, with the remaining 4 percent seeing unchanged or falling values.

While residential land is the most expensive in Harju County, it has not risen fastest there: values grew quickest at the other end of the country, in Võru County, at 55.9 percent, as well as in Järva County at 55.6 and Rapla County at 55.5. The slowest rise was seen in Ida-Viru County at 12.6 percent.

Forest land value rose across Estonia by between 46 percent in Harju County and 58.8 percent in Järva County, the fastest growth of any land type. The median price of unbuilt land roughly doubled in four years.

Residential land makes up about half of Estonia's total value at €22.2 billion, with commercial and industrial land coming to about 18 percent, at €8.1 billion.

Land values set in 2026 will be used to calculate land tax from 2028. Local governments decide the tax rate, for residential land between 0.1 and 1 percent. They also decide how much land tax may rise by in a year.

World.title: Estonia's judges may take pay dispute to European Commission
World.content:
Estonian judges may turn to the European Commission in the face of a four-year pay freeze, but Minister of Finance Jürgen Ligi (Reform) believes everyone must currently make savings.

Judges are concerned about a decision in the state budget strategy to curb salary growth for senior public officials over the next four years.

Judges have a special status under the Constitution, and their salaries are also linked to the obligation to hold office for life. As reduced indexation was initially supposed to end in 2028, the government decided to extend it until 2031.

Although judges are outraged, Ligi said he currently sees no reason to discuss judges' special status.

"The initial decision has been made, and it is not reasonable to discuss judges' special status. What is reasonable to discuss is whether those who currently fall outside this regulation should also have their regulations changed, primarily the Riigikogu," he said.

The minister added that indexing salaries and linking them to average wages or employment is a fairly safe approach.

"Nothing unfair or disproportionate is happening there. We are going through difficult times, and in a situation where the public sector is making cuts across the board, it is difficult to argue that anyone is exempt from the inevitability of cuts," he explained.

Ligi compared the current situation to the financial crisis, when there were also major political risks, but relief could then be expected from the introduction of the euro. Now the situation is more serious.

Anu Uritam, a Harju County Court judge who heads the Estonian Association of Judges, told ERR that this argument is understandable, but judges are unwilling to accept the situation.

"Which areas the state cuts and which it invests in is a political decision. We are going through difficult times, but that has not prevented the state from investing in major construction projects, from Süku to Rail Baltica. So ultimately, it is a political decision where the state chooses to allocate its resources and where to make cuts. As for the judicial system, the administration of justice is one of the state's core functions, and a state cannot function without it," she said.

Uritam explained that judges' workloads have increased, for example, due to the migration crisis, and that finding new judges is becoming increasingly difficult because the judicial system has undergone several budget cuts.

She added that by reducing indexation, the state has already broken its promise regarding judges' social guarantees.

Uritam therefore does not rule out raising the issue at the international level as well.

"One option we have not yet used is to approach the European Association of Judges through the Estonian Association of Judges and ask it to draw up a resolution supporting Estonian judges. This would be forwarded to the governments of European member states, and we could also inform the European Commission. In other words, we will try to draw attention to the problem internationally as well," she promised.

World.title: Agricultural drones make first flights in Estonia as rules start to ease
World.content:
Agricultural drones capable of crop-spraying and seeding are making their first flights in Estonia, though strict safety rules still limit wider use.

Simpler survey drones have been in use by Estonian farmers for several years already, to gather field data. From this week, the law permits the aerial spraying of plant protection products, though under strict conditions.

Farmers have been trained at a Rural Knowledge Center (METK) open day at the Nurmsi drone center in Järva County on Thursday, learning to use drones for field monitoring as well as for sowing and weed control.

"Weed infestation, sowing errors, drainage system failures — a great deal of different information. Together with the Rural Knowledge Center, we are currently learning spectral analysis, how to analyze the light reflected from plants by spectral bands," said Madis Pruus, agronomist at Järva County-based agricultural concern Väätsa Agro.

That analysis reveals the health of a given crop. Väätsa Agro has been using simpler and lower-cost drones for six years now, to gather information from fields. This helps in making production decisions.

METK estimates that drones are still not a regularly used tool in day-to-day Estonian agriculture, even as they can perform about a dozen different tasks.

"A drone allows precision farming techniques, variable-rate work cards or spot treatments only," said Ainar Härm, drone technology engineer at METK. For example, if there is a patch of thistles in the middle of a field, only that patch can be treated. "We don't have to go and treat the whole field," he added.

Drones have other advantages too, for instance being lightweight or, since they are airborne, not leaving much of a footprint at all, unlike heavy agricultural plant.

"Since an agricultural drone is light and doesn't flatten down the field, you can work field edges in spring when the fields are soft. You can fertilize and spread seeds," said Anti Konsap, senior engineer at METK.

The main obstacle so far to wider use has been strict restrictions on drone flying, though the situation is gradually improving, experts say.

"From yesterday the law permits the use of plant protection products for aerial spraying, but according to special conditions. It is very important to remember that the product itself must also be approved for aerial use. To my knowledge that list is still extremely short," said Taavi Võsa, researcher in agro-technology at METK.

Farmers who attended the open day said that although drones may turn into an efficient aid, they will fully replace neither the tractor nor the farmer at any time soon.

World.title: Iraqi pharmacy sets Guinness World Record with 79,069 hydration pledges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has achieved a Guinness World Records title after Haya Pharmacy’s “Ghaith” hydration awareness campaign collected 79,069 pledges in one month, encouraging people across the country to adopt healthier water-drinking habits.

The initiative, which broke the record in Baghdad on October 5, 2026, got the highest pledges for a hydration awareness campaign in a single month.

The campaign, which was created in partnership with the Ebers marketing team, integrated community participation and public health awareness efforts to encourage regular water intake.

The campaign was strategically driven from Dubai, with teams from Ebers and Haya Pharmacy overseeing its execution on the ground in Iraq.

The success marks a significant milestone for Haya Pharmacy’s public health programs, demonstrating the effectiveness of national awareness campaigns in promoting better lives and community engagement.

World.title: Iraq signs agreement with Swiss pharma giant Roche
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Swiss pharmaceutical manufacturer Roche has inked a strategic partnership deal with Iraq’s Ministry of Health to strengthen healthcare services, with a focus on ophthalmology and hemophilia A.

In Baghdad, Swiss Ambassador Peter Nelson and officials from Roche and the Iraqi Health Ministry attended the signing of the agreement.

The partnership’s goal is to enhance patient care by strengthening diagnostic capacities, introducing sophisticated medical technology, and providing specialized training for Iraqi healthcare personnel.

Roche also reiterated its long-standing commitment to Iraq’s healthcare sector, emphasizing the necessity of working with government institutions to provide access to breakthrough therapies and medical knowledge.

The company thanked Iraqi Health Minister Dr. Abdul Hussein Al-Mousawi for his support of foreign pharmaceutical companies and recognition of the significance of intellectual property protection in promoting medical innovation.

The arrangement is part of an attempt to modernize Iraq’s healthcare system and provide access to specialized medical services.

World.title: Maserati expands Iraq presence with new automotive partner
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Italian luxury carmaker Maserati has appointed Tiraz Automotive and Service Group as its new official partner in Iraq, aiming to strengthen its presence and expand customer access to the brand.

The deal was inked on September 18 in Modena, Italy, during a meeting between Maserati personnel and a Tiraz team headed by Kambiz Fathibitaraf.

Maserati hopes that the relationship would allow it to grow its operations in Iraq and provide consumers with a more personalized ownership experience, including access to its Fuoriserie customization program.

Customers may personalize their automobiles with various colors, materials, and design features that suit their specific interests.

The appointment is part of Maserati’s strategy to expand its presence in the Iraqi luxury automobile market and increase its local customer base.

World.title: Iraq signs gas capture agreement with US firm Morgan Hughes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US-based Morgan Hughes Energy has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Iraq’s General Company for Carbon Economics (GCCE) to develop projects aimed at capturing and utilizing associated gas currently flared at oil production sites across Iraq.

The agreement was signed in Baghdad by Morgan Hughes Energy Managing Director Gregory Bloom and GCCE, under the patronage of Iraq’s Minister of Environment, Sarwa Abdulwahid, and in the presence of US Chargé d’Affaires Steven Fagin.

The proposed partnership will focus on recovering low-pressure associated gas and using it to generate electricity for oil production facilities, reducing gas flaring and reliance on Iraq’s national electricity grid.

The initiative also aims to develop carbon credit projects using internationally recognized monitoring and verification standards, creating potential revenue opportunities through carbon markets while supporting Iraq’s emissions reduction targets.

Morgan Hughes Energy said it plans to bring American expertise and technology to the projects, supporting Iraq’s energy security and hydrocarbon development.

The company operates in the upstream and midstream oil and gas sectors, with interests across the Middle East, including offshore gas production, pipeline infrastructure, and gas storage facilities.

The MoU represents an initial step towards a broader strategic partnership between the two companies, with specific projects still subject to further development.

World.title: Iraq to issue licenses for digital banks in early 2028
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) confirmed on Wednesday that final approvals for the establishment of digital banks will be issued in early 2028.

The spokesperson for the CBI, Mahmoud Dagher, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) that final permissions for digital banking licenses will be granted after the banking reform phase is complete, by the end of 2027 or the start of 2028.

Oliver Wyman is presently leading the banking reform process, and organizations that sought to establish digital banks and gained preliminary permissions are aware of the timescale for gaining final authorizations, according to Dagher.

In October 2025, the CBI has received approximately 80 applications to create digital banks in the country.

Licenses can only be awarded following a set of criteria based on market research, the nature of the business, and other countries’ experiences, where the number of digital banks is often limited to three or four.

Earlier in 2025, officials from the CBI and representatives from Oliver Wyman discussed a banking reform proposal offered by the Iraqi Private Banks League (IPBL) to modernize Iraq’s banking industry and align operations with worldwide practices.

The strategy aims to stabilize the banking sector to function more securely and effectively, as well as local legislation, while strengthening governance, compliance, and risk management.

The CBI noted that adopting the strategy will boost local and international trust in Iraq’s banking industry.

Iraq’s central bank reached an agreement earlier with Oliver Wyman to perform a thorough analysis of the conditions under which Iraqi banks are prohibited from conducting transactions in US dollars.

Oliver Wyman focuses on improving bank procedures to align with international standards, creating effective strategies to reintegrate Iraqi banks that have been barred from conducting US dollar transactions back into the banking sector, both domestically and internationally.

World.title: Iraq’s Development Road to provide million job opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The designs for the Development Road project have reached their final stages and will be fully completed before the end of 2026, according to the Iraqi Ministry of Transport.

The spokesperson for the Ministry of Transport, Ali al-Khalidi, said that the Development Road project is expected to generate approximately 100,000 job opportunities during its first phase.

Plans include the construction of modern stations, industrial zones, and residential areas along the route, developments that could potentially create over a million jobs as the project and its associated facilities expand, according to al-Khalidi.

The Iraqi official explained that 95 percent of the project’s railway designs have been completed, with 92 percent of the highway designs finished, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Extending from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, with both the highway and railway being parallel lines, the first phase of the project is expected to be completed in 2033.

The Development Road’s primary objective is to transport goods from al-Faw Grans Port to Turkey—and onward to Europe—and vice versa.

Work is currently underway to finalize an agreement with Turkey to establish a fund that would finance the project’s implementation by Turkish companies through an oil-for-financing arrangement, according to INA.

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

World.title: Norway’s DNO considers exporting Iraqi Kurdistan oil via Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Norwegian oil producer DNO is actively exploring routes through Syria to export its Iraqi Kurdistan crude oil to the Mediterranean.

According to Reuters, the initiative aims to bypass local market constraints and fetch significantly higher international benchmark prices.

DNO has been selling oil from its Tawke and Peshkabir fields to the local market at low prices. Although its domestic sales price increased somewhat to $45 per barrel in October 2026 compared to an average of $38.50 in the third quarter, it is still significantly below global benchmarks.

Due to the Syrian civil war, transport to the Mediterranean through Syria was previously impossible. However, regional logistics are shifting. Significant volumes of southern Iraqi fuel oil and crude are already being transported by tanker trucks directly through Syria for export.

Reflecting past delays in payments from the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), DNO requires international buyers to deposit US dollars into its offshore accounts before any oil is collected.

While trucks would be necessary for short-term movements, long-term solutions would encounter infrastructural obstacles.

Despite prior political support from the United States to study the route, rebuilding a key Iraq-Syria oil pipeline may cost around $15 billion and take years to become fully operational.

DNO is stepping up its drilling operations to increase the gross output from its important Kurdish licenses, which averaged 77,621 barrels of oil per day in the third quarter of 2026.

World.title: Iraq, Syria discuss exporting two million bpd of oil via Baniyas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa discussed on Wednesday the development of economic and security cooperation, particularly the export of Iraqi oil through Baniyas with a capacity up to two million barrels per day.

The discussions took place during the first visit by an Iraqi prime minister to Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime in late 2024. The visit marks a step toward strengthening relations between the two countries, which share a border stretching over 600 kilometers.

The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement that the meeting addressed increasing trade exchange and developing the agricultural sector to achieve food and economic integration, in addition to discussing oil exports via Syria’s Baniyas port.

However, the statement did not mention when the route will start operating at the specified capacity.

Al-Zaidi highlighted initiatives to develop partnerships in the social and economic domains, boost security cooperation, and coordinate stances on regional and global concerns.

The Syrian Presidency said that the extended discussions in Damascus covered approaches to promote security, economic, and commercial cooperation, as well as regional and international developments.

Iraq started earlier exporting limited quantities of oil through the Syrian port of Baniyas—a move prompted by disruptions of maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the conflict in the Middle East.

In July, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to revive the Haditha–Baniyas pipeline. A deal was signed with a consortium of three companies, including US-based Chevron, to carry out the project.

The pipeline was built in 1952, but it was abandoned in 2003 due to damage sustained during the invasion of Iraq by the United States. Its reactivation would provide an outlet for Iraqi oil exports via the Mediterranean Sea.

World.title: Can amend privacy act, revoke law if needed: Government
World.content:
âCentre open to amending DPDP Act rules or the law itself to address media concerns over its impact on press freedom, days after Supreme Court agreed to hear challenge

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Centre Friday said it is open to changing the rules of Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and, if necessary, the law itself to eliminate the possibility of its application becoming an impediment for journalists and media houses.Senior officials at the ministry for electronics & information technology said that sections of the law, which have been flagged as violative of the constitutional provisions guaranteeing freedom of speech and expression, are applicable to data fiduciaries and they are not for journalists."This law is only on data fiduciaries-those who keep and control data. Journalists and media houses do not come under this category," When told about the worry among journalists that DPDP Act does not expressly exempt media houses, he said, "The rules can always be amended to allay any concern on that count. The rules have the same power as the law. If necessary, we can go a step further to change the law itself."The DPDP Act has been been justified in citing citizen's right to privacy, the need to protect data and in placing obligations on data fiduciaries.Centre's reaction came days after the apex court agreed to examine a plea filed by Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) which represents 21 of India's leading news media organisations and challenged the validity of various provisions of the act and rules framed under it.The association alleged that the law was violative of the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression and threatened the full spectrum of journalistic activity.Officials said that the the concern about the DPDP act becoming an impediment for journalists will be addressed by carving out exemptions for them in the rules and, if necessary, in the law itself.I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnav said on Friday that Section 7 of the DPDP Act is for data fiduciaries like banks, telecom providers and insurance companies and media does not come within its ambit. "This govt is committed to uphold the constitutionally guaranteed rights to freedom and expression". Section 7 says that "the personal data of a data principal may be processed by a data fiduciary (a) for the specified purpose for which the Data Principal has voluntarily provided her personal data. .. and in respect of which she has not indicated... that she does not consent to the use of her personal data."

World.title: Discourage weaponisation of rape law in relationships gone sour: SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Society and courts must discourage weaponisation of criminal law against men in the aftermath of an emotional discord and breakup of a consenting romantic relationship, Supreme Court said Friday, expressing concern over the disturbing trend of criminal provision of rape being invoked to prosecute men after relationship turns sour.

A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said the legislature never intended consensual sexual acts between adults to be retrospectively criminalised merely because the relationship came to an end. "It is unfortunate that despite judicial deprecation, this trend is increasing, and it is a matter of concern as often settlement of disputes come with huge monetary considerations to be borne by the male accused," it said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The court underlined "a worrying trend in recent years, wherein consensual relationship is given a colour of sexual assault".

"In fact, such an approach denudes the man of any agency entirely, as the mere factum of being in a consensual relationship at one point would bind him to it entirely for fear of being accused of rape at a subsequent point of time," SC said, while allowing the plea of a man who was being prosecuted for rape on a complaint filed by his erstwhile live-in partner with whom he shared a relationship for seven years..

The top court also cautioned that the trend carries the risk of undermining the gravity of the serious criminal offence of rape.

World.title: Government asks ministries to identify cases that can be withdrawn
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cabinet secretary T V Somanathan has directed secretaries of ministries and departments to identify cases that can be withdrawn following decriminalisation of several offences under Jan Vishwas Act and removal of obsolete legal provisions.

They have been asked to complete the exercise by the end of this month.

The move is part of govt's efforts to reduce its litigation burden and avoid pursuing cases that may have lost their relevance following changes in the legal framework. The review will cover cases affected by amendments under Act and other legal reforms.

Currently, there are over 3.5 lakh litigations involving central govt pending for more than five years, including over one lakh legacy cases across 19 high courts.

According to a presentation, the revenue department has the highest number of cases pending for more than five years at 1.27 lakh, followed by railways (45,583), department of military affairs (32,464), labour and employment (28,822) and corporate affairs (27,109).

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Officials said some ministries, including road transport, defence and telecommunications, may have fewer pending cases, but the financial implications of these litigations are likely to be substantially higher.





In two rounds under Jan Vishwas legislations, in 2023 and 2026, several sections of different central laws have been decriminalised and rationalised by introducing compliance provisions.

TOI has learnt that while chairing a meeting of all secretaries, Somanathan informed them that a dedicated "litigation management portal" will be launched in Nov to monitor the functioning of litigation management cells, review of legacy litigations and appeals, mediation and screening of cases. Ministries and departments will have to regularly update the status of cases.

World.title: Census 2027 population enumeration phase to be of record 50 days
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The population enumeration phase of Census 2027 will last longer than in past census exercises, with its duration spanning nearly one-and-a-half months from Jan 10 to Feb 28, including the 15-day self-enumeration window, as against the earlier Phase-2 duration of 20 days, conventionally running from Feb 9-28.

Sources told TOI that the house-to-house population enumeration schedule announced earlier for poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab also spans 35 days. The longer duration may be linked to the increased number of questions at 40, including pertaining to caste, to be asked in Phase-2 of Census 2027, as against 29 in 2011.

No census has been declared in Manipur. The census exercise in the state was put on hold after demands from various sections within the state that the National Register of Citizens (NRC) exercise be conducted first.

A notification issued by the Union home ministry Friday declared that a nationwide census of population shall be undertaken - except in Manipur (till further declaration); poll-bound states of Goa, UP, Punjab and Uttarakhand, where it was preponed in view of the impending assembly elections early next year; and UT of Ladakh and snow-bound, non-synchronous areas of Himachal Pradesh and UT of Jammu & Kashmir, where it has already been completed - from Jan 25 to Feb 27, 2027.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





This shall be preceded by a window of self-enumeration from Jan 10-24. While the reference date for Census 2027 has already been declared as March 1, 2027, a revisional round will be conducted from March 1-5, 2027.

The new fields to be captured in Phase-2 of Census include, apart from caste, spouse's name and mother and father's particulars, the respondent's nationality as declared, permanent address, place of Covid-19 vaccination, total number of bank accounts, mobile number, Aadhaar number, voter ID number, passport number and availability of driving licence.

While the mobile number, Aadhaar and voter ID may be shared if available, the passport number is required only from an Indian passport holder.

World.title: UK govt announces new ‘safe and legal’ routes for refugees in India to resettle in UK
World.content:
UK announces three new refugee resettlement routes for people in India and six other countries, allowing sponsorship through charities, employers and universities.

TOI correspondent from London:

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In a bid to dissuade asylum-seekers from arriving in Britain on the backs of lorries or via small boats, the UK home office has announced three new âsafe and legalâ sponsorship routes for refugees in India and six other countries to come to the UK and claim asylum.The new routes are initially targeted at refugees who have sought protection in India, Bangladesh, Egypt, Kenya, Malaysia, Pakistan and Uganda.To be eligible, the refugees will need to be outside their country of nationality, to have been verified by the UNHCR as meeting the definition of refugee and to have registered with the UNHCR or relevant authorities in one of these seven countries before Oct 1. So, in Indiaâs case, it could be Tibetans, Sri Lankan Tamils, Afghans, Rohingya and others from Myanmar, who could be eligible for these routes, but not Indian nationals residing in India, nor internally displaced people.The refugee sponsorship routes, modelled on a similar programme in Canada, allow sponsors in the UK to identify refugees they wish to sponsor. The new routes are named community sponsorship, which enables UK charities to identify refugees they wish to sponsor; refugee work, which enables UK employers to sponsor and provide refugees jobs; and refugee study, which enables UK universities to sponsor refugees to study in the UK.Once resettled, the refugees will have an immediate right to work, study and to access welfare benefits in Britain and be placed on a five-year path to permanent resettlement.Sponsors will have to finance and provide their accommodation, the aim being to reduce the amount UKâs govt spends on asylum hotels.Applications to be sponsors for the community and study route have opened and the first arrivals are expected in autumn 2027. Applications under the work route will open in spring 2027.Both Reform UK and the Conservatives vowed to shut the scheme if they come to power. Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said until illegal migration is stopped, âwe should not be creating new routes into the UK for asylum claimantsâ.

World.title: Bhutan GLOF creates new lake downstream, raises fears of secondary hazards
World.content:
DEHRADUN/KOLKATA/GUWAHATI: A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) originating in Bhutan, which prompted an alert across parts of Assam and West Bengal on Friday, has led to the formation of a new temporary lake downstream, raising concerns about a possible secondary hazard.

Bhutanâs National Centre for Hydrology and Meteorology (NCHM) confirmed that the outburst had led to the creation of a new artificial lake at Taktsemakhang, situated at the confluence of Sintaphu Chhu and Lungu Chhu, also known as Gangchen Tag Chhu. The newly formed body of water is being monitored for any potential secondary flood hazard, with NCHM advising residents in the Mochhu and Punatsangchhu river valleys to remain vigilant and avoid riverbanks and low-lying areas.

The Oct 29 GLOF originated from Shintaphu glacial lake which, according to International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) estimates, contained 6 to 7 million cubic metres of water, equivalent to approximately 2,400-2,800 Olympic-size swimming pools, before the breach. The volume of water released remains under assessment. Indiaâs Central Water Commission (CWC) subsequently issued a special flood advisory for West Bengal and Assam, warning that water levels in Alipurduar and Dhubri districts could rise sharply as floodwaters moved downstream through the Sankosh river system.





West Bengal had issued a high alert across north Bengal but the GLOF has had little or no impact in the state. On Friday morning, as water from the Bhutan hills came downstream, the Sankosh river rose 1.5 metres from its normal level but began receding soon. By Friday afternoon it appeared the crisis was over and people who had taken refuge in flood centres returned to their homes. No damage was reported. The Alipurduar district administration had opened 18 flood shelters in Kumargramduar block on Thursday night and around 10,000 people living along the banks of the Sankosh in Kumargram tea estate, Kumargram forest village, Pakriguri and Bholka had taken refuge in these shelters along with a couple of thousand from Assam.

Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the state was closely monitoring the possible impact of the glacial lake outburst across all vulnerable revenue circles of Dhubri and Kokrajhar districts. âOur teams â¦ are ready to respond if needed. Residents are requested to stay alert, follow official updates and cooperate with officials,â he said.

According to Bhutanâs national daily âKuenselâ, the GLOF sent floodwaters down the Mochhu river, damaging roads, bridges and public infrastructure in Gasa and Punakha.

No casualties have been reported. Floodwaters washed away facilities at Gasa Tshachu, damaged sections of the Punakha-Gasa Secondary National Highway and the Gasa-Laya road, and swept away a Bailey bridge in Punakha built in 2022 with Indian support.

Ashim Sattar, a glacial hazard expert at IIT Bhubaneswar, told TOI that the formation of temporary lakes downstream is a known risk during such disasters. âDuring GLOFs, powerful floodwaters erode river valleys and carry large amounts of debris, which can temporarily block river channels and form new lakes.

Such lakes generally drain naturally, but they can also become secondary flood hazards if not regularly monitored,â Sattar said.

He explained that Shintaphu was a medium-sized glacial lake located close to the Lunana glacial lake complex, a cluster of four lakes, including Thorthormi, considered one of Bhutanâs most hazardous.

According to NCHM, the flood crossed Taktsemakhang around 8.27 pm on Thursday. Warning sirens along Mochhu and downstream Punatsangchhu were activated as monitoring stations recorded a sharp rise in river levels.

At Yebesa, the water level peaked at 6.7 m at 11 pm before receding to a normal level of 2.84 m around 12.30 am on Friday, a drop of 3.86 m within 90 minutes.

Sattar noted that timely activation of the regional early-warning network prevented loss of life.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The incident highlights the growing threat of cascading disasters in the Himalayas, where an initial glacial breach can trigger secondary hazards downstream through valley erosion, sediment deposition and temporary river blockages.

Previous assessments by ICIMOD and UNDP identified 47 major potentially dangerous glacial lakes (PDGLs) across the transboundary Koshi, Gandaki and Karnali river basins. Current estimates show that 388 GLOFs have been documented across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region, including Karakoram and the central and eastern Himalayas.

In 2015, a GLOF in the headwaters of the Mo Chuu river, where Sintaphu lake is located, prompted Bhutanese authorities to work with the SERVIR-Himalaya initiative to assess glacial lake risks in the catchment, according to experts at ICIMOD.

World.title: BJP mock Parliament cruel joke on democracy: Congress
World.content:
Congress slams BJP over 'mock Parliament'

NEW DELHI: Congress Friday mocked the "BJP-sponsored mock parliament" in the capital as a "cruel joke", even as opposition was forced to postpone its "public impeachment" of CEC Gyanesh Kumar to Saturday because of bad weather.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal claimed "BJP-sponsored outfits" held a 'mock parliament' Friday after BJP has made a "mockery" of Parliament for the last 12 years."First treat Parliament as rubber-stamp to steamroll bills and silence opposition and now run a 'mock parliament' to make a cruel joke of democracy," he said, referring to a 'mock parliament' on 'democracy vs anarchy' at NDMC Convention Centre. Amid rain and flanked by INDIA bloc members, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi Friday invited all to attend the Nov 1 "Chalo Dilli" rally at Ramlila Maidan.

World.title: Over 100 EWS candidates allotted open PG seats in private colleges with fees up to Rs 2 crore
World.content:
NEW DELHI: More than 100 candidates from the economically weaker section (EWS) category have been allotted postgraduate medical seats in the open category under the self-financed quota in private colleges, where tuition fee for some courses can be up to Rs 2.1 crore over three years.

The allotments were made in the first round of NEET-PG 2026 counselling, according to the seat allotment list. The list records the candidates' category as EWS while the allotted seat category was open and the quota was mentioned self-financed merit seat.

Among those allotted seats was a candidate with NEET-PG rank of 79,396, who secured MS obstetrics and gynaecology at Padmashree Dr DY Patil Medical College, Navi Mumbai, where the three-year tuition is around Rs 2 crore. Another candidate, ranked 71,263, was allotted MD radio-diagnosis at Raja Rajeswari Medical College, Bengaluru, where the three-year tuition is around Rs 1.8 crore. Candidates had listed these colleges and courses in their counselling choices and were allotted seats based on their preferences and rank.

They can retain the seat, seek an upgrade or exit.

World.title: Rain fails to dampen spirits as thousands turn up for Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi concert, marking beginning of Aura World Tour
World.content:
The rain-soaked Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi turned into a sea of white turbans, music and cheers on Friday (October 30, 2026) evening as thousands of fans braved hours of rain to catch Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh perform in the capital.

The unseasonal showers, which continued through the day and into the evening, did little to dampen the enthusiasm of concertgoers, who began gathering outside the stadium hours before the show. By evening, the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium Metro station was packed, with queues stretching at its exit as fans made their way to Gate No. 14 of the venue. With no general parking available at the stadium, many opted to travel by Metro. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) had also extended services on all lines (except the Airport Express line) upto midnight for the concertgoers.

The excitement was visible as early as 3 p.m., with fans arriving in groups, some dressed in Dosanjh’s popular white and black kurta-pyjama and turban combination. Several women, too, sported white turbans with their outfits.

Students from universities, including Jamia Millia Islamia and Delhi University, along with residents and visitors from other cities, gathered around the box office. Some were still hoping to get their hands on last-minute tickets.

“We could not get the tickets online, but we really wanted to attend the show. So, we came here in the hope that we might get a last minute ticket or from someone who had an extra one,” a student told The Hindu.

Many fans had travelled from different parts of the country and abroad, with some attending their second or even third Dosanjh concert. The audience was diverse, spanning children, young fans and older couples. Among those Dosanjh invited on stage was a CRPF personnel.

Complaint filed seeking curbs on Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi show

Pooja Bajaj, who had travelled from London, said this was her first time watching the singer perform live. “We have come from London to watch Diljit Dosanjh’s concert. This is the first time I am attending it,” she said excitedly.

Satnam Singh had travelled all the way from Toronto, Canada, specifically for the Delhi show. Having previously attended Dosanjh’s concert in Ludhiana in December, he said he was keen to experience the singer’s performance in the capital as well.

“I had attended the concert in Ludhiana earlier in December. I have come from Toronto, especially for this. I enjoyed Diljit’s concert in Toronto as well,” he said.

For Tarasha Kaur, who arrived with her son and other family members, the evening was an opportunity to finally experience the singer’s performance, after following his concerts through videos.

“My son attended Diljit’s show in Canada and he loved it. Since then, we have wanted to attend too. Now, all of us are together for this show. Earlier, we enjoyed the show through videos and today we are going to do it live,” she said.

“Punjabi pride is so central to Diljit’s personality, and seeing him represent that identity on a global stage makes me immensely proud. He has all the qualities you would expect from an international artiste. He is charming in a very Punjabi way, immensely talented, values his roots and his fans, and is not afraid to make a political statement when needed. That combination is what makes him special,” said Kiran Singh, who had come from Chandigarh to attend Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi concert.

For one teenage fan, the concert was special as it was the first time her parents had relaxed her curfew to let her attend a show.

“My parents know how big a fan I am of Diljit. His posters are everywhere in my room. I have never stepped out after 7 p.m. alone, but today, for this concert, my parents allowed me to go,” she said.

Another fan had travelled from Ludhiana, Dosanjh’s hometown, to watch him perform in the national capital.

Addressing the crowd, Dosanjh referred to the uncertainty surrounding the Delhi leg of his tour and said several attempts had been made to prevent the first show from taking place.

“We wanted to do the first show in Delhi. Many tried to stop this show, but I’m here and the first show has been done. I am in India until December 20 and will do all the other shows also. Try and stop me,” he told the audience.

The Delhi concert marked the opening leg of Dosanjh’s Aura India Tour 2026, with the singer set to perform in several cities across the country. The show had drawn attention in the days leading up to it after the Delhi Police initially withheld permission over “specific threat-related inputs” and security and law-and-order concerns during the festive season, before clearing it following discussions with the organisers.

Fans also praised the arrangements at the venue, particularly the assistance provided by the event staff and the police.

“The management was too good. Everyone attended to us so well, proper guidance was provided to us. Enjoyed a lot, it was awesome,” a fan said.

Another concertgoer, who was attending his third Dosanjh show and second in Delhi, said the experience was even better than his previous visits.

“This was even better than the previous one. The crowd was very good, and the Delhi Police provided a lot of support. I’m also going to Indore and Lucknow to attend the concert,” he said.

The setlist spanned Dosanjh’s early Punjabi hits and his biggest chartbusters. Between performances, he paused for spontaneous interactions with the audience, posed for photographs, encouraged fans to sing along and even handed out return gifts.

As the concert drew to a close, Dosanjh looked up at the clouds and thanked them for making the opening show of his nationwide tour a success.

By around 10 p.m., concertgoers streamed out of the stadium and made their way towards the main road, looking for cabs and auto-rickshaws to get home.

World.title: Heavy polling in second phase panchayat elections for Sarpanch, Ward Panch in Rajasthan
World.content:
A heavy polling took place in the second phase of village panchayat elections for Sarpanch and Ward Panch in 22 districts of Rajasthan on Friday (October 30, 2026). While 45 Sarpanches were earlier elected unopposed, as many as 3,626 village panchayats went to polls and 1.06 crore voters exercised their franchise.

The highest voter turnout was recorded at 84.37% in Jaipur district’s Rampura Dabri. Voters arrived at polling booths in large numbers, enthusiastically, with elderly people and women seen standing in queues to exercise their right to vote.

People turned up to vote despite light rain and drizzle at places such as Kotputli-Behror, situated on the Jaipur-Delhi national highway, and the Malakhera area in Alwar district. Counting of votes started immediately after the polling ended, while the results were expected to be declared by late night.

Residents of Karanpur village in Dausa district’s Mahwa area boycotted polling in protest against the delimitation exercise, while the villagers at Dausa’s Pyara Ka Nagla and Jalore’s Bawatra and Dayalpur did not turn up for voting in protest against the change of their panchayats.

Rajasthan gram panchayat polls: second phase held amid reports of minor clashes, protests

Rival groups of villagers in Kotputli-Behror’s Majra Aheer and Jodhpur’s Sangariya Phata clashed over allegations of bogus voting. Police intervened at both places and brought the situation under control. ()

World.title: On JD(U) 23rd foundation day, party gives credit to Nitish for Bihar’s development
World.content:
Ruling Janata Dal (United) on Friday (October 30, 2026) celebrated its 23rd foundation day of the party and credited the party’s President and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar leadership for the Bihar’s development.

JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha wrote a message on social media account X asserting that with the trust of the people, the dedication of its workers, and the resolve for good governance, the JD(U) has carved out a distinct identity in Bihar’s politics.

“Under the leadership and guidance of our esteemed national president, Nitish Kumar ji, the party has played a pivotal role in advancing Bihar’s development, social justice, good governance, and inclusive growth. On this special occasion, heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all senior leaders, dedicated workers, and supporters of the party,”Mr. Jha wrote.

He added that we should come together to strengthen the resolve for public service and continue working tirelessly for Bihar’s progress and prosperity.

JD(U) State president Umesh Singh Kushwaha also extended greetings on the party’s foundation Day and said that the 23-year glorious journey of the JD(U) under the leadership of Nitish Kumar is dedicated to the values ​​of social justice and good governance.

Speaking to the media, he called Mr. Kumar as the party’s undisputed leader and his son Nishant Kumar who is also the Health Minister of Bihar as future leader of the party. Mr. Kushwaha said that the JD(U) was founded on October 30, 2003, drawing inspiration from the ideals of the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, Dr. Baba Saheb Bhimrao Ambedkar, Loknayak Jayaprakash Narayan and Jannayak Karpoori Thakur.

“Since its inception, the party has remained committed to advancing the principles of social justice, good governance, and social harmony throughout its 23-year journey. When Nitish Kumar took the reins of Bihar in November 2005, he ushered a new era for the state,” Mr. Kushwaha said.

He added that Mr. Kumar introduced a transformative model centred on “development with justice,” good governance, and women’s empowerment that fundamentally altered both the destiny and the image of Bihar.

JD(U) State president pointed out that while the term “Bihari” had become synonymous with contempt and neglect before 2005, Nitish Kumar, through his efforts, restored honour and self-respect to Bihar and its people.

In his congratulatory message, Mr. Kushwaha asked all the party workers and leaders to take a resolve to move the JD(U) to unprecedented heights of success in days to come.

“We shall further strengthen the hands of the party’s future and our popular Health Minister, Nishant ji. We shall reinforce our commitment in taking the socialist principles of our leader, Nitish Kumar, as well as the contributions he has made toward the development of Bihar, to every household and every individual,”Mr. Kushwaha said.

Also, JD(U) has decided to organise a programme titled Sushasan Diwas: Nitish Samvad (Good Governance Day: Dialogue with Nitish) across all districts of the State on November 24, 2026.

Senior leader and minister Leshi Singh, has been appointed as the ‘State Coordinator’ for the execution of this programme.
